post.summary: Add a trusted-JWT connection: your system signs a short-lived JWT for a person and sends them to login_url?token=…&redirect_url=…. Atlas checks the signature against jwks_uri, iss, aud, exp, the max age, and that the jti was never used before, then signs them in and seats them in organization_id. An active connection needs jwks_uri, issuer and audience.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique key per intended write (16 to 128 characters recommended, e.g. a UUID). A retry with the same key and the same request replays the first response for 24 hours with Idempotent-Replay: true; the same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, and while the first is still running a retry is 409 too. A failed write (4xx/5xx) does not consume the key. A dry run never uses it.

organization_id.description: The organization people who sign in this way are seated in.

jwks_uri.description: An https URL serving the signer's JSON Web Key Set (public RS / PS / ES / EdDSA keys; HS keys are ignored). Cached per connection for 10 minutes, or your Cache-Control max-age between 1 minute and 1 hour; a token signed with a key id Atlas has not seen refetches at most once a minute; if the URL is down, cached keys keep working for up to 30 minutes past expiry. Updating the connection refreshes the cache.

issuer.description: The exact `iss` the tokens carry.

audience.description: An `aud` value the tokens must carry.

email_claim.description: The claim carrying the email address (default email). email_verified: true lets the sign-in link to an existing account with that verified email.

max_age_seconds.description: The longest a token may live (exp − iat).

default_role_id.description: The organization role a newly seated member gets (else org:member).

A retry with the same key and the same request replays the first response for 24 hours with Idempotent-Replay: true; the same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, and while the first is still running a retry is 409 too. A failed write (4xx/5xx) does not consume the key. A dry run never uses it.

organization_id.description: The organization people who sign in this way are seated in.

jwks_uri.description: An https URL serving the signer's JSON Web Key Set (public RS / PS / ES / EdDSA keys; HS keys are ignored). Cached per connection for 10 minutes, or your Cache-Control max-age between 1 minute and 1 hour; a token signed with a key id Atlas has not seen refetches at most once a minute; if the URL is down, cached keys keep working for up to 30 minutes past expiry. Updating the connection refreshes the cache.

issuer.description: The exact `iss` the tokens carry.

audience.description: An `aud` value the tokens must carry.

email_claim.description: The claim carrying the email address (default email). email_verified: true lets the sign-in link to an existing account with that verified email.

max_age_seconds.description: The longest a token may live (exp − iat).

default_role_id.description: The organization role a newly seated member gets (else org:member).

login_url.description: Send the person here with ?token=<jwt>&redirect_url=<your app URL>.

post.summary: Schedule a GRACEFUL deletion of a user: opens a cancellation grace window (grace_seconds, default the instance erasure grace of 7 days) and emits user.deletion_scheduled. When the window lapses the worker finalizes the purge (reusing the shared soft-delete → 30-day PII scrub). DELETE /v1/users/:id remains the immediate path. The instance's `pre_user_deletion` Actions are asked first: one may refuse (403 ACTION_BLOCKED with its reason, nothing is scheduled) or pause it (scheduled but held: user.deletion_paused is emitted and the person must re-confirm). The person is emailed (deletion_scheduled, then the reminders in compliance.retention.deletionReminders) through the instance's own email provider.

The user's deletion date, the in-flight erasure request's scheduled date and the reminder plan all move together; the person is mailed the new date and `user.deletion_rescheduled` is emitted. The `pre_user_deletion` Actions are asked again for the new date (a refusal is 403 ACTION_BLOCKED) and a legal hold refuses the move. 409 when the user has no scheduled deletion, the deletion is paused (resume it with POST /v1/users/{id}/deletion/reconfirm first) or the user is already erased. Returns the user.

post.summary: Bulk-create users from an array, deduping by verified email, through the same path sign-up uses. Plaintext passwords are Argon2id-hashed; Argon2id, bcrypt, PBKDF2/scrypt (Django, passlib), Firebase scrypt (with password_hash_config.firebase), Better Auth scrypt and Node crypto.scrypt `scrypt$N$r$p$salt$key` hashes are imported verbatim (a Node string with an all-digit salt is also a valid Django one and must be named: password_hash_algorithm scrypt_node or scrypt_django; scrypt_node takes salt_encoding, default utf8 = the salt text as written). A hash that does not describe itself is imported by naming it: password_hash_algorithm (scrypt, pbkdf2, md5, sha1, sha256, sha512, their _salted forms, hmac_sha256, bcrypt, …) with password_hash_params (scrypt n or log_n / r / p / key_length; pbkdf2 digest / iterations / key_length; md5 and sha* salt_position prefix|suffix; encoding and salt_encoding hex|base64|base64url|utf8) and password_salt; the hash may be the bare digest or `<salt>$<hash>` / `<name>$<salt>$<hash>` (e.g. `scrypt$<salt>$<hash>` with the parameters given separately). Every imported hash is checked with a constant-time compare and upgraded to Argon2id on the first successful sign-in; a format that cannot be checked is rejected per row (unsupported_password_hash, the message names the field). Each row may also carry external_id, image_url (alias profile_image_url: an https URL; an invalid one fails the row with invalid_image_url), created_at, phone_number / phone_numbers and organization_memberships (org by id, external id or slug, plus a role); create_organizations:true creates a missing org. Per-row failures are recorded, never fatal. password_policy "until_email_verified" holds the password of a row without email_verified true until an email on the account is proven by any route; a correct password is refused until then with password_not_yet_usable (a wrong one gets the normal failure). Body: an array of users, or { users, upsert?, notify?, create_organizations?, password_policy?, password_hash_config? }. An import never notifies the imported users: with notify false (the default) no email, SMS or push is sent as a consequence of the import, whatever templates are configured; notify:true is reserved for future welcome messages and currently sends nothing.
post.description: One call can carry, per row, the identities (`external_accounts`: provider and provider_user_id), the password hash (with `password_hash_algorithm` and params) and the old system's id (`external_id`). The per-row report (`results`, one entry per row, in order) gives `index`, `external_id`, `email_address`, `user_id` and `outcome` (created | updated | matched | failed); failures are also listed in `errors`, and non-fatal findings in `warnings`. Add `?dry_run=true` to run the whole batch (up to 5,000 rows) through the real import inside a transaction that is rolled back: the answer carries the same per-row report as `would_return` and nothing is written.

post.summary: Resolve a batch of email addresses to user ids in one call. VERIFIED, LIVE users match by default. For RIGHTS FULFILMENT / DSAR, pass include_unverified:true so an account whose email was never confirmed is still found — otherwise a rights request for such a subject would wrongly complete as "no record". Deleted users are excluded by default (after DELETE /v1/users/:id an address stops resolving here, so a rights orchestrator is not told an erased subject still exists and a uniqueness check does not turn a returning user away); pass include_deleted:true to match them, flagged with `deleted`. Each result carries a `verified` flag, so you can always tell the cases apart: ABSENT from `data` means no such live user; PRESENT with `verified:false` means the account exists but hasn't confirmed that email. (For a DSAR you can skip this lookup entirely by opening the request with subject_email on POST /v1/data_subject_requests, which resolves verified-then-unverified server-side.) Boolean flags also accept "true"/"1"/"yes"/1.

post.summary: Open a request for a subject from a lookup. `type` takes the canonical words or Atlas's aliases; the answer echoes `canonicalType`. A deletion or closure is `scheduled` until `executeAfter` (default: the instance erasure grace) and nothing is erased before it; restriction and rectification wait for an operator. The same `caseId` (or an erasure already in flight for the person) returns the existing request (200) instead of a second one (201). With `privacy:grants:revoke`, an erasure also revokes the Sign in with Atlas grant (step `grant_revoke`); without it the step is `skipped: insufficient_scope`. Send `Idempotency-Key` (16–128 characters); a retry with the same key replays the first answer, a different body is a 409. Answers `X-Version: 2`; send a W3C `traceparent` to correlate (its trace-id is stored on the request and returned as `trace`). Errors carry `{ error, field }` next to `errors`.

get.summary: Everything a privacy integration wires, in one view: the hosted-page consent manager (`cookie_consent`, as GET /v1/instance/cookie_consent answers it), the data-rights orchestrator (`privacy_orchestrator`), the DSR completion webhook to the orchestrator (`dsr_webhook`) and the narrow executor key the connect minted (`executor_key`, never its secret). `connected` is true when all four are in place. Needs `instance:read` and `secret_keys:read`.

post.summary: Wire a consent manager / data-rights orchestrator to the instance both ways in one call. `preset` is an orchestrator preset (`cookiemunch` fills the banner script, CSP origins and case URLs from `site_id`) or `custom` (send `cookie_consent.script_url` and `orchestrator.name` / `case_url` yourself). Sets the hosted-page CMP, the orchestrator Atlas opens cases with (`api_key` or `partner_link_id`), the DSR completion webhook to the orchestrator's executor connection (`completion_webhook_url`, or with preset cookiemunch `executor_connection_id`: Atlas reads that connection's `webhookUrl` from Cookie Munch and `dsr_webhook.secret_destination` says where its signing secret goes), and mints a secret key with `privacy:*` scopes and `cookie_consent:read` only (default `privacy:execute` + `privacy:grants:revoke` + `cookie_consent:read`) for the orchestrator to call the executor protocol with, or uses the one it already holds (`key.id`). `executor_key.action` says which: `minted`, `kept`, `upgraded` (a re-run added requested scopes the key lacked; secret unchanged) or `adopted`. `warnings` says when a new key is minted. Idempotent: a re-run updates the same settings and returns the same key without its secret (`idempotent_replay: true`); rotate it with POST /v1/secret_keys/{id}/rotate. The body is validated in full before anything is written; errors name the nested field (`cookie_consent.script_url`, `key.scopes.0`). Needs `instance:write` and `secret_keys:write` (and recent MFA for an operator token on first mint). → 201 when the orchestrator or the key was created, else 200.

Optional on a re-run when the endpoint exists. With preset cookiemunch, send executor_connection_id instead and Atlas reads it.

post.summary: Register a webhook endpoint: an HTTPS url (any receiver), or an event destination (AWS EventBridge, Google Cloud Pub/Sub, Cloudflare Queues) with your own credentials. Omit enabled_events for "*". `active: false` creates it switched off: nothing is delivered until PATCH { active: true }, and POST /v1/webhook_endpoints/{id}/test still works on it. `secret` sets your own signing secret (whsec_ + at least 32 characters; 422 otherwise); without it Atlas generates one. Idempotent create: `external_ref` returns the existing object on a repeat (200, `idempotent_replay: true`, no secret re-shown); `metadata` tags it (filter lists with ?metadata[key]=value).

post.summary: Rotate the endpoint signing secret. The new secret is revealed exactly once. Send `secret` to rotate to a secret you chose (whsec_ + at least 32 characters, different from the current one; 422 otherwise). By default (`overlap_seconds` 0) the old secret stops signing at once. With `overlap_seconds` (at most 604800 = 7 days) every delivery carries two signatures in `atlas-signature` (`v1,<new> v1,<old>`, the new one first), so a verifier holding either secret passes while you deploy the new one; after that only the new secret signs. Set an overlap only once every receiver verifies with an SDK that accepts several signatures (@atlasauth/backend 0.9.1+, Python/Ruby/PHP/Go 0.7.0+, Java 1.5.0+, .NET 1.6.0+, Rust 0.13.0+, Elixir 0.4.0+) or a verifier that splits the header on spaces: a verifier that splits it on ',' rejects every delivery for the whole overlap, even with the new secret. `previous_secret_expires_at` says when the old secret stops signing (epoch ms), or null when it already has; endpoint reads show it too while the overlap is open.

post.summary: Send a synthetic webhook.test event to this endpoint only (never fanned out), also when the endpoint is switched off (active: false). It is signed exactly like a real delivery, with the endpoint's own signing secret (both secrets during a rotation overlap). Two answers, by status: by default the attempt is made now (waiting up to 10 s; ?wait shortens that) and the answer is 200 OK with the result (object webhook_test_result): delivery_id, event_id, event_type (webhook.test), url (the exact URL tried), status (success | failed), http_status, latency_ms, response_snippet (first 1 KB of the response), error (the delivery-log code), error_kind (non_2xx, redirect, timeout, tls, dns, connection_refused, network, url_blocked; null on success), signature_header_sent and will_retry. A failed attempt is still 200: read status. With ?wait=0 the delivery is queued for the worker instead and the answer is 201 Created (object webhook_delivery: id, event_id, url, status pending). Check for 2xx, not for 200. Both answers carry the shared test-call fields ok, status, http_status and latency_ms (the same four a hook test returns); while queued, ok, http_status and latency_ms are null.

post.summary: Register a Sign in with Atlas app (an OpenID Connect client on https://atlasauth.net) for this platform's account. post.summary: Rotate the app's webhook signing secret. The new `webhook_secret` is returned once and signs every delivery from now on. By default (`overlap_seconds` 0) the previous secret stops signing at once. With `overlap_seconds` (at most 604800 = 7 days) it signs each delivery too, as a second `v1,` entry in `atlas-signature` after the new one, so a verifier holding either secret passes. Set an overlap only once every receiver verifies with an SDK that accepts several signatures (@atlasauth/backend 0.9.1+, Python/Ruby/PHP/Go 0.7.0+, Java 1.5.0+, .NET 1.6.0+, Rust 0.13.0+, Elixir 0.4.0+) or a verifier that splits the header on spaces: a verifier that splits it on ',' rejects every delivery for the whole overlap, even with the new secret. `webhook_previous_secret_expires_at` says when it stops (epoch ms), or null. 409 when the app has no webhook.

post.summary: Start a support impersonation: a session for `user_id` whose token carries `act.sub` = `staff_user_id`. The instance policy (GET /v1/instance/impersonation_policy) decides the rules: `reason` (max 500 characters) is required unless the policy turns that off, `reason_code` must be one of the policy's codes when it lists any, the session lasts at most the policy's limit (`max_duration_seconds` can only shorten it; never more than 1 hour), and `read_only` (default from the policy) makes the session refuse every change on the Frontend API and puts `ro: true` in its token. When the policy requires approval the call answers 202 with a pending `impersonation_request`; a second staff member decides it with POST /v1/impersonations/requests/{id}/approve or /deny. Optional `require_staff_org_id` and `require_staff_mfa` apply to the staff user (and to the approver). Refused for banned, deleted and impersonation-protected users. Emits `impersonation.started` (and the older `session.impersonation_started`); the user is emailed when the policy says so and sees the session at GET /v1/client/me/staff_access. To export the trail, use GET /v1/audit_logs?action=session.impersonation_started&format=jsonl.

put.summary: Replace the scope catalogue. Each scope has a `name`, a `label` and a `description` per locale ({ "en": "…", "es": "…" }), `sensitive`, and `requires_verified_client`. The consent screen shows the label and description in the user's language (falling back to its base language, then `en`). A scope with `requires_verified_client` is refused at /oauth2/authorize with `invalid_scope` unless the app's status is `approved` or that scope is in the client's `approved_scopes` (per-scope review). The owner and testers of a client still in development may request it too. A client still needs the scope in its allowed scopes to request it. `requires_client_level` (`any`, `verified` or `certified`) sets the level a client needs (`requires_verified_client: true` means `verified`; the stricter wins); a `certified` client is an approved one the instance has certified (PATCH /v1/oauth_clients/{id} `certified`). `owner_exempt: true` lets the developer who owns a client request the scope with it on their own account whatever the client's level. A name ending `:*` (`listings:*`) is a wildcard entry: it covers every `listings:<anything>` for gating, consent text and released claims, and a client or grant that holds `listings:*` holds each of them. By default the whole list is checked and nothing is written if any entry is bad (422, one problem per field). `?mode=partial` applies the valid entries and answers 200 with `rejected: [{ index, name, errors }]` (a rejected entry leaves the scope of that name as it was). `?too_long=truncate` cuts over-long labels and descriptions instead of refusing them and lists each cut in `warnings`.

Never returns the private signing key. auth_config includes sections owned by other routes (branding, design, hosted_pages and so on); they are read-only through PATCH /v1/instance unless sent back unchanged.

field.description: unknown_field: the full path, e.g. auth_config.strategies.atlasId.

inactive_methods.description: Sign-in methods that are switched on but not offered to users (not on the hosted pages, the embedded components or the Frontend API environment), because they need an email provider and the instance has none. Email is bring-your-own. They become active on their own once a provider is configured. Password is listed only when sign-up must verify the address by email and no user holds a password yet.

limited_methods.description: Sign-in methods that still work without an email provider, minus the parts that need email: password sign-in for users who already hold a password, without password reset (and without password sign-up while sign-up must verify the address by email).

signup_usable.description: GET only. Whether a new user can create an account right now. False when no first-factor sign-up method is active (email methods without an email provider, no social provider, no SSO connection, no Sign in with Atlas); preflight reports the same as no_usable_signup_method.

signup_unusable_reason.description: GET only. When signup_usable is false: why, and the fix (turn on Sign in with Atlas first). Null otherwise.

patch.summary: Update allowed origins and auth_config (a partial, validated, merged patch — not a replace). Open or public-suffix wildcard origins refused (a single-label https://*.your-domain.com is accepted; shared hosts like *.vercel.app on development instances only); an invalid auth_config returns 422. A method that needs email (email code, email link, password sign-up that verifies by email) is accepted even when the instance has no email provider yet (email is bring-your-own; Terraform or config import may add the provider later in the same apply): the response lists it under inactive_methods, users are not offered it, and it becomes active on its own once a provider is configured (PUT /v1/messaging_providers/email). Captcha always runs on your own provider keys: turning a captcha ON for a flow (or changing its provider) before both the provider site key (auth_config.captcha.siteKey) and its secret (PUT /v1/instance/captcha_secret) are set returns 422 CAPTCHA_KEYS_REQUIRED with param naming the missing one — store the secret first, then enable. Removing the site key while a flow uses it returns 409 CAPTCHA_IN_USE unless force=true, which also turns the captcha off on those flows. Setting the retired raw branding fields (branding.customCss / customHtmlHeader / customHtmlFooter) returns 422 naming the field — use the design settings (PUT /v1/instance/design) instead; clearing them (null or "") is accepted. The response echoes auth_config_resolved so you can confirm the change took effect, and `warnings`: an origin_still_referenced entry for every removed origin that webhook endpoints (not marked external) or OAuth client URIs still point at, naming each one and the POST /v1/instance/move_origin call that moves them. Strict writes: auth_config.strictRequestBodies (true on instances created from 2026-10 on) refuses unknown body fields with 422 UNKNOWN_FIELD on every Backend API write; set it to opt in or out, or send Atlas-Strict: true | false on one request. Every auth_config key is checked at every depth against the auth_config schema: strict, an unknown or moved key is 422 UNKNOWN_FIELD with param naming its full path (auth_config.strategies.atlasId), meta.did_you_mean when a real key is close, and meta.hint naming the endpoint for a setting that has its own (auth_config.branding → PATCH /v1/branding, design → PUT /v1/instance/design, hostedPages → PATCH /v1/instance/hosted_pages, …); lenient, the key is dropped (never stored) and listed in warnings as unknown_field and in the Atlas-Unknown-Fields header. A null on any key and an unchanged echo of a stored section (the raw auth_config GET returns, sent back as is) are always accepted.

Only holders can register clients at POST /oauth2/register (Authorization: Bearer <token>) once oauthProvider.requireInitialAccessToken is on. The token is returned exactly once and stored hashed; optional expiry and use limit. Audited as oauth_initial_access_token.created.

parameters.description: A unique key per intended write (16 to 128 characters recommended, e.g. a UUID). A retry with the same key and the same request replays the first response for 24 hours with Idempotent-Replay: true; the same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, and while the first is still running a retry is 409 too. A failed write (4xx/5xx) does not consume the key. A dry run never uses it.

post.summary: Establish a session for a user in one call — returns jwt + refresh_token, audited as a first-party sign-in (not impersonation unless actor.sub is set). Pass set_cookies:true (+ optional cookie_domain) to also get the ready-to-set Set-Cookie strings, so a backend can relay one response to establish a real browser session for a known reader. Bypasses the sign-in gate. With mode "browser_ticket" no session is minted here: the response is a one-time ticket (60 s by default, single use, this instance only) that a browser redeems with POST /v1/client/sign_ins {strategy:"ticket"}, plus, when you pass redirect_url (an allowed origin), a ready `url` that signs the browser in and lands on redirect_url. This is the successor of the deprecated POST /v1/sign_in_tokens for support handoffs and end-to-end tests; audited as sign_in_ticket.created.

get.summary: Fetch a single session. Another instance session id is 404, never 403.

The session's advisory risk: `{ score (0-100), level (low|medium|high), reasons[], computed_at }`. Reasons come from signals Atlas already holds: `new_device`, `new_country`, `impossible_travel` (against the user's previous session), `bot_likely` and `breached_password` (at sign-in). The same object is on the session (`risk`) and, when `session.includeRiskClaim` is on, in the session token as the `risk` claim; `risk.elevated` is sent when a session turns high. Advisory only: Atlas never allows or denies anything because of it. Fields are null and `reasons` empty when the session was never assessed, which means unknown, not safe.

Cheap session-freshness check for a relying party: `{ id, status, user_id, expires_at, last_active_at? }`, where status is active, expired, revoked or ended. `:id` is the session id or the `sid` claim of an ID token (a device or CIBA sign-in answers from its grant, without last_active_at). Sent with `Cache-Control: private, max-age=5` and an ETag; `If-None-Match` answers 304. Another instance session is 404, never 403. A banned user session is revoked at once and the back-channel logout is sent in the same request.

last_active_at.description: Epoch ms; absent for a device or CIBA sign-in.

post.summary: Keep a session alive from your backend: slides its inactivity (idle) window as if the user had just loaded a page. Use it when your app mounts the Atlas SDK only on some pages, so time spent on pages without it does not count as inactivity. Never extends past the session's absolute expiry and never revives an ended session — a revoked session is 409 SESSION_REVOKED, a session that already timed out is 409 SESSION_IDLE_EXPIRED, and one past its absolute expiry is 409 SESSION_EXPIRED; an unknown id is 404. At most one effective write per minute per session: a touch within 60 seconds of the session's last activity returns the current state with extended:false, so calling it on every request is safe. No request body. Returns the session with last_active_at and idle_expires_at.

post.summary: Mint an end-user API key for a user, organization or machine (returns the ak_ secret once; `metadata` is your own vocabulary on the key, the same object as `claims`, returned on verify; `dies_with: "sign_out_everywhere"` on a user key revokes it when that user signs out everywhere), OR import an existing key by its SHA-256 hash (hash_algorithm "sha256" or "sha256_hex"), or by its bcrypt or Argon2id hash string (hash_algorithm "bcrypt" or "argon2id": verified on first use by the imported prefix, then re-hashed to SHA-256), so it verifies against the original secret. Normally authenticated with an sk_ key; a LAN/offline MACHINE may instead self-provision a key for ITSELF by presenting Authorization: Bearer <machine JWT> (token_use:m2m from /v1/machines/token) + x-publishable-key — the subject is forced to that machine and it cannot grant itself management-plane scopes. Send credential: "key_pair" to mint a key with NO shared secret (like an Apple .p8): Atlas generates a P-256 pair and returns the private key once as private_key (a PKCS#8 PEM; never stored, logged, sent in a webhook, or replayed by an Idempotency-Key retry), or, when you send public_key (SPKI PEM, P-256 or Ed25519), keeps only yours and returns no private key. The holder signs short-lived JWT assertions (alg ES256 or EdDSA, kid = the key id, iss = the key id, aud = audience, iat, exp, optional nbf, jti, scope) that you verify with POST /v1/api_keys/verify {token} or exchange at POST /v1/api_keys/token. audience (1-256 characters, key_pair only) defaults to the instance id. secret is null on a key_pair key, and it is never accepted as an ak_ bearer. Pass public_key (an SPKI PEM) to make the key proof-of-possession: tokens minted from it carry cnf.jkt and a resource verifies a holder-signed proof OFFLINE. Pass limits (an array of { unit, amount, period } with period request|second|minute|day|month|total) to set per-key spend caps and rate limits, metered with POST /v1/api_keys/{id}/usage. Key controls: enabled (false = minted disabled), rate_limit { max, window_seconds } (per-key verify throttle), remaining (a use budget each successful verify spends), prefix (a custom secret prefix such as acme, giving acme_<id>_<secret>), type (a key type such as sk, giving ak_sk_<id>_<secret>; required and checked against endUserApiKeys.keyTypes when the instance sets that list, 400 otherwise; also accepted on import), and expires_in_seconds as an alternative to expires_at, and allowed_ips (up to 100 IPv4/IPv6 addresses or CIDR ranges; verify then needs the end caller's client_ip and refuses callers outside the list). The instance expiry policy (endUserApiKeys.defaultExpiresInSeconds / maxExpiresInSeconds) gives a key sent without an expiry the default lifetime and refuses one longer than the ceiling (400). Emits api_key.created (on mint, import and machine self-provisioning). An import is idempotent: it honours Idempotency-Key (a retry replays the first answer), and re-sending the same hash for the same subject, prefix and type answers 200 with the stored key and `outcome: "already_present"` (nothing is written, no event fires); a first import answers 201 with `outcome: "created"`. A hash that already exists with a different subject, prefix or type is refused with 409 CONFLICT and nothing is changed.

post.summary: Verify a presented end-user API key secret, or a key-pair assertion. Send token (a JWT signed with the private key of a key_pair key) instead of secret (sending both is a 400; sending neither answers valid: false, as before). An assertion must carry alg ES256 (raw 64-byte r||s) or EdDSA matching the stored key, kid and iss equal to the key id, aud the key's audience, iat (at most 60 s ahead) and exp (lifetime at most the key's max_token_lifetime_seconds, default 3600, hard cap 86400); a jti is single-use until exp; an optional scope (space-separated) must be a subset of the key's scopes and narrows the result. A success adds credential: "key_pair", audience, jti and exp (epoch seconds) to the verification. Refusals: valid:false with code invalid_assertion (nothing proving the holder signed it, no id), then, only for a genuine signature, assertion_expired, assertion_not_yet_valid, wrong_audience, assertion_lifetime_too_long, assertion_replayed, scope_not_granted. Any secret works: a natively minted ak_ key AND an imported key of any format or prefix (resolved by its SHA-256). Returns the subject, name, claims, scopes, constraints, spend caps (limits) and their current-window usage, or valid:false alone (unknown, revoked, expired, disabled or subject deleted; never says which). Send required_scopes to require scopes the key must carry. A live key refused by its own policy answers valid:false with a code: insufficient_scope (missing_scopes), rate_limited (retry_after_ms, from the key rate_limit) usage_exhausted (no remaining uses left), ip_not_allowed (client_ip is outside the key's allowed_ips) or client_ip_required (the key has allowed_ips and no client_ip was sent; fails closed). Send client_ip, the END caller's address, because this call is server-to-server. Each successful verify spends one remaining use, atomically. Rate-limited.

post.summary: Meter usage against a key's spend caps, atomically. Body: amount (positive integer), unit (app-defined, e.g. requests or usd_cents), optional idempotency_key. When the debit fits every cap for that unit it is recorded (day, month and total counters, plus second/minute counters for a unit capped on those windows) and allowed:true is returned; when it would exceed a cap — or is larger than a per-request cap — NOTHING is recorded and the response is 200 with allowed:false and code LIMIT_EXCEEDED, so you enforce it in your own transaction. Concurrent debits on one key serialize: two can never both pass a cap only one fits under. Second and minute windows are fixed windows aligned to the UTC clock (a 600/minute cap refuses the 601st request until the next whole minute); day and month windows are UTC calendar windows. The same idempotency_key (kept 24 hours) returns the first outcome without counting again (idempotent_replay:true); reusing it with a different unit or amount is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. A revoked or expired key is 409 CONFLICT; an unknown id 404. The first time a cap fills or refuses a debit in a window, api_key.limit_reached is emitted (once per cap per window).

post.summary: Rotate an end-user API key with an overlap: mint its successor and keep the old key working until the overlap ends.
post.description: The successor has the same subject, name, claims, scopes, constraints, limits, rate limit, remaining uses, allowed networks, organization binding and proof-of-possession key as the old key, a fresh secret (returned once, in `secret`) and, unless you send `expires_at` / `expires_in_seconds`, the same lifetime the old key was given (held to the instance expiry policy). Spend-cap counters start from zero on the successor. The old key stops working at `overlap_seconds` from now (default 86400, at most 604800); `overlap_seconds: 0` revokes it at once with reason `rotated`. Tokens minted from the old key never outlive it. A key_pair key rotates the same way, with a new key id: Atlas generates a new pair (private_key returned once, never replayed) or keeps the `public_key` you send; `secret` and `prefix` do not apply to it. A key can be rotated once: rotate the successor next. Revoked or expired keys, and keys whose owner is gone, are 409. Emits `api_key.created` (the successor), `api_key.updated` (the old key, new expiry) or `api_key.revoked` (no overlap) and `api_key.rotated`. A revocation-feed consumer sees the old key only if it was revoked at once; an overlapping old key simply expires. Send `secret` and `prefix` to choose the successor's secret yourself (the secret must start with the prefix; one Atlas already holds is 409). With no body fields an imported key keeps its format: its stored prefix plus a fresh random tail; when that prefix cannot be regenerated from, the call is refused with 422 and you send `secret` and `prefix`. Honours Idempotency-Key.

post.summary: Mint a short-lived, JWKS-signed access JWT (token_use:api_key, jti) whose exp is clamped to the smallest of the request, the key expiry and the org ceiling; scopes + constraints are embedded so a resource verifies it OFFLINE against the instance JWKS. When the key registered a public_key, the token also carries cnf.jkt (proof-of-possession) and a resource additionally checks a holder-signed proof. Authenticate with (1) an sk_ bearer + the ak_ in the body, (2) an Authorization: Bearer ak_… that self-mints for itself, or (3) no bearer + x-publishable-key naming the instance with the ak_ in the body. A key_pair key's signed assertion is accepted in the same places: Authorization: Bearer <assertion> (self-mint), or an sk_ bearer or publishable key with the assertion in the body field assertion. The token's lifetime never exceeds the assertion's exp, and a token minted from a key_pair key carries no cnf. A key only ever mints within its own instance. The api_keys:read scope applies ONLY to the sk_ path; the ak_ and publishable-key paths are self-scoped.

If the instance was using Atlas's shared development credentials for this provider (a dashboard option on development instances), saving your own replaces them. Does NOT enable the provider — use POST /v1/oauth_providers/{provider}/enabled for that. Accepts display-only fields with no credentials: display_name, icon_url, and mode ('native'|'redirect', to force a native provider like Google through the redirect flow; "" clears the override) — sent together with credentials, they are applied in the same call. Providers with no client credentials (steam, siwe, siws, siwb, siwf) accept display fields and, for the wallets, their verifier `settings` (siwe: domain, chain_ids, rpc_url; siws: domain, networks; siwf: domain, chain_ids, optimism_rpc_url, id_registry_address) — validated (hostnames, positive-integer chain ids, https RPC URLs) and returned as `setting_values`; a credential field (client_id, client_secret, scopes, values, custom_redirect_uri, native) is a 400 naming it. Turning a wallet sign-in on is the auth_config strategy toggle (PATCH /v1/instance strategies.siwe / siws / siwf).

post.summary: Managed email: Atlas sets up your sending domain (the domain of `from_address`) on YOUR OWN Resend or Brevo account, with your API key, and sends through it once the domain is verified. Pass `transport` ("resend" | "brevo") with `config.api_key`, or `provider_id` of your configured Resend or Brevo email provider; without either the call is refused with 422 (param `config.api_key`). The key is stored, write-only, as the instance's email provider in `managed_domain` mode. Returns 201 with the DNS `records` to publish (DKIM, SPF / return-path for Resend; ownership, DKIM, DMARC for Brevo). Until the domain is verified email delivery stays unavailable and preflight warns `managed_email_unverified`. Pass `dns: {provider: "cloudflare", api_token}` and Atlas writes the records itself (DNS-only; the token is write-only) IN THE BACKGROUND: the call answers 202 at once with the records and `dns.status: "pending"`, then Atlas writes them and checks with your provider until the domain is verified (`dns.status` pending → verifying → verified; `dns.last_error` and `failed` when it cannot). No further call is needed; GET shows progress and POST …/verify checks at once. Atlas also registers a bounce / complaint webhook on your Resend or Brevo account, for this instance only (`feedback_webhook`, `feedback_webhook_id`); the counts appear in `usage`. No Atlas sending limits apply (`limits: null`): the account and its limits are yours. Atlas never uses an email account of its own. 409 when the domain is set up on another Atlas instance; 502 MANAGED_EMAIL_PROVIDER_ERROR when your provider refuses.

get.description: Branding is its own resource: it is read and written here, not as an auth_config section of PATCH /v1/instance (which accepts only branding.audiences). The response is { object: "branding", ...fields, resolved }. Main fields: applicationName (page title, headline, email copy), logoUrl, colorPrimary / colorBackground / colorText (emails, and the hosted look before a design is saved), supportEmail (email footer), theme (light | dark | auto), layout (centered | split | wall), fontFamily / fontUrl, legal { termsUrl, privacyUrl, required } (the Terms / Privacy line on the hosted pages; discovery publishes them as op_tos_uri and op_policy_uri), copy, providers, socialButtons, signUpFields, audiences. resolved holds every field with the value in force (defaults filled in).

Top-level fields replace; socialButtons merges one level deeper: its per-provider maps (labels, displayNames, icons, modes, styles) merge per provider key, and a null value deletes that key. URLs: legal.termsUrl and legal.privacyUrl must be https:// on every instance, development included (a localhost policy page is refused with 422 VALIDATION_FAILED, param branding.legal.privacyUrl); logoUrl is https or a raster data: URI. The same fields cannot be sent as auth_config.branding on PATCH /v1/instance (strict writes refuse them with 422 UNKNOWN_FIELD and meta.hint naming this endpoint).

Re-sending a row only refreshes it, so a retry is safe. `dry_run: true` validates and counts without writing.

post.summary: Issue a dead-man liveness beacon. PRINCIPAL path (no Authorization header): submit `beacon`, a v2 beacon signed with the grant principal's own key (scope = a grant_ref they issued, or '*'): the principal halts their agents just by withholding, without trusting the operator. OPERATOR path (`sk_` + `pca:write`): the server signs with the guardian key (`scope`, `validity_ms`). `seq` must strictly increase per (scope, issuer) (409 on replay); validity is hard-capped at one hour. A pure-PQ or hybrid principal beacon is accepted only under the PQ key pinned for the issuer (POST /v1/pca/pq-pins), and only after the issuer check is it charged to the per-source pqVerifyUnitsPerSourcePerMin budget (429 when exhausted) and verified, Ed25519 half first. Beacons gate adjudication only when `auth_config.pca.beacons` is enabled.

get.summary: The OAuth tokens revoked for this API, oldest first, for a resource server that polls this list instead of asking Atlas per request (`createAccessTokenVerifier({ revocation: true })`). Each item is a refresh-token family that ended (`family_id`, the `fid` claim of every access token minted from it: a refresh token was reused, the client called /oauth2/revoke, or an admin, the user or a logout ended the grant) or one access token revoked on its own (`jti`). Reject a token whose `fid` or `jti` is listed. Rows are kept for 48 hours (`retention_seconds`), longer than any access token can live. Page with `after` (the `next_cursor` of the previous page); `server_time` is when the answer was computed: poll again with `since` a little before it. The `oauth_tokens.revoked` webhook carries the same facts for a push.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Epoch milliseconds. Defaults to the retention window; older values are raised to it (see `window_start`).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1 to 5000. Default 1000.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page.

parameters.name: starting_after
parameters.description: Cursor: return only items after this one. Pass the previous page's `next_cursor` (the last item's id). An unknown cursor is a 400.

family_id.description: The refresh-token family (the `fid` claim). Null for a single access token.

jti.description: The `jti` of a single revoked access token. Null for a family.

reason.description: refresh_token_reuse, client_revoked, admin_revoked, user_revoked, grant_revoked or logout.

revoked_at.description: Epoch ms.

server_time.description: Epoch ms when the answer was computed.

window_start.description: Epoch ms the list actually starts from.

retention_seconds.description: How long a row is kept.

post.summary: Create an enterprise SSO connection. The IdP client secret is write-only.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique key per intended write (16 to 128 characters recommended, e.g. a UUID). A retry with the same key and the same request replays the first response for 24 hours with Idempotent-Replay: true; the same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, and while the first is still running a retry is 409 too. A failed write (4xx/5xx) does not consume the key. A dry run never uses it.

organization_id.description: Bind to one organization; null = instance-wide.

type.description: Connection protocol.

saml_single_logout.description: SAML Single Logout: advertise our SingleLogoutService, accept IdP-initiated LogoutRequests, and send the IdP a LogoutRequest on sign-out (when its SLO endpoint is known).

saml_idp_slo_url.description: The IdP SingleLogoutService Location (https). Filled by IdP metadata import.

saml_idp_slo_response_url.description: The IdP SingleLogoutService ResponseLocation, when it differs from the Location.

saml_idp_slo_binding.description: How logout messages are sent to the IdP: `redirect` (default) or `post`; null resets to redirect.

saml_idp_slo_soap_url.description: The IdP SOAP-binding SingleLogoutService (https). When set, a session ended server-side (admin or API revoke, ban, deletion, password reset) is logged out at the IdP over this back channel.

saml_artifact_resolution_url.description: The identity provider ArtifactResolutionService (https). When set, the SAML HTTP-Artifact binding is accepted: the sign-in arrives as a short artifact and Atlas redeems it with a signed ArtifactResolve over a direct server-to-server call.

saml_artifact_mtls.description: Also present the instance SAML signing certificate as a TLS client certificate on the artifact call. Needs a locally held signing key.

saml_require_encrypted_assertions.description: Refuse assertions not encrypted to this connection's encryption key (generate one first).

saml_honor_idp_session_lifetime.description: End a session no later than the SessionNotOnOrAfter the identity provider states in its assertion. Off by default.

require_consent_screen.description: After the identity provider vouches for the person, show who they are about to sign in as and through which provider, and let them continue or cancel before the sign-in completes. Applies to every connection type; each choice is audited.

github_access.description: GitHub as this oidc connection's identity provider (register a GitHub OAuth app; its client id / secret are oidc_client_id / oidc_client_secret; oidc_issuer may be left out). Only people who are active members of one of `allowed_organizations` or `allowed_teams` ("org/team-slug") and have a verified primary email can sign in; anyone else is sent back with __atlas_error=github_team_required. Scopes requested: read:user user:email read:org. null removes it.

saml_acs_path.description: SAML migration: keep the ACS path your IdP app already posts to (e.g. /saml/acs/acme) on your own frontend API domain. Needs a custom frontend API domain; unique per instance; cannot sit under /v1, /oauth2, /hosted, /.well-known or /scim. The SP metadata then advertises it. null = the standard /v1/sso/saml/acs.

allowed_domains.description: Email domains routed to this connection. For an organization-owned connection each must be a verified domain of that organization (400 otherwise).

email.description: The claim (OIDC) or attribute (SAML) holding the email address.

email_verified.description: The claim/attribute asserting the email is verified. A remapped email is treated as unverified unless this is set and true.

attribute_mapping.description: Which IdP claim or attribute carries each profile field (dot paths reach nested OIDC claims). Applies to OIDC and SAML connections. null clears it.

oidc_scopes.description: OIDC only: extra scopes requested from the IdP on top of openid email profile (e.g. groups, offline_access). null clears them.

rerole_on_sign_in.description: Opt-in (default off): on every later sign-in, also move the role of an existing member who has no recorded role source (joined by invitation, or before sources were recorded) when their claims now map to a different role. A role set through the API or dashboard, and another source's members, are never touched. null turns it off.

claim_role_mappings.description: Map an IdP claim value to an org role (first match wins). Sets the role a member is seated with, and on later sign-ins moves the role of a member this connection seated when their claims map elsewhere. Claims that map to nothing leave the role unchanged; a role set through the API or dashboard, and the organization's creator, are never changed.

provisioning_mode.description: For an org-bound connection: `member` (default) seats the JIT user as an org member; `end_user` seats them into the org's reader pool instead (no role).

update_on_sign_in.description: false (default): mapped values are applied when the account is created (and fill empty fields later). true: names, image and metadata are re-applied on every sign-in.

token_endpoint_auth_method.description: How Atlas authenticates to the upstream token endpoint. private_key_jwt signs a client assertion with an Atlas-held key published at client_jwks_uri.

oidc_max_age_seconds.description: Ask the identity provider for a sign-in no older than this many seconds (`max_age`), and refuse an id_token whose `auth_time` is older. 0 forces a fresh login. null: not set.

logout.description: Upstream logout. OpenID Connect providers only.

rp_initiated.description: On Atlas sign-out, hand back the upstream end-session URL (id_token_hint, post_logout_redirect_uri, state) to send the browser to.

post_logout_redirect_url.description: Where the user lands after the upstream logout when the app names no return URL.

backchannel.description: Accept OIDC Back-Channel Logout tokens at backchannel_logout_uri and end the matching Atlas sessions.

frontchannel.description: Accept OIDC Front-Channel Logout: the provider loads frontchannel_logout_uri in an iframe and the matching Atlas sessions end.

frontchannel_session_required.description: Front-channel: require iss + sid (default true). false also ends the framing browser's own session from this provider when they are absent.

end_session_endpoint.description: An explicit end-session endpoint; default: the discovery document's.

idp_initiated_login.description: OIDC third-party initiated login at initiate_login_uri. OpenID Connect providers only.

allowed_targets.description: Where a login may land: exact URLs, or bare origins (any path). Required when enabled.

default_target.description: The landing page when the request names no target_link_uri; must be an allowed target.

client_jwks_uri.description: Register as the client JWKS URL (private_key_jwt).

backchannel_logout_uri.description: Register as the back-channel logout URI.

frontchannel_logout_uri.description: Register as the front-channel logout URI.

post_logout_redirect_uri.description: Register as a post-logout redirect URI.

initiate_login_uri.description: Register as the initiate-login URI (third-party initiated login).

upstream_urls.description: OIDC connections: the URLs to register at the IdP.

domain_warnings.description: Routing domains of an organization-owned connection that are not verified domains of the organization (saved before verification was required). Verify them or remove them.

patch.summary: Update an SSO connection. A secret is only re-encrypted when a new one is supplied.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique key per intended write (16 to 128 characters recommended, e.g. a UUID). A retry with the same key and the same request replays the first response for 24 hours with Idempotent-Replay: true; the same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, and while the first is still running a retry is 409 too. A failed write (4xx/5xx) does not consume the key. A dry run never uses it.

organization_id.description: Bind to one organization; null = instance-wide.

type.description: Connection protocol.

saml_single_logout.description: SAML Single Logout: advertise our SingleLogoutService, accept IdP-initiated LogoutRequests, and send the IdP a LogoutRequest on sign-out (when its SLO endpoint is known).

saml_idp_slo_url.description: The IdP SingleLogoutService Location (https). Filled by IdP metadata import.

saml_idp_slo_response_url.description: The IdP SingleLogoutService ResponseLocation, when it differs from the Location.

saml_idp_slo_binding.description: How logout messages are sent to the IdP: `redirect` (default) or `post`; null resets to redirect.

saml_idp_slo_soap_url.description: The IdP SOAP-binding SingleLogoutService (https). When set, a session ended server-side (admin or API revoke, ban, deletion, password reset) is logged out at the IdP over this back channel.

saml_artifact_resolution_url.description: The identity provider ArtifactResolutionService (https). When set, the SAML HTTP-Artifact binding is accepted: the sign-in arrives as a short artifact and Atlas redeems it with a signed ArtifactResolve over a direct server-to-server call.

saml_artifact_mtls.description: Also present the instance SAML signing certificate as a TLS client certificate on the artifact call. Needs a locally held signing key.

saml_require_encrypted_assertions.description: Refuse assertions not encrypted to this connection's encryption key (generate one first).

saml_honor_idp_session_lifetime.description: End a session no later than the SessionNotOnOrAfter the identity provider states in its assertion. Off by default.

require_consent_screen.description: After the identity provider vouches for the person, show who they are about to sign in as and through which provider, and let them continue or cancel before the sign-in completes. Applies to every connection type; each choice is audited.

github_access.description: GitHub as this oidc connection's identity provider (register a GitHub OAuth app; its client id / secret are oidc_client_id / oidc_client_secret; oidc_issuer may be left out). Only people who are active members of one of `allowed_organizations` or `allowed_teams` ("org/team-slug") and have a verified primary email can sign in; anyone else is sent back with __atlas_error=github_team_required. Scopes requested: read:user user:email read:org. null removes it.

saml_acs_path.description: SAML migration: keep the ACS path your IdP app already posts to (e.g. /saml/acs/acme) on your own frontend API domain. Needs a custom frontend API domain; unique per instance; cannot sit under /v1, /oauth2, /hosted, /.well-known or /scim. The SP metadata then advertises it. null = the standard /v1/sso/saml/acs.

allowed_domains.description: Email domains routed to this connection. For an organization-owned connection each must be a verified domain of that organization (400 otherwise).

email.description: The claim (OIDC) or attribute (SAML) holding the email address.

email_verified.description: The claim/attribute asserting the email is verified. A remapped email is treated as unverified unless this is set and true.

attribute_mapping.description: Which IdP claim or attribute carries each profile field (dot paths reach nested OIDC claims). Applies to OIDC and SAML connections. null clears it.

oidc_scopes.description: OIDC only: extra scopes requested from the IdP on top of openid email profile (e.g. groups, offline_access). null clears them.

rerole_on_sign_in.description: Opt-in (default off): on every later sign-in, also move the role of an existing member who has no recorded role source (joined by invitation, or before sources were recorded) when their claims now map to a different role. A role set through the API or dashboard, and another source's members, are never touched. null turns it off.

claim_role_mappings.description: Map an IdP claim value to an org role (first match wins). Sets the role a member is seated with, and on later sign-ins moves the role of a member this connection seated when their claims map elsewhere. Claims that map to nothing leave the role unchanged; a role set through the API or dashboard, and the organization's creator, are never changed.

provisioning_mode.description: For an org-bound connection: `member` (default) seats the JIT user as an org member; `end_user` seats them into the org's reader pool instead (no role).

Only members SCIM manages follow (seated by SCIM; not a role set through the API or dashboard, and never the organization's creator). A member whose roles or groups map to nothing keeps their role (org:member when first seated).

ip_allow_list.description: The source addresses the token is limited to; empty = any address.

profile_lock.description: While true, the user attributes this directory owns (first_name, last_name, external_id) cannot be edited anywhere but the identity provider: a self-service profile edit, or a Backend API PATCH without the Atlas-Scim-Lock-Override: true header, is refused with 409 (reason scim_profile_locked). Off by default.

rotated_from.description: On rotate: the token this one replaces and when it stops working (epoch ms).

token.description: The bearer token + SCIM base URL — returned ONCE, on create only. Store it now.

warnings.description: On create: non-blocking notes. `no_sso_connection` = the organization has no SSO connection yet, so provisioned users cannot sign in through the IdP until one exists.

422.description: Unprocessable. Includes UNKNOWN_FIELD when the request sends `Atlas-Strict: true` (or the instance enables strict request bodies) and the body has a field this endpoint does not accept.

post.summary: Rotate a live SCIM token: mint its replacement (same organization, connection, scopes, role mappings, IP allow-list and profile lock) and retire the old one after grace_period_seconds (default one day; 0 revokes it now), so the identity provider can be switched over without a gap in provisioning. The new secret is revealed once. Only a live token can be rotated (409 otherwise). An operator token needs a recent MFA. Accepts Idempotency-Key.

parameters.description: A unique key per intended write (16 to 128 characters recommended, e.g. a UUID). grace_period_seconds.description: How long the previous token keeps working so the identity provider can be switched over (default 86400). 0 revokes it immediately.

prefix.description: Recognisable prefix; never the whole token.

scopes.description: ["read"] makes a read-only token (list and fetch; every write is refused with 403). Omitted or null = read and write.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Only clients owned by this developer (an Atlas user or organization id).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1-500. Without limit (and without starting_after) the whole list is returned.

parameters.name: starting_after
parameters.description: Cursor: return only items after this one. Pass the previous page's `next_cursor` (the last item's id). An unknown cursor is a 400.

allowed_sign_in_methods.description: The sign-in methods a session must have used for this app: password, email_code, email_link, passkey, phone_code, siwe, siws, siwb, siwf, a provider such as oauth_google, or the families oauth (any social provider) and enterprise_sso (any enterprise connection). The hosted pages offer only these when the sign-in is for this app; a session made another way signs in again at /oauth2/authorize.

primary_color.description: A hex, rgb() or named CSS colour.

branding.description: The heading, sub-heading, logo and primary colour of the hosted sign-in and sign-up pages when the sign-in is for this app.

claims_allowlist.description: The user claims this app receives in its ID token and from userinfo (for example email, name, org_id). Protocol claims (iss, sub, aud, exp, iat, nonce, auth_time, acr, amr, azp, sid) always pass. [] = protocol claims only.

writable_traits.description: The identity traits a session that came from this app (a native app that exchanged its token for a session) may change through PATCH /v1/client/me. Others are refused with 403.

enabled.description: Turn risk-based MFA on or off for sign-ins to this app.

mode.description: audit scores and records sign-ins without changing them.

mid_session.description: The refresh-time check for sessions that came from this app (its native token exchange).

risk.description: Overrides of the instance's riskBasedMfa for sign-ins to this app (a sign-in started from this app's /oauth2/authorize request). A field left null keeps the instance value; weights, signals and reputation feeds stay instance-wide.

added_origins.description: Create and update responses only: the origins this write added to allowed_origins (add_redirect_origins, or because a connected integration signs users in with this client). [] when none were added.

previous_secret_expires_at.description: After a rotation with overlap: when the previous secret stops working (epoch ms). Null when only the current secret is accepted.

disabled.description: A disabled client is refused at every OAuth endpoint (kept, not deleted).

require_pkce.description: PKCE is required for this client even though it is confidential.

profile.description: The policy profile the client is assigned (PUT /v1/oauth_clients/{id}/profile).

login_url.description: Your own sign-in page for this client (PUT /v1/oauth_clients/{id}/delegated_ui).

consent_url.description: Your own consent page for this client.

delegate_consent.description: 'always' when a first-party client's consent is sent to consent_url.

device_url.description: Your own device-approval page for this client.

discovery_source.description: `cimd` when the client was created from its Client ID Metadata Document (its client_id is that document's URL); null for a registered client.

skip_logout_confirmation.description: RP-initiated logout skips the confirmation page (first-party clients only).

refresh_touches_session.description: A refresh slides the Atlas session the grant came from; once that session has ended the refresh fails (first-party clients only).

require_verified_email.description: No authorization code is issued for a user whose primary email is not verified.

status.description: Review state. development: only the owner and testers can authorize; suspended: refused at /oauth2/authorize and the token endpoint.

testers.description: User ids besides the owner who may authorize a client in development.

approved_scopes.description: Gated scopes approved for this client alone (per-scope review).

rate_limit_per_minute.description: Token endpoint requests per minute this client may make; null = no limit.

default_scopes.description: Scopes a request without `scope` gets; null = none.

require_openid.description: false = a pure-API client: no openid required, no ID token issued.

certified.description: The instance certified this client (the level above approved).

certified_at.description: When the client was certified (epoch ms); null = not certified.

subject_type.description: The `sub` this client sees: the user id, a per-sector pairwise identifier, or the user's external_id.

subject_fallback.description: With subject_type external_id: what a user without an external_id gets.

client_secret_expires_at.description: When the current client secret stops authenticating (epoch ms). Null = it does not expire.

access_token_format.description: `jwt`: a signed JWT verifiable against the JWKS. `opaque`: a random `oat_…` reference validated at the introspection endpoint (and by Atlas's own endpoints). null inherits: the API's format, then the client's, then the instance default.

token_lifetimes.description: This client's token lifetime overrides (seconds); null = inherited.

refresh_token_absolute_ttl_seconds.description: The longest a refresh token can be used. Default 2592000 (30 days).

refresh_token_idle_ttl_seconds.description: How long a refresh token survives unused; at most the absolute lifetime. Default 2592000.

session_absolute_ttl_seconds.description: The oldest a sign-in may be (age since the user authenticated) and still authorize this app silently; past it the user signs in again. Default: no limit beyond the session lifetime.

session_idle_ttl_seconds.description: How long the user's session may sit idle before this app asks them to sign in again; at most the session absolute limit. Default: no limit.

client_secret.description: The client secret — returned on create (absent when auth method is `none`); a generated one can be fetched once more within 10 minutes (client_secret_reveal).

client_secret_reveal.description: Where and until when the secret can be fetched once more (POST /v1/oauth_clients/{id}/secret/reveal). Absent when you chose the secret yourself.

has_more.description: Whether another page follows the cursor.

next_cursor.description: The cursor to pass as `starting_after` for the next page on a keyset-paginated list; null on the last page (and absent on lists that are not cursor-paginated).

post.summary: Register an OAuth client (confidential or public PKCE). A confidential client's secret is in the response; a generated one can be fetched once more within 10 minutes with POST /v1/oauth_clients/{id}/secret/reveal (`client_secret_reveal` gives the path and deadline). Send `client_secret` to choose the secret yourself (32-256 random printable characters), so a provisioning script can re-run safely. `require_verified_email: true` makes /oauth2/authorize refuse users whose primary email is not verified. Idempotent create: `external_ref` returns the existing object on a repeat (200, `idempotent_replay: true`, no secret re-shown); `metadata` tags it (filter lists with ?metadata[key]=value). `add_redirect_origins: true` also adds the redirect URIs' origins to allowed_origins (append only; listed in added_origins); a client that a connected integration signs users in with (its oauth_client_id, or tagged metadata product=<integration id>) gets them automatically.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique key per intended write (16 to 128 characters recommended, e.g. a UUID). A retry with the same key and the same request replays the first response for 24 hours with Idempotent-Replay: true; the same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, and while the first is still running a retry is 409 too. A failed write (4xx/5xx) does not consume the key. A dry run never uses it.

first_party.description: Skips the consent screen for a first-party app.

add_redirect_origins.description: Also add the origins of redirect_uris to the instance's allowed_origins: https origins, plus http://localhost, 127.0.0.1 and [::1] on a development instance; private-use schemes never. Append only (never removes an origin); an origin already allowed (exactly or by a wildcard) is skipped. Each write is an instance.updated entry in the config changelog. The response lists what was added in added_origins. A client a connected integration signs users in with gets this automatically.

skip_logout_confirmation.description: First-party clients only (422 otherwise). When true, RP-initiated logout (/oauth2/logout) with this client_id and an exactly registered post_logout_redirect_uri ends the browser session (with back- and front-channel logout) and redirects straight back with state, without the "Sign out?" page. Default false.

refresh_touches_session.description: First-party clients only (422 otherwise). When true, the sign-in of the app follows the Atlas session it came from: every successful refresh_token grant (and POST /oauth2/session/touch) also counts as activity on that Atlas session, sliding its inactivity window (never past its absolute expiry, at most one write a minute), and once that session has ended (signed out, revoked, inactive or expired) the refresh fails with invalid_grant and the grant is revoked, offline_access included. Grants not issued under a browser session (device flow, CIBA) are unaffected. Default false.

require_verified_email.description: When true, /oauth2/authorize issues no code to this client for a user whose primary email is not proven (a sign-up that skipped verification does not count). The first time, the user is sent through the hosted sign-in, which asks them to verify the address with a code, and the authorization then continues; if they come back still unverified, or under prompt=none, or when the account has no email, the application has no email provider, or the client uses its own login_url, the redirect carries error=access_denied with an error_description saying why. Only new authorizations are checked (existing refresh tokens keep working). Default false.

owner.description: The developer (an Atlas user or organization id) who owns this client. null clears (update).

status.description: Review state; default approved. development: only the owner and testers can authorize. suspended: new authorizations and refreshes are refused at once and `oauth_client.status_changed` fires on every change.

testers.description: User ids besides the owner who may authorize a client in development.

approved_scopes.description: Gated scopes (requires_verified_client) approved for this client alone, so it may request them before the whole app is approved. Only the instance sets this; changes are audited. The owner and testers of a client in development may request gated scopes without it.

default_scopes.description: The scopes an authorization or device request without `scope` gets (each must be one the client may request; include `openid` unless require_openid is false). Including offline_access here makes every sign-in a long-lived grant: a refresh token with offline_access already outlives the browser session. null clears.

default_resource.description: The identifier of the API (resource server) an authorization or device request without `resource` or `audience` is made for. Must be a registered API. null clears.

require_openid.description: Default true. false makes this a pure-API client: /oauth2/authorize accepts a request without `openid` and the token response carries an access token and no ID token. Confidential clients without the implicit grant only; PKCE rules are unchanged.

certified.description: The instance certifies (true) or withdraws certification of an approved client: the level above verified, for scopes whose requires_client_level is certified. Update only; an unapproved client cannot be certified.

rate_limit_per_minute.description: Most token endpoint requests per minute this client may make; over it the endpoint answers 429 with Retry-After. null removes the limit.

login_url.description: https URL of your own sign-in page; /oauth2/authorize then redirects there with a login_challenge. null clears (update).

consent_url.description: https URL of your own consent page (consent_challenge). null clears (update).

delegate_consent.description: 'always': a first-party client's consent is also sent to its consent_url instead of being granted silently. Needs the client's own consent_url. null clears (update).

device_url.description: https URL of your own device-approval page; /oauth2/device then sends the signed-in user there with a device_challenge. null clears (update).

secret_expires_in_seconds.description: How long the issued client secret authenticates, in seconds (reported as client_secret_expires_at). Omit for a secret that does not expire. Ignored for a public client.

subject_type.description: OpenID Connect `sub` for this client. `public` (default): the user id. `pairwise`: a per-sector identifier, the same in the id_token, access token, userinfo, introspection and back-channel logout tokens, that clients on other sectors cannot correlate. `external_id`: the user's external_id, in all of those places (a user without one follows subject_fallback). Changing it changes the `sub` of every user of the client.

subject_fallback.description: With subject_type external_id, for a user who has no external_id: `atlas_user_id` (default) uses the Atlas user id as `sub`; `refuse` fails the authorization with access_denied.

sector_identifier_uri.description: An https URL serving a JSON array that lists every redirect_uri of the client. Its host is the pairwise sector. Required for a pairwise client whose redirect_uris span more than one host; null clears it.

patch.summary: Update an OAuth client's registration (name, redirect_uris, scopes). The secret is immutable here. Accepts `metadata` (replaces the provisioning tags) and `add_redirect_origins` (adds the redirect URIs' origins to allowed_origins, append only; listed in added_origins, automatic for an integration's sign-in client).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique key per intended write (16 to 128 characters recommended, e.g. a UUID). A retry with the same key and the same request replays the first response for 24 hours with Idempotent-Replay: true; the same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, and while the first is still running a retry is 409 too. A failed write (4xx/5xx) does not consume the key. A dry run never uses it.

first_party.description: Skips the consent screen for a first-party app.

add_redirect_origins.description: Also add the origins of redirect_uris to the instance's allowed_origins: https origins, plus http://localhost, 127.0.0.1 and [::1] on a development instance; private-use schemes never. Append only (never removes an origin); an origin already allowed (exactly or by a wildcard) is skipped. Each write is an instance.updated entry in the config changelog. The response lists what was added in added_origins. A client a connected integration signs users in with gets this automatically.

skip_logout_confirmation.description: First-party clients only (422 otherwise). When true, RP-initiated logout (/oauth2/logout) with this client_id and an exactly registered post_logout_redirect_uri ends the browser session (with back- and front-channel logout) and redirects straight back with state, without the "Sign out?" page. Default false.

refresh_touches_session.description: First-party clients only (422 otherwise). When true, the sign-in of the app follows the Atlas session it came from: every successful refresh_token grant (and POST /oauth2/session/touch) also counts as activity on that Atlas session, sliding its inactivity window (never past its absolute expiry, at most one write a minute), and once that session has ended (signed out, revoked, inactive or expired) the refresh fails with invalid_grant and the grant is revoked, offline_access included. Grants not issued under a browser session (device flow, CIBA) are unaffected. Default false.

require_verified_email.description: When true, /oauth2/authorize issues no code to this client for a user whose primary email is not proven (a sign-up that skipped verification does not count). The first time, the user is sent through the hosted sign-in, which asks them to verify the address with a code, and the authorization then continues; if they come back still unverified, or under prompt=none, or when the account has no email, the application has no email provider, or the client uses its own login_url, the redirect carries error=access_denied with an error_description saying why. Only new authorizations are checked (existing refresh tokens keep working). Default false.

owner.description: The developer (an Atlas user or organization id) who owns this client. null clears (update).

status.description: Review state; default approved. development: only the owner and testers can authorize. suspended: new authorizations and refreshes are refused at once and `oauth_client.status_changed` fires on every change.

testers.description: User ids besides the owner who may authorize a client in development.

approved_scopes.description: Gated scopes (requires_verified_client) approved for this client alone, so it may request them before the whole app is approved. Only the instance sets this; changes are audited. The owner and testers of a client in development may request gated scopes without it.

default_scopes.description: The scopes an authorization or device request without `scope` gets (each must be one the client may request; include `openid` unless require_openid is false). Including offline_access here makes every sign-in a long-lived grant: a refresh token with offline_access already outlives the browser session. null clears.

default_resource.description: The identifier of the API (resource server) an authorization or device request without `resource` or `audience` is made for. Must be a registered API. null clears.

require_openid.description: Default true. false makes this a pure-API client: /oauth2/authorize accepts a request without `openid` and the token response carries an access token and no ID token. Confidential clients without the implicit grant only; PKCE rules are unchanged.

certified.description: The instance certifies (true) or withdraws certification of an approved client: the level above verified, for scopes whose requires_client_level is certified. Update only; an unapproved client cannot be certified.

post.summary: Show a confidential client's secret once more: for a script that crashed between the create (or rotate) response and saving the secret. Works once, within 10 minutes of the POST /v1/oauth_clients or POST /v1/oauth_clients/{id}/rotate_secret that generated it, and only while that secret is still the client's current one. The secret is kept encrypted for that window only and is cleared by this call, so a second call, a call after the window, a secret you chose yourself, or one rotated away since is 410 and the answer is to rotate. Audited (oauth_client.secret_revealed / oauth_client.secret_reveal_refused). An operator token needs a recent MFA. With `?dry_run=true` nothing is consumed: the response says whether the reveal is still available and until when. Unknown client is 404.

post.summary: Carry over what users granted a previous OAuth provider: records their consent and stores refresh-token hashes (bcrypt or sha256, never the tokens). An app holding an old refresh token gets a new access token from the token endpoint once, with a new Atlas refresh token; from then on it rotates as usual. Import the clients first (POST /v1/oauth_clients with client_id). The response lists one result per submitted row (index, status imported|failed, client_id, user_id, refresh_tokens, message) plus totals. Failures are reported per row and never stop the others. With `?dry_run=true` every row is validated exactly as a real import would and the same report comes back at the top level with `dry_run: true`, but nothing is written. `would_return` carries the same report for older callers and is deprecated: read the top-level fields.

post.summary: Sign a user out of this app and of Atlas in one server-side call. The path takes the client id (`oac_...`) or its public `client_id`. Body `sid` = the `sid` claim of the id_token Atlas issued to this client. Revokes every refresh grant this client holds under the sid (offline_access included) and forgets its ID-token-only sign-in; revokes the Atlas session itself exactly like POST /v1/sessions/{id}/revoke (session.revoked webhook, back-channel logout to every other app signed in through it); and sends this client a back-channel logout so its other servers hear it. Afterwards the Atlas cookie in the browser points at a dead session, so no redirect to /oauth2/logout is needed (it remains available when you want a post_logout_redirect_uri). Needs BOTH `oauth_clients:write` and `sessions:write` on the key. 404 when the client or the session is not in this instance; 403 when that session never signed in to this client (use POST /v1/sessions/{id}/revoke for any session). A session that had already ended answers `session: "already_ended"` and still has the grants of this client under it revoked. Supports `?dry_run=true`.
