post.summary: Claim a custom domain (fapi or accounts). Returns 201 with the full custom_domain object — including its `id` (dom_…), which you pass to POST /v1/domains/{id}/verify once DNS is published — plus the CNAME `instructions` to follow (a subdomain of the Atlas platform domain is refused with 403: those are assigned by Atlas only). Pass `dns: {provider: "cloudflare", api_token}` and Atlas writes the CNAME itself: it finds the zone, creates the record DNS-only (never proxied; `dns.proxied: true` is refused), waits briefly for it to resolve and verifies, so the domain can go from nothing to active in one call (`verified` in the response; otherwise call verify later). The token is stored encrypted and is never readable back (the response shows only `dns.provider` and `token_set`). An existing record that points elsewhere is not overwritten unless `dns.overwrite` is true (409 DNS_RECORD_CONFLICT); a rejected token is 422 DNS_TOKEN_REJECTED; no visible zone is 422 DNS_ZONE_NOT_FOUND.
post.description: With `method: "path"` (and `hostname`, `base_path` — default `/__atlas`), the Frontend API is served under that prefix on a host you already run, with no DNS record: the response carries `verification` (an https file whose whole body is the token, at `https://<hostname>/.well-known/atlas-verify/<token>`). Verifying fetches it (public addresses only, no redirects); on a pass the domain is active, the issuer becomes `https://<hostname><base_path>` (earlier issuers are listed in discovery for 7 days) and `instructions` says whether Atlas routes the prefix (the host is on Atlas's ingress) or which reverse-proxy rule to add. A host claimed by another instance, by any method, is 409. `base_path` without `method: "path"` is 400 (param `base_path`).

get.summary: Explain a refusal. Every error response carries a `trace_id` (and an `Atlas-Trace-Id` header); this returns the decision chain behind it: the request, the credential, the checks it passed and the one that refused (`decided_by`: captcha, policy, risk, rate_limit, scope, step_up, access_policy, verification or validation), with the error `code`, `reason`, a plain `explanation` and safe details such as the limit or the missing scope. Traces name the user when the request acted for one. Kept 7 days; rate-limit refusals are sampled (one per route per 10 seconds). Another instance trace is 404. Needs diagnostics:read.

get.summary: Check your setup in one call. Lists findings about configuration the server can see is broken or worth knowing — no sign-in method enabled, a social provider enabled without credentials, OAuth clients without redirect or post-logout URIs, a first-party client origin missing from allowed_origins, an allowed https origin that login readiness would fail (CORS or session cookie), sign-up that new users cannot complete, custom domains not serving yet, email or SMS sign-in without a provider, a Cookie Munch site that does not match the sign-in host, an OAuth client whose back-channel logout URI is failing (oauth_client_backchannel_failing: 3 consecutive failed deliveries, or one answered with a redirect, which Atlas never follows), a webhook endpoint whose last delivery was redirected (webhook_endpoint_redirecting), a webhook endpoint that is failing (webhook_endpoint_failing: a failure streak is running), switched off after repeated failures (webhook_endpoint_disabled: an error when it carries session or account events) or on a host that is not one of the instance origins or redirect hosts (webhook_endpoint_off_origin, unless it is marked external), a first-party client without a back-channel logout URI (oauth_client_no_backchannel_logout_uri), and the security posture group (group: security_posture — pkce_not_required, passkey_without_uv, auto_link_unverified) — each with a severity, a stable code, a plain message and the fix. A finding that does not apply to how the instance integrates (the embedded-component checks on an origin Atlas is confident signs in through the hosted redirect) is listed under suppressed with the reason, not in findings; integrations shows how each allowed origin was judged. ok is true when there are no errors. ok covers configuration; to confirm a browser can sign in on a given origin, use GET /v1/diagnostics/login_readiness?origin=… for each production origin. Every code is listed by GET /v1/instance/preflight/codes. A warning or info finding you have acknowledged (PUT /v1/instance/preflight/acks/{code}) is still listed, with acknowledged: { reason, by, at, expires_at } and acknowledged_at; count only the findings without it. Errors are never acknowledged. Read-only.

get.summary: Long-poll the revocation stream: one ordered list of everything that ended a session, a refresh-token family, an API key, a machine, a machine grant or a person's access, each with ids, reason and actor. Resume by cursor: pass the `next_cursor` of the previous answer as `after`. With neither `after` nor `since` it answers empty with a `next_cursor` that points at "now", so a new consumer starts from this moment. `wait` (seconds, up to 30) holds the request open until an event arrives. Order is commit order: the cursor is a sequence number assigned to what has committed, so a consumer that follows it never skips an event, however late it committed. Retention is the event log's (90 days), and webhook endpoints subscribed to the same event types are its second channel. Delivery is at-least-once and in order; keep your handler idempotent.

parameters.description: Resume after this position (the `next_cursor` of the previous answer, a whole number). Anything else is a 400. Omit, with no `since`, to start from now.

parameters.description: Start from a point in time (ISO 8601 or epoch ms) instead of a cursor.

parameters.description: Seconds to wait for an event when there is none yet, 0 to 30. Default 0.

get.summary: Server-Sent Events stream of the revocation stream (the same events as `GET /v1/revocations`). Each `revocation` event carries the frame as JSON and its `seq` as the SSE `id`; resume with `Last-Event-ID` or `after`. post.summary: Take an amount from one of a grant's counters, atomically. A denial is a 200 decision with `allowed: false`.
post.description: The grant defines its counters in `constraints.counters`, for example `{ "orders": { "limit": 10, "window": "day" } }`. The limit is read from the grant on every call. Windows are fixed and aligned to UTC (`none`, `minute`, `hour`, `day`, `month`). `idempotency_key` is required and unique per grant and counter: a repeat returns the stored original decision, even after the window has rolled. A counter with `amount_field` takes its amount from that field of `context`. With `lease: true` the amount is reserved for `ttl_seconds` (at most 300, and never past the window); the unused part returns when the lease is released or expires. Leases are refused for counters with `amount_field`. Crossing 80% and 100% of a window emits `grant.usage_threshold`, and reaching 100% also emits `grant.exhausted`.

put.summary: Rotate the instance signing key automatically. Every interval_days the worker publishes a new key (prepublish_hours before it signs), switches to it, and keeps the previous key published until every token it signed has expired: at least the longest token lifetime the instance uses plus the key set cache, never under 24 hours, and never dropped while one of its tokens can still be presented. Keys in a cloud KMS rotate at the scheduled time (they cannot be held back) and are limited to RS256 and ES256. An earlier rotation still inside its grace window postpones the next one. Needs a recent MFA sign-in.

post.summary: Delegate authority to an agent. A root delegation (delegator_user_id) lets the agent act for that user; a child (parent_delegation_id) lets an agent pass part of what it holds to a sub-agent. A child can only narrow its parent: its scopes must be a subset, its lifetime ends no later, and the chain is limited by the instance's maxDelegationDepth. Loops are refused. The agent's tokens then carry delegation and act claims, are narrowed to the delegated scopes, and stop verifying when the delegation is revoked. Needs a recent MFA sign-in. Honours Idempotency-Key.

post.summary: Check a signed bot request (Web Bot Auth, RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures, Ed25519, tag web-bot-auth). Send the method, the absolute URL and the headers your server received. Atlas reads the Signature-Agent header, fetches the bot's key directory from <Signature-Agent>/.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory (cached, over a transport that refuses private addresses), checks the keyid against the keys' JWK thumbprints, verifies the signature and its created/expires window, then applies your allow and block lists. decision is allow, block or unknown; only a verified request is ever allowed or blocked. The decision is written to the audit log (agent.web_bot_auth_decision). 600 calls per minute.

put.summary: Save a page template as the page's draft. A template is data: components (heading, text, image, link, button_link, list, divider, spacer, columns, custom) in four regions (header, above_form, below_form, footer). It is validated on save: https and mailto links only, and no script ever. A custom component carries your own html and css (and a frame height in pixels, 40 to 1200): only an allowlisted set of tags, attributes and CSS properties is accepted (anything else is refused with the reason: a 400 naming the first problems), and it is drawn in a sandboxed frame that cannot reach the sign-in form. The live page is unchanged until you promote. mfa, reset and verify are the sign-in steps (second factor, password reset, email verification): their template replaces the page's while the step shows. consent and device are the OAuth consent and device pages. client_id, organization_id and locale save it for that audience.

get.summary: Read the instance's referral attribution settings: provider, endpoint, capture parameters, consent, auto-enroll and link template, with the connection status and the providers Atlas supports. Secrets are reported as *_set markers only.

provider.description: `webhook` (the Atlas referral protocol, any platform) or a built-in vendor adapter id (`referalli`, `dub`, `firstpromoter`). The retired spelling `referally` is accepted on write and reads back as `referalli`; see `providers[].aliases`.

endpoint_url.description: Base URL of the platform connection (generic protocol).

connection_id.description: Your label for the connection on the platform side.

provider_aliases.description: Retired spellings of `provider` that are still accepted on write.

partner.description: Registers a referral code the user chose in your app with the platform.

auto_enroll.description: Every new user becomes a referrer: the platform returns the partner's code and tracked link in the sign-up answer, and Atlas stores them.

alias.description: Re-keys a customer whose external_id changed after sign-up.

user.description: Takes user lifecycle updates (email, name, suspension).

ping.description: Answers a ping for "Test connection" (org, program, clock).

identity.description: Answers a read of a user's own referral code and link; Atlas uses it to fill a user's code after a sign-in and for existing users when the connection is made.

origins.description: Takes the instance's app origins on its connection, so its browser calls pass CORS with no dashboard step.

widget_token.description: Mints a short-lived token for the platform's live widget (hosted_panel "widget").

inbound.description: Sends Atlas referral changes made after sign-up (two-way sync).

accounts.description: Takes an organization's owner (accountRef = the organization's external_id, else its id; ownerCustomerRef = the owner's customerRef), so the organization's payments earn for the owner's referral. On only while the platform's ping advertises `accounts`.

capabilities.description: What the chosen provider can do now: its built-in capabilities plus anything its last ping advertised (`partner` turns on only when the platform says it accepts user-chosen codes).

one_click.description: One-click connect to a referral platform (an OAuth install: the merchant picks an organization and program, and no secret is copied). `one_click` is the Referalli preset; `one_click_presets` lists every platform.

id.description: The preset id to put in the install URL.

available.description: Whether this deployment offers it. When false, connect with a key or the signing secret.

redirect_uri.description: Atlas's callback, the redirect URI to register with the platform.

items.description: One-click connect to a referral platform (an OAuth install: the merchant picks an organization and program, and no secret is copied). `one_click` is the Referalli preset; `one_click_presets` lists every platform.

id.description: The preset id to put in the install URL.

available.description: Whether this deployment offers it. When false, connect with a key or the signing secret.

redirect_uri.description: Atlas's callback, the redirect URI to register with the platform.

one_click_presets.description: Every platform this deployment offers a one-click install for.

signing_secret_set.description: Whether a signing secret is stored (the value is never returned).

api_key_set.description: Whether a vendor API key is stored (the value is never returned).

url_params.description: Query parameters that carry a referral code, in priority order.

context_cookie.description: Compatibility: the first entry of `context_cookies` (null when there is none). Kept for clients written against the single-cookie field; read `context_cookies`.

context_cookies.description: The canonical field. First-party tracking cookies read under consent, in the order they are tried (the first one present wins). Empty = never read a cookie.

auto_enroll_users.description: Every new user becomes a referrer (gets a code and link from the platform).

partner_portal_url.description: The partner portal a referrer manages their partnership in (payouts, stats). Linked from the "Refer a friend" panel on the hosted account page (/hosted/user); null = no portal link.

timeout_ms.description: How long a sign-up waits for the platform (100-5000).

tracking_token.description: Public tracking token (Referalli provider); powers the "Invited by" code lookup. Not a secret.

code_lookup_url.description: Public, CORS-enabled URL template containing {code}. The hosted sign-up page calls it from the browser and shows "X invited you" when it answers {valid: true, partnerDisplayName, refereeReward?}. Null = no lookup (a built-in provider may supply its own).

signup_code_field.description: Show an optional "Referral code" field on hosted sign-up (default false).

browser_sources.description: The referral programs whose script or cookie the browser reads, in order. Defaults to the provider's own program (every program for the Atlas referral protocol).

browser_sources_default.description: Whether browser_sources is the provider's default.

consent_provider.description: Which consent manager decides on the tracking cookie's ids: auto (any common one), one manager, or app (only the app's referralConsent). Default auto.

forward_lifecycle.description: Forward reported users' email / name changes and suspension status to the platform (default true).

mirror_to_public_metadata.description: Mirror the result into the user's public_metadata.referral {referred_by, partner_id, own_code} (own_code is kept for existing readers), and the user's own code and link into public_metadata.<provider id> {code, linkUrl} (for example public_metadata.referalli). Skipped, never forced, when the bag would pass the 8 KB metadata limit (default false).

hosted_panel.description: What the hosted account page's referrals panel draws: the static code and link, or the platform's live widget (default link).

include_referral_claims.description: Add the user's own code as a referral_code claim, and their link as referral_link when one is stored, to session tokens and ID tokens (default false). Both are absent for a user with no code.

report_linked_atlas_id_signups.description: Report the first sign-in of an Atlas ID account to a Sign in with Atlas app this instance manages (adopted with PUT /v1/platform/atlas_id_apps/{id}/managed_by) as a sign-up, with customerRef = the sub the app sees and the referral read from the authorize request. The answer arrives as user.referral_attributed with source sign_in_with_atlas and a link_kind: automatic when the code was read from the landing URL parameters named in url_params, explicit when the app forwarded ref / ref_* parameters on the authorize request. A repeat sign-in reports nothing. Default false.

missing.description: What the chosen provider still needs before referrals can be enabled.

last_ping.description: The last ping ("Test connection") of a provider that answers one.

error_code.description: e.g. signature_rejected, connection_paused, timeout, network_error, ping_not_ok.

auto_enroll_users.description: The platform connection's own auto-enrol setting.

server_time.description: The platform's clock as it reported it.

clock_skew_ms.description: The platform's clock minus Atlas's, in ms.

clock_skew_warning.description: True when the skew is over 60 seconds.

A body field this route does not know, top level or inside security, is 422 UNKNOWN_FIELD with param naming it, and nothing is saved; a known field with a bad value is 400 VALIDATION_FAILED with param. post.summary: Start a one-click connection to a referral platform (`:preset` is `referalli` or any platform listed in `one_click_presets` of the settings): returns the platform's authorize URL (OAuth, PKCE). The merchant picks an organization and program there; the platform creates the connection and returns its signing secret to Atlas server to server, so nothing is copied. For Referalli, Atlas then requires v2 signatures and registers the two-way sync webhook; it pings either way. Referrals stay off until you turn them on. 404 for an unknown preset; 422 REFERRALS_NOT_CONFIGURED when this deployment does not offer it (see `available` in `one_click_presets`): connect with a key or the signing secret instead. Any platform can implement the install: see the referral protocol guide.

post.summary: Backfill: queue sign-up calls for existing users created since a date, each with its real sign-up time, so the platform dates the referrals correctly and replays the payments since. Codes come from `codes` or a metadata path; users with no code are reported only when auto_enroll_users is on; users already reported are skipped unless `force` is set. `user_ids` limits the job to those users (`since` is then optional). Calls go out at about 10 per second. Up to 10,000 users per request. Requires referrals to be on (422 REFERRALS_NOT_CONFIGURED).

post.summary: Send every organization's owner to the referral platform once (an `accounts` call per organization: accountRef = the organization's external_id, else its id; ownerCustomerRef = the owner's customerRef). The owner is the organization's creator while they hold the creator role or org:admin, else the longest-standing member holding one of those roles; organizations with no such member are counted in organizations_without_owner and skipped. Calls go out at about 10 per second through the delivery log (kind `accounts`), oldest first, up to 10,000 organizations per request (continue with `starting_after` = `next_starting_after`); the platform treats a repeat as a no-op. Atlas already sends these on its own when an organization is created, its external_id changes or its owner changes, and once when the platform first advertises `accounts`: use this after restoring data or to be sure. Requires referrals to be on and the platform to advertise `accounts` (422 REFERRALS_NOT_CONFIGURED otherwise).

get.summary: Read the instance's before_user_create hook: the endpoint Atlas calls for every self-service sign-up so your app can set the user's external_id and metadata first. The signing secret is reported as signing_secret_set only.

enabled.description: Whether the hook is live. False while it is pending.

pending.description: True while the hook was declared enabled: "pending" and has not passed its test yet. It is off until then.

pending_since.description: When it was declared pending (ms since epoch); null when not pending.

last_test_at.description: When the background check last ran (ms since epoch).

last_test_error.description: Why the last background check failed, or that Atlas stopped checking after 7 days.

url.description: Your endpoint. https only (http only for localhost on a development instance).

signing_secret_set.description: Whether a signing secret is stored (the value is never returned).

timeout_ms.description: How long a sign-up waits for the hook (500-5000, default 3000).

fail_closed.description: When true, a timeout, error or unusable answer refuses the sign-up (403 SIGN_UP_DENIED) instead of letting it continue without your answer. Default false.

last_call.description: The outcome of the last REAL call (a sign-up); "Test hook" calls do not change it. Null until the first real sign-up reaches the hook. Every call, tests included, is in GET …/before_user_create/calls.

error.description: Why it failed; for denied, the reason your hook gave.

recent.description: Real calls in the last 24 hours (on GET only). A failed or timed-out call let the sign-up through without your answer (no external_id), unless fail_closed refused it.

failed_24h.description: Calls that timed out, errored or answered something unusable (denials are not failures).

patch.summary: Update the before_user_create hook. Only the fields you send change; null clears. The hook is called (signed like a webhook) after the user id is assigned and before user.created, the referral call and any session. It may answer {external_id, public_metadata, private_metadata, unsafe_metadata}, or deny the sign-up with {"deny": true, "reason": "..."} or HTTP 403: the person gets 403 SIGN_UP_DENIED with your reason, no user is kept and no user.created is sent. A slow or failing hook does not block the sign-up unless fail_closed is true. The body (schema BeforeUserCreateHookRequest; your answer is BeforeUserCreateHookResponse) carries data.user, data.strategy, data.referral, data.request ({client_id, app_context, login_hint} of the authorize request, nulls when absent) and data.invitation (the pending instance invitation for the address, or null) and data.organization ({id, external_id, role, role_mapped, via: sso | domain} when the sign-up comes through an organization SSO connection or a captured auto-join domain, else null). Turning the hook on, or changing the url or signing_secret of a fail_closed enabled one (or turning fail_closed on for it), first sends the signed test call: unless it returns a valid answer (an answer object, possibly empty, or a deny) the change is refused with 409 HOOK_TEST_FAILED (meta: url, status, the first 200 bytes of the response body, outcome) and the hook stays as it was. ?force=true (or force in the body) skips the test and is audit-logged. enabled: "pending" stores the hook OFF without testing (sign-ups proceed and the hook is not called, fail_closed included) and Atlas turns it on in the background once the test passes (see GET: pending, pending_since, last_test_at, last_test_error). A dry run (?dry_run=true) makes the same test call and changes nothing: it answers would_return (the hook exactly as the PATCH would leave it, e.g. enabled: true) and changes [{section, before, after}] with would_return_status 200, or would_return_status 409 with the refusal. An enabled hook that is not fail_closed is not re-tested when its url or secret changes.

post.summary: Send a sample sign-up (a user that does not exist) to the hook and report its answer. Nothing is stored on any user; the call appears in the delivery log flagged test, and does not change last_call. The call says it is a test: `"test": true` in the body (real calls send false) and an `atlas-test: 1` header, so the hook answers without reserving an id or creating anything. Answers with the shared test-call fields ok, status (success | failed), http_status and latency_ms (the same four a webhook endpoint test returns), plus answer or error.

post.summary: Spend units of a plan feature for a user or organization, atomically and exactly once per `idempotency_key`. The answer is the decision (200 whether allowed or not; `reason` is `not_entitled` or `limit_reached`); a retry with the same key replays it and never spends twice. Who counts: when the subject's live subscription is on an entitlement provider (Autumn, Commet) that provider owns the balance and `source` is `provider`; otherwise Atlas counts (`source` `atlas`) against the plan's numeric limit for the feature (`-1` or no limit is unlimited) in the current billing period, or the UTC calendar month when there is no period. For `atlas` the limit check and the write are one transaction, so concurrent consumes can never pass the limit. A consume does not bill: report billable usage with POST /v1/billing/usage. Emits entitlement.limit_reached once, when a consume takes the window to its limit.

post.summary: Create a custom OAuth 2.0 / OIDC provider (Atlas is the relying party). OIDC: give the issuer and the endpoints are discovered (a bad issuer is a 400 now, not a broken button later). OAuth 2.0: give the authorize, token and userinfo endpoints. Set client authentication (client_secret_basic/post/jwt, private_key_jwt with an Atlas-held key, or none), a declarative profile_mapping, upstream logout and third-party initiated login. The response names the URLs to register at the provider. Starts disabled unless `enabled: true` (which needs a client id, a secret for the secret methods, and a signing key for private_key_jwt).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique key per intended write (16 to 128 characters recommended, e.g. a UUID). A retry with the same key and the same request replays the first response for 24 hours with Idempotent-Replay: true; the same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, and while the first is still running a retry is 409 too. A failed write (4xx/5xx) does not consume the key. A dry run never uses it.

A random data key is created, wrapped by the KMS key set with PUT /v1/vault/key_provider (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS or Azure Key Vault) and proved by an unwrap before anything depends on it. From then on everything Atlas encrypts for the instance depends on that KMS key; values written earlier stay readable until the re-encryption sweep has moved them. If the key is later disabled, deleted or its access removed, requests that need the instance data fail with 503 CUSTOMER_KEY_UNAVAILABLE within five minutes; nothing falls back to a platform key.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique key per intended write (16 to 128 characters recommended, e.g. a UUID). A retry with the same key and the same request replays the first response for 24 hours with Idempotent-Replay: true; the same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, and while the first is still running a retry is 409 too. A failed write (4xx/5xx) does not consume the key. A dry run never uses it.

422.description: Unprocessable. Includes UNKNOWN_FIELD when the request sends `Atlas-Strict: true` (or the instance enables strict request bodies) and the body has a field this endpoint does not accept.

put.summary: Set the cache window: how long Atlas may use a loaded data key without your KMS confirming it, which is how long a revoked key keeps working (60 to 3,600 seconds, default 300). Shorter revokes faster but depends on the KMS being reachable more tightly: Atlas re-confirms every 20 seconds, so a KMS outage longer than the window takes the instance down.

post.summary: Define a connection: an owner (an organization or a user) and a third-party API. `kind` is oauth (rides a linked provider account; for an organization, the account of the member who shared it), api_key or client_credentials (a credential the owner enters). `allowed_hosts` lists the only hosts the relay may call. An owner may hold several connections of one provider (one per provider account): create one per account, then call `POST /v1/connections/{id}/connect`. A connection is never a sign-in method.

parameters.description: A unique key per intended write (16 to 128 characters recommended, e.g. a UUID). A retry with the same key and the same request replays the first response for 24 hours with Idempotent-Replay: true; the same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, and while the first is still running a retry is 409 too. A failed write (4xx/5xx) does not consume the key. A dry run never uses it.

type.description: external: an opaque id from your own account system (up to 128 characters), for a SaaS that does not run its sign-in on Atlas yet. It needs no Atlas user or organization and counts toward no MAU. Move it to a real user or organization later with PATCH owner: nothing reconnects.

provider.description: A built-in or custom OAuth provider key for oauth; any short key otherwise.

config.description: api_key: placement (header or query), name, scheme. custom_header: name. hmac_secret: algorithm, encoding, signature_header, prefix, timestamp_header. client_credentials: token_url, client_id, scopes, auth_style, grant_type, account_id, audience, resource, extra_params, request_format, token_header. jwt_bearer: preset, token_url, issuer, subject, audience, scopes, alg, lifetime_seconds, extra_claims. oauth1: preset (netsuite_tba, x_ads, discogs, trademe, bricklink, cardmarket), mode (tba = entered keys, three_legged), signature_method (HMAC-SHA1, HMAC-SHA256, PLAINTEXT), realm, realm_from_url, scope, request_token_url, authorize_url, access_token_url, request_token_method. github_app_installation: app_id, client_id, app_slug, installation_id, repositories, permissions. admin_consent: tenant, scope. oauth: scopes, user_scopes (Slack), install_redirect_url (Shopify). Any kind: metadata (handles you set by hand, such as {"marketplace_id":"EBAY_GB"}; returned with the provider's own handles on token reads) and signing (per-request signing, see POST /v1/connections/{id}/sign).

metadata.description: Shorthand for config.metadata: up to 20 lowercase keys with string values. eBay: marketplace_id (EBAY_US, EBAY_GB...).

allowed_methods.description: Relay verbs allowed for this connection (default GET, HEAD, POST).

environment.description: The provider environment the credential belongs to. sandbox selects the provider's test hosts (Salesforce test.salesforce.com, PayPal and QuickBooks sandboxes, DocuSign demo...).

host_params.description: Values that fill the provider's host templates for this one connection, for example {"subdomain":"acme"} (Zendesk), {"shop":"acme"} (Shopify), {"domain":"acme.my.salesforce.com"} (Salesforce My Domain), {"data_center":"eu"} (Zoho), {"tenant":"contoso.onmicrosoft.com"} (Microsoft), {"host":"git.example.com"} (self-managed GitLab). Each key is checked against that provider's allowlist pattern; a value that is not a plain label or public hostname is refused with 400 `host_params.<key>`.

purpose.description: Only data is accepted. A sign-in link is an external account.

type.description: external: an opaque id from your own account system (up to 128 characters), for a SaaS that does not run its sign-in on Atlas yet. It needs no Atlas user or organization and counts toward no MAU. Move it to a real user or organization later with PATCH owner: nothing reconnects.

name.description: Your label for this account, for example "Support inbox".

status.description: needs_reauth: the token expired or was refused and cannot be refreshed. revoked: disconnected on purpose.

scopes.description: The scopes the provider granted.

expires_at.description: When the access token expires, epoch milliseconds. Refreshed automatically on read.

refresh_expires_at.description: When the provider retires the refresh token (epoch ms): the lifetime the provider stated, or its documented default (eBay about 18 months, Etsy and Shopify 90 days from the last refresh). connection.expiring goes out 14, 3 and 1 days before. Null when unknown or when there is no refresh token.

authorized_by_user_id.description: Who connected it. Informational only: the connection does not depend on that user, who may be deleted.

code.description: The provider's own error when it answered (invalid_grant, invalid_client...), else a local reason (no_refresh_token, unauthorized, host_changed).

httpStatus.description: The HTTP status the provider answered with.

last_error.description: Why the connection left connected, or why the last refresh failed.

refresh_failures.description: Consecutive failed refreshes; 0 when healthy. A provider outage is retried with backoff and announced (connection.refresh_failed) after 3.

next_refresh_at.description: When the keep-alive worker next refreshes this connection (epoch milliseconds), null when there is nothing to keep alive.

external_account_id.description: Deprecated, always null: a connection owns its tokens and no longer rides a user's linked account.

has_secret.description: Whether a credential is stored. The credential itself is never returned by this object.

secret_expires_at.description: When the entered credential expires (epoch ms). connection.secret_expiring reminders go out 30, 7 and 1 days before.

previous_valid_until.description: While a rotation's overlap window is open: when the replaced version stops being accepted (epoch ms).

allowed_methods.description: The relay verbs this connection may use. GET, HEAD and POST unless set.

created_at.description: When the connection was created (epoch ms).

updated_at.description: When the connection last changed (epoch ms).

A WooCommerce store (`provider` woocommerce, `kind` basic, `host_params.store` the store host) is connected through its key handshake: send the owner to the returned URL, the store approves and posts a consumer key and secret to Atlas, which keeps them as the connection's basic credential. Reconnecting the same provider account updates the same connection; a different account answers 409 unless `create_if_new` is true. get.summary: The connection's live token for your backend. An oauth connection's token is refreshed first when it is expired or about to be (single-flight across processes, using the client that issued it and the connection's host_params). Built for sync workers: the response carries an `ETag` and `Cache-Control: private, max-age=<seconds until just before expires_at>`, so cache it until then; send `If-None-Match` and an unchanged, still-valid token answers 304 with no body and no vault read; `min_ttl_seconds` refreshes first when less than that much validity remains. A grant connection (client_credentials, jwt_bearer, github_app_installation, admin_consent) has its token minted from the credential Atlas holds instead, answered with `Cache-Control: no-store` (no ETag); pass `subject` to a jwt_bearer connection to act as that user (Google domain-wide delegation). Includes the captured handles (`metadata`, `token_response`) and any further named credentials. 402 CONNECTION_REQUIRED with `meta.reason` not_connected, needs_reauth, revoked or refresh_failed when there is no usable token. When the provider answers 401 to the token, call `POST /v1/connections/{id}/token/refresh` instead of re-reading. Rate limit: 6,000 reads per minute per secret key and 300 per minute per connection by default, plus any per-provider limit you set; raise or set them with `PUT /v1/connections/token_limits` (RateLimit-* headers on every response, 429 with Retry-After beyond them). Reads are audited as connection.token_read once per connection per minute with the read count (a read that refreshed is always audited); the token itself is never logged.

post.summary: Bulk-import existing provider refresh tokens as connections, up to 500 rows, so nobody reconnects. Each row: provider, owner, external_id (the provider-side account: how a re-import finds the same connection), refresh_token (or access_token), and optionally scopes, metadata, environment, host_params, name, allowed_hosts and token_family (rows that were exported with the same token_family came from one grant and share one refresh token: the first row spends it, the others join its token set as siblings). By default (validate true) each refresh token is spent once against the provider with the OAuth client that will own the connection, and the tokens the provider issues are stored, so the imported copy stops being current on a rotating provider. Rows are OAuth by default; a row with `kind` (api_key, bearer, basic, custom_header, hmac_secret, client_credentials, oauth1 and the other credential kinds) instead carries `credentials` (the kind's secret fields exactly as PUT /v1/connections/{id}/credentials takes them: api_key, token, username and password, value, secret, client_secret, or for oauth1 consumer_key, consumer_secret, token and token_secret), a non-secret `config` (placement, header name, signing, oauth1 preset such as discogs, trademe, bricklink or cardmarket...) and allowed_hosts. Credentials are checked by the same parser as credential entry and stored encrypted in the vault the same way; nothing is sent to the provider, so a dry run reports them ok_unverified or invalid_row (a missing credential field). An imported Shopify access token without a refresh token is a non-expiring offline token: it is stored as is and keeps working, unless exchange_expiring is true, which swaps it for an expiring token with a refresh token. A failing row creates and changes nothing. Rows may also carry refresh_token_expires_at (epoch ms or ISO 8601) and config.scopes. dry_run (in the body or as ?dry_run=true) stores nothing and reports per row `check`: ok (the provider accepted a refresh), refresh_refused, invalid_row, provider_unavailable, or ok_unverified (shape checked only). A provider that rotates refresh tokens would lose the customer's token to a dry-run refresh, so its rows are ok_unverified unless verify is true (body or ?verify=true), which accepts that rotation. A row whose provider has a unique_external_id policy and whose account another owner holds fails with external_id_taken. Idempotent on Idempotency-Key. Tokens go straight to the vault and never appear in the answer or the audit log.

A failed write (4xx/5xx) does not consume the key. A dry run never uses it.

host_aliases.description: The declared host aliases (see the PUT body).

put.summary: Set the cookie-consent CMP for the hosted pages (any provider). Replaces the whole setting; a body of just { "enabled": false } (or true) switches the stored setting off (or on) instead. script_url and every extra_origins entry must be https URLs; only their exact origins are added to the page CSP. Optional settings_link adds a "Cookie settings" link to the page footer that reopens the CMP preferences. When the CMP is Cookie Munch (script on cookiemunch.net) and a site_id is set, the save also checks the site with Cookie Munch and returns warnings: cmp_site_unknown when Cookie Munch does not know the id, cmp_site_domain_mismatch when the site is not registered and verified for the sign-in host or a parent domain of it (unless that host is listed in host_aliases). The check has a short timeout and never fails the save. A body of just { "host_aliases": ["<slug>-fapi.atlasauth.net"] } declares the hosted-pages host as an alias of the site, for a product with no domain of its own to register at the consent manager.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique key per intended write (16 to 128 characters recommended, e.g. a UUID). A retry with the same key and the same request replays the first response for 24 hours with Idempotent-Replay: true; the same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, and while the first is still running a retry is 409 too. A failed write (4xx/5xx) does not consume the key. A dry run never uses it.

schema.description: The whole setting (script_url required), or just { "enabled": false | true } to switch a stored setting off or on without deleting it, or just { "host_aliases": [...] } to declare hosts.

enabled.description: false keeps the configuration but renders nothing (no CMP script, no CSP origins, no settings link). Default true. Sent alone, it toggles the stored setting.

script_url.description: Your CMP script URL. Must be https; its origin is added to the page CSP.

site_id.description: Your CMP site id (sent as data-cbid). Send this or site, not both.

provider.description: The linked partner platform id, e.g. cookiemunch.

host.description: The host the site is registered for.

site.description: Name the CMP site by reference instead of site_id. Atlas looks up the verified site registered for the host (or a parent domain) through the linked partner platform on every save and stores both the reference and the resolved id; the check re-resolves when it fails. 400 when the provider is not linked or no site matches the host.

blocking_mode.description: The CMP prior-blocking mode, e.g. "auto" (sent as data-blockingmode).

extra_origins.description: Other https URLs the CMP loads from or calls; each origin is added to the page CSP.

settings_link.description: A "Cookie settings" link in the footer of the hosted sign-in, sign-up and account pages and Sign in with Atlas pages, for reopening the CMP preferences. Needs a preset or at least one attribute. null or omitted: no link. Unknown fields inside it are reported in Atlas-Unknown-Fields (e.g. settings_link.foo).

label.description: The base link text (English), e.g. "Cookie settings".

labels.description: Per-language link text, keyed by page locale (any language the hosted pages speak: en, es, fr, de, pt-BR, ja, nl, ar, he, fa, hi, zh-Hans, zh-Hant, ko, it, pl, tr, ru, sv, id, vi, th; any other key is refused with a 400). Each value is 1-60 characters. The hosted page renders labels[<page locale>], else (on a non-English page) the preset's own translation of "Cookie settings", else label.

preset.description: Fills in the CMP's reopen trigger: cookiemunch adds data-cc="show-settings"; cookiebot calls Cookiebot.renew(); onetrust calls OneTrust.ToggleInfoDisplay(); custom adds nothing (use attributes).

attributes.description: Extra attributes for the link. Allowed names: data-*, aria-*, id, class, and href (an https URL or a #fragment). Event handlers (on*), style and every other name are refused with a 400; data-atlas-* is reserved for presets. Values are at most 200 characters and are HTML-escaped.

culture.description: page (default): the CMP tag on the hosted pages carries data-culture=<the page language> (?locale=, else Accept-Language), so the banner matches the page. browser: no data-culture; the CMP picks its own language.

host_aliases.description: Hosts the hosted pages are served on that your consent manager's site is knowingly not registered for, typically the instance's default `<slug>-fapi.atlasauth.net` host when your product has no domain of its own to register. Bare hostnames. A Cookie Munch site check that finds the site registered for another domain reads as ok on these hosts (no cmp_site_domain_mismatch). Sent alone ({ "host_aliases": [...] }) it sets only the aliases and keeps the CMP setting, also when an integration supplies the CMP; [] or null clears them. Omitted on a full PUT, they stay as they are. DELETE clears them.

allOf.description: The consent-management platform (CMP) injected into the hosted pages. enabled:false with no other fields when none is set; enabled:false WITH the fields when it is configured but switched off.

enabled.description: Whether the CMP (and the settings link) render on the hosted pages.

site.description: The site reference ({ provider, host }) when the site was named by reference; site_id is what it resolved to.

rendered_labels.description: The text the link renders on a page in each supported locale.

rendered_attributes.description: The attributes the rendered link carries: yours plus the preset's trigger.

culture.description: page (default): the CMP tag carries data-culture=<page language>, the same tag as <html lang>. browser: no attribute.

name.description: The exact name, or null when pattern describes a family of keys.

pattern.description: A * wildcard for keys with an id suffix, e.g. atlasid:*.

domain.description: For a cookie: its Domain (a leading dot = your registrable domain and its subdomains, when cross-subdomain cookies are on) or the exact Frontend API host for a host-only cookie. For storage: "your app's origin".

path.description: For a cookie: the Path it is set at. On a path mount, __session and __atlas_uat stay at / (your app reads them) and every other Atlas cookie moves under the base path (/__atlas, /__atlas/v1, ...). Null for browser storage.

lifetime_seconds.description: Seconds; null = browser session (cookie) or until cleared (storage).

lifetime.description: The lifetime in words, for a cookie policy table.

lifetime_range.description: Present when the lifetime follows an instance setting (session.absoluteMs for __atlas_rt, __atlas_uat, __atlas_sessions and __atlas_fedcm): lifetime_seconds is this instance's value, which wins over the default the product-wide embed manifest shows; min/max bound what any instance can set.

purposes.description: The purpose in every language the hosted pages speak, keyed by locale (en, es, fr, de, pt-BR, ja, nl, ar, he, fa, hi, zh-Hans, zh-Hant, ko, it, pl, tr, ru, sv, id, vi, th).

get.summary: Every cookie and browser-storage key the hosted pages set for this instance as a CMP-neutral declaration (name, provider, domain, category, type cookie or localStorage, duration, description), with the domain computed from your sign-in host and cross-subdomain setting. A consent manager imports it once; no manual rows. Needs only cookie_consent:read. Without a key the same list is public: GET /v1/storage_declaration on the Frontend API host.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: json (default), or csv: name,provider,domain,category,purpose,duration,duration_seconds,type,description for a generic importer.

declarations.description: See GET /v1/storage_declaration for the row shape.

get.summary: One report of everything that connects the instance to the outside world, in the shared integration-health shape { checks: [{ id, ok, detail, fix, docs, hop? }], generatedAt }: every preflight finding (id = its code), the links to other platforms, each webhook endpoint (failing or disabled, with the hop that fails: dns, tls, http, a challenge page, or auth), back-channel logout receivers, the referral platform, the email sender, the consent manager and the SDK versions seen. ok: null means not known or not configured. Failing receivers are probed live (at most 6 per report).

parameters.name: only
parameters.description: Only these sources, comma-separated (see GET /v1/integration-health/providers). An unknown source is a 400.

parameters.name: probe
parameters.description: false: no live reachability probes; the hop comes from the recorded deliveries only.

id.description: A preflight code verbatim, or <source>.<check> (webhooks.endpoint_failing, email.provider, …).

ok.description: false = failing; null = not known or not configured (never "fine").

hop.description: For a reachability check: the hop that failed.

status.description: The HTTP status a reachability check saw.

source.description: The provider that produced the row (preflight, connections, webhooks, backchannel, referrals, email, consent, sdk, …).

observedAt.description: Epoch ms of the evidence (the last delivery or test).

get.summary: The integration-health check providers (source and what each one reports).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1-500. Without limit (and without starting_after) the whole list is returned.

parameters.name: starting_after
parameters.description: Cursor: return only items after this one. Pass the previous page's `next_cursor` (the last item's id). An unknown cursor is a 400.

get.summary: Every identity integration: the four presets (chatly, forumulate, cookiemunch, referalli; connected or not) and every custom integration, each with its health — last mint, mints and reported verify errors in the last 24 hours, the last verify error, and the event and back-channel logout receivers (state, failing_since, consecutive failures, 24-hour success rate).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1-500. Without limit (and without starting_after) the whole list is returned.

parameters.name: starting_after
parameters.description: Cursor: return only items after this one. Pass the previous page's `next_cursor` (the last item's id). An unknown cursor is a 400.

items.description: enabled:false, connected:false (and nothing else) when the integration was never connected. A preset answers object <preset>_integration (chatly_integration, …) with its own fields; a custom integration answers object integration.

added_origins.description: PUT only: the origins this write added to allowed_origins from the redirect URIs of the OAuth client the service signs users in with. [] when none were missing.

warnings.description: PUT only (forumulate; [] otherwise): what already replaces the Atlas reader button in Forumulate, read from each configured space's public reader sign-in settings (up to 5 spaces). existing_sign_in_url_overrides: an org- or space-level signInUrl sends readers to that page instead of showing any sign-in button (sign_in_url, space_ids). atlas_reader_provider_missing: the spaces offer other providers and not the Atlas one. Report only, unless the PUT sent replace_existing with a Forumulate API key: then Atlas makes the change, and replace_failed says why it could not (the integration is saved either way). A space Atlas cannot read adds nothing. Never blocks the save.

events_secret_stored.description: PUT with forumulate_api_key (forumulate, default events_url) only: the Atlas reader providers in Forumulate that received the events signing secret as webhookSecret. The secret itself is never in this answer. null when it could not be stored (see the events_secret_not_stored warning).

channel.description: PUT with chatly_api_key (chatly): the channel that received the events signing secret.

replaced.description: PUT with replace_existing (forumulate) only: what Atlas changed in Forumulate's org reader sign-in registry. null when it could not (see the replace_failed warning).

sign_in_url_cleared.description: The org-level signInUrl that was cleared, or null when none was set.

providers_removed.description: The reader providers removed: every one that is not the Atlas provider.

audience.description: The aud of every token minted for it.

audience_format.description: Custom only: the regular expression the audience must match.

template.description: chatly: the name getToken({ template: 'chatly' }) (deprecated alias) uses.

identity_verification.description: chatly: what the channel's identity verification needs (no shared secret).

spaces.description: forumulate: the connected spaces and where a reader redeems a token. Reader cookies are host-only, so the redeem must happen on the host the reader reads.

redeem_url.description: Where the reader's browser redeems the token: the redeem_url you gave, else the space's primary reader address (its site or custom domain, the first of its readerEndpoints in Forumulate, read when you send forumulate_api_key), else the platform address https://forumulate.com/api/public/orgs/<org>/spaces/<id>/reader-auth/jwt.

redeem_urls.description: Every redeem address known for the space, redeem_url first, the platform address last.

reader_auth_provider.description: forumulate: the external_jwt reader provider (verified against this instance's JWKS), labelled `source: recommended`: Atlas cannot read what Forumulate holds, so this is not a read-back. The preferred order, atlas_byo first, is reader_auth_providers.

reader_auth_providers.description: forumulate: Atlas's recommended reader providers in order: atlas_byo, then the external_jwt method (verified against this instance's JWKS, no shared secret). Each entry carries `source: recommended`.

principal_claim.description: Where the value of the `principal` claim comes from (null = not carried). This is a source, not a claim name: point a receiver at principal_claim_name.

principal_claim_name.description: The name of the claim in the token that carries the principal (null = not carried). This is what a receiver such as Chatly reads (Chatly channel setting principalClaim).

ext_claim.description: Where the value of the `ext` claim comes from (null = not carried). A source, not a claim name.

ext_claim_name.description: The name of the claim in the token that carries your external id (null = not carried).

claims.description: The opt-in organization and metadata claims (all off by default).

extra_claim_names.description: The claim names the claims setting adds to a token (each only when it has a value), e.g. org_id, org_slug, org_role, plan.

issuer.description: The iss of every token (the instance issuer).

jwks_url.description: The JWKS that verifies the tokens.

token_schema.description: The JSON Schema of the token claims.

events_url.description: Where Atlas delivers user.updated, user.banned, user.unbanned, user.deleted and session.revoked (signed like any webhook). null = none.

events_url_default.description: True when events_url is the preset's default.

backchannel_logout_url.description: Where Atlas POSTs an OIDC Back-Channel Logout token on every session end. null = none.

backchannel_logout_source.description: Where the receiver comes from: set on the integration, the backchannel_logout_uri of the service's first-party OAuth client (logout tokens then carry that client_id as aud), or the preset's own path. null = no receiver.

backchannel_logout_client_id.description: With source oauth_client: the client whose backchannel_logout_uri is used.

oauth_client_id.description: The first-party OAuth client the service signs users in with, as set. null when not set (Atlas then looks for a first-party client tagged with provisioning metadata product=<integration id>).

verify_error_report_url.description: Informational: where the service documents its verify-error reporting.

cmp.description: A consent manager (any CMP) the hosted sign-in pages load from this integration when no cookie_consent is stored. The Cookie Munch preset brings its own; null = none.

site_id.description: The data-cbid / site id the script needs.

extra_origins.description: Extra https origins the CMP calls (CSP).

consent_api.description: The consent API the CMP exposes on the page, so the hosted pages read and record consent through it and not only through the banner. The Cookie Munch preset declares `window.__fdConsent`; null = none.

global.description: The `window` property holding the API (a plain identifier).

has_method.description: Method answering true | false | null (no decision yet). Default `has`.

request_method.description: Method that asks the visitor and records the answer, `(category, {reason, vendor}) → Promise<boolean>`. Absent = Atlas never asks.

category_map.description: Atlas category name → the CMP's own name, when they differ.

atlas_id_users.description: Also mint for Sign in with Atlas users who are not on this instance.

per_call_audience.description: Per-call audiences: getToken({ for, <param>: value }) mints a token whose aud is template with {<param>} filled in, when the value is the configured one, listed in allowed, or any_matching is on. Omitted on PUT = the preset default (its param, the configured value only); null = the integration mints for its configured audience only. A custom integration has none until it sets one.

param.description: The per-call parameter, e.g. cbid (cookiemunch), channel (chatly), org_id (forumulate, referalli), or your own for a custom integration (1-32 lowercase letters, digits or "_").

template.description: The audience with {<param>} in it once. Presets: always <preset>:{<param>} (leave it out on PUT). Custom: required, e.g. acme:{tenant}.

allowed.description: Further permitted values of the parameter (not whole audiences). The configured audience is always permitted.

any_matching.description: Any value of the format is permitted (1-128 letters, digits, ".", "_" or "-"; a custom integration also needs audience_format, which the whole audience must match). Default false.

default.description: GET only: true when this is the preset default.

atlas_id_issuer.description: The second issuer to trust when atlas_id_users is on.

metadata.description: Provisioning tags.

get.summary: One identity integration, with its health. For a preset or custom id that was never connected: enabled:false, connected:false. The integration id: a preset (chatly, forumulate, cookiemunch, referalli) or a custom integration id (2-40 lowercase letters, digits, "_" or "-", starting with a letter).

schema.description: enabled:false, connected:false (and nothing else) when the integration was never connected. A preset answers object <preset>_integration (chatly_integration, …) with its own fields; a custom integration answers object integration.

added_origins.description: PUT only: the origins this write added to allowed_origins from the redirect URIs of the OAuth client the service signs users in with. [] when none were missing.

warnings.description: PUT only (forumulate; [] otherwise): what already replaces the Atlas reader button in Forumulate, read from each configured space's public reader sign-in settings (up to 5 spaces). existing_sign_in_url_overrides: an org- or space-level signInUrl sends readers to that page instead of showing any sign-in button (sign_in_url, space_ids). atlas_reader_provider_missing: the spaces offer other providers and not the Atlas one. Report only, unless the PUT sent replace_existing with a Forumulate API key: then Atlas makes the change, and replace_failed says why it could not (the integration is saved either way). A space Atlas cannot read adds nothing. Never blocks the save.

events_secret_stored.description: PUT with forumulate_api_key (forumulate, default events_url) only: the Atlas reader providers in Forumulate that received the events signing secret as webhookSecret. The secret itself is never in this answer. null when it could not be stored (see the events_secret_not_stored warning).

channel.description: PUT with chatly_api_key (chatly): the channel that received the events signing secret.

replaced.description: PUT with replace_existing (forumulate) only: what Atlas changed in Forumulate's org reader sign-in registry. null when it could not (see the replace_failed warning).

sign_in_url_cleared.description: The org-level signInUrl that was cleared, or null when none was set.

providers_removed.description: The reader providers removed: every one that is not the Atlas provider.

audience.description: The aud of every token minted for it.

audience_format.description: Custom only: the regular expression the audience must match.

template.description: chatly: the name getToken({ template: 'chatly' }) (deprecated alias) uses.

identity_verification.description: chatly: what the channel's identity verification needs (no shared secret).

spaces.description: forumulate: the connected spaces and where a reader redeems a token. Reader cookies are host-only, so the redeem must happen on the host the reader reads.

redeem_url.description: Where the reader's browser redeems the token: the redeem_url you gave, else the space's primary reader address (its site or custom domain, the first of its readerEndpoints in Forumulate, read when you send forumulate_api_key), else the platform address https://forumulate.com/api/public/orgs/<org>/spaces/<id>/reader-auth/jwt.

redeem_urls.description: Every redeem address known for the space, redeem_url first, the platform address last.

reader_auth_provider.description: forumulate: the external_jwt reader provider (verified against this instance's JWKS), labelled `source: recommended`: Atlas cannot read what Forumulate holds, so this is not a read-back. The preferred order, atlas_byo first, is reader_auth_providers.

reader_auth_providers.description: forumulate: Atlas's recommended reader providers in order: atlas_byo, then the external_jwt method (verified against this instance's JWKS, no shared secret). Each entry carries `source: recommended`.

principal_claim.description: Where the value of the `principal` claim comes from (null = not carried). This is a source, not a claim name: point a receiver at principal_claim_name.

principal_claim_name.description: The name of the claim in the token that carries the principal (null = not carried). This is what a receiver such as Chatly reads (Chatly channel setting principalClaim).

ext_claim.description: Where the value of the `ext` claim comes from (null = not carried). A source, not a claim name.

ext_claim_name.description: The name of the claim in the token that carries your external id (null = not carried).

claims.description: The opt-in organization and metadata claims (all off by default).

extra_claim_names.description: The claim names the claims setting adds to a token (each only when it has a value), e.g. org_id, org_slug, org_role, plan.

issuer.description: The iss of every token (the instance issuer).

jwks_url.description: The JWKS that verifies the tokens.

token_schema.description: The JSON Schema of the token claims.

events_url.description: Where Atlas delivers user.updated, user.banned, user.unbanned, user.deleted and session.revoked (signed like any webhook). null = none.

events_url_default.description: True when events_url is the preset's default.

backchannel_logout_url.description: Where Atlas POSTs an OIDC Back-Channel Logout token on every session end. null = none.

backchannel_logout_source.description: Where the receiver comes from: set on the integration, the backchannel_logout_uri of the service's first-party OAuth client (logout tokens then carry that client_id as aud), or the preset's own path. null = no receiver.

backchannel_logout_client_id.description: With source oauth_client: the client whose backchannel_logout_uri is used.

oauth_client_id.description: The first-party OAuth client the service signs users in with, as set. null when not set (Atlas then looks for a first-party client tagged with provisioning metadata product=<integration id>).

verify_error_report_url.description: Informational: where the service documents its verify-error reporting.

put.summary: Connect (or replace) an identity integration: any service that verifies a user with a JWT. getToken({ for: '<id>' }) then mints a token of at most 120 s with aud = audience, sub (the Atlas user id), ext (external_id), principal (the branding audience the user signed in under), sid, email, email_verified, name and locale, verifiable against the instance JWKS. Atlas also delivers user.updated / user.banned / user.unbanned / user.deleted / session.revoked to events_url and an OIDC Back-Channel Logout token to backchannel_logout_url on every session end. ?dry_run=true validates in full and answers { object: 'dry_run', changes, would_return } without saving. Also accepts metadata tags and external_ref. The OAuth client the service signs users in with (oauth_client_id, else the client tagged product=<integration id>) gets its https redirect-URI origins added to allowed_origins (append only, recorded in the config changelog); the response lists them in added_origins. For forumulate, warnings says when Forumulate already sends readers elsewhere (existing_sign_in_url_overrides: an org-level signInUrl; atlas_reader_provider_missing), read from its public reader sign-in settings. With replace_existing: true and forumulate_api_key (a Forumulate org admin's API key, used for this call only and never stored) Atlas clears the org-level signInUrl and removes every non-Atlas reader provider in Forumulate, and answers replaced. forumulate_api_key alone also reads each space's reader addresses, so spaces[].redeem_url is on the host its readers read. The integration id: a preset (chatly, forumulate, cookiemunch, referalli) or a custom integration id (2-40 lowercase letters, digits, "_" or "-", starting with a letter).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique key per intended write (16 to 128 characters recommended, e.g. a UUID). A retry with the same key and the same request replays the first response for 24 hours with Idempotent-Replay: true; the same key with a different request is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, and while the first is still running a retry is 409 too. A failed write (4xx/5xx) does not consume the key. A dry run never uses it.

schema.description: Replaces the whole connection. { "enabled": true|false } alone switches a saved connection on or off and keeps the rest. Presets: audience is "<preset>:<id>" (chatly also accepts { channel }, forumulate { org_id, spaces }). Custom integrations: name and audience are required.

enabled.description: Default true.

replace_existing.description: forumulate only: also make the Atlas button the org's reader sign-in in Forumulate (clear the org-level signInUrl, remove every non-Atlas reader provider). Needs forumulate_api_key. Not applied in a dry run.

forumulate_api_key.description: forumulate only: an API key with Forumulate's admin scope, used for this call only and never stored. Atlas reads each connected space's reader addresses with it (so spaces[].redeem_url is on the space's own host) stores the events signing secret as webhookSecret on the org's Atlas reader provider (when events_url is the default) and, with replace_existing, replaces the reader sign-in. A failed read saves the integration anyway and adds a reader_addresses_unread warning; a failed secret write adds events_secret_not_stored. Not used in a dry run.

chatly_api_key.description: chatly only: a Chatly API key with the channels:write permission, used for this call only and never stored. Atlas stores the events signing secret with it as the channel's identityVerification.eventsSecret (when events_url is the default), so no manual reveal is needed. A failed write saves the integration anyway and adds an events_secret_not_stored warning with the exact call. Not used in a dry run.

audience.description: chatly:<channel> | forumulate:<org> | cookiemunch:<cbid> | referalli:<org> | any value for a custom integration.

name.description: Custom only (required): the display name.

role.description: Custom only.

audience_format.description: Custom only: a regular expression the audience must match (anchored).

claims.description: Opt-in claims, resolved at every mint. org: org_id and org_slug of the session's active organization; org_role: the user's role key there (both only while the user is a member); public_metadata: up to 10 keys copied to top-level claims, from the active organization's public_metadata, else the user's. A key Atlas sets itself (email, sub, org_id, ...) is refused. context: an allow-list of per-mint claims, { <claim name>: [<allowed values>] } (up to 10 names, 50 values each); a getToken call may send context: { <name>: <value> } and the pair is signed into that token. Omitted or null = none.

events_url.description: https; null = no event deliveries. Omitted = the preset's default.

backchannel_logout_url.description: https; null = none. Omitted = the backchannel_logout_uri of the service's first-party OAuth client when it has one, else the preset's default.

oauth_client_id.description: The client_id of the first-party OAuth client the service signs users in with. While backchannel_logout_url is omitted, that client's backchannel_logout_uri becomes the receiver (kept in step when the client changes). Omitted = the first-party client tagged with provisioning metadata product=<integration id>; null = none.

post.summary: Re-send what the integration's event receiver never got: every event since `since` with no successful delivery, including events recorded while the receiver was disabled. Each goes out signed and addressed as of now, with its original event id. A failed event already waiting on its retry schedule (for example after the receiver refused it) is not sent twice: its retry is moved to now (`retries_brought_forward`), so calling this again after fixing the receiver re-sends it at once. Switches a disabled receiver back on. At most 1,000 events per call (`has_more` + `next_since` to continue). Delivered events are never re-sent, including with two calls at once and no Idempotency-Key. 409 when `since` is older than the 90-day event retention; past the 30-day delivery log Atlas cannot tell what was delivered, so an older `since` can re-send delivered events. 404 when the integration has no event receiver. Honours Idempotency-Key.

A failed write (4xx/5xx) does not consume the key. A dry run never uses it.

post.summary: Rotate the signing secret of the integration's event receiver. The new secret is revealed exactly once. By default (`overlap_seconds` 0) the old secret stops signing at once. With `overlap_seconds` (at most 604800 = 7 days) every delivery carries two signatures in `Atlas-Signature` (`v1,<new> v1,<old>`, the new one first), so the service verifies with either secret while it deploys the new one; after that only the new secret signs. `previous_secret_expires_at` says when the old secret stops signing (epoch ms), or null when it already has. Audited as integration.<id>.events_secret_rotated. 404 when the integration has no event receiver.
