message.description: Human-readable. On the Frontend API (/v1/client/...) it is written in the request language: ?locale=, else a top-level "locale" body field, else Accept-Language (en, es, fr, de, pt-BR, ja, nl, ar, he, fa, hi, zh-Hans, zh-Hant, ko, it, pl, tr, ru, sv, id, vi, th; anything else is English). Do not branch on it.

reason.description: Frontend API sign-in, sign-up, verification and reset errors: a stable, finer-grained reason than code (e.g. form_password_incorrect vs form_code_incorrect under VERIFICATION_FAILED). Safe to branch on and to key your own translations by. form_identifier_not_found is reserved: an unknown identifier is reported exactly like a wrong password (form_password_incorrect), so these flows never reveal whether an account exists.

did_you_mean.description: ROUTE_NOT_FOUND only: the closest documented paths (an alias table of common guesses, then edit distance).

allowed_methods.description: ROUTE_NOT_FOUND only: the path exists, but only for these methods.

principalMatched.description: Present when atlas.principal was sent: true when the matched account signed in as that principal, false when it signed in only as others, null when it never signed in under any principal.

canary.description: Present (true) when the subject is a conformance canary: a synthetic person, never backed by real data.

requestedType.description: The word the caller sent (an alias, or the canonical one).

canary.description: Present (true) on a conformance canary request: synthetic, never backed by real data.

result.description: Single-request reads only, once done. Access: `{ format: "inline", body, bytes, sha256 }`. Erasure: `{ erased_at, personal_data_scrubbed_at }`.

signing_secret.description: Only on the write that minted it.

completion_webhook_secret.description: Only on the write that created the endpoint. The same format as every webhook endpoint signing secret (atlas_<env>_whsec_…; secrets issued earlier read whsec_…). The whole string, prefix included, is the HMAC key.

preset.description: The orchestrator preset (null before any connect).

connected.description: The consent manager is on, the orchestrator and its completion webhook are set, and the executor key is live.

dsr_webhook.description: The managed completion webhook endpoint (`webhook_endpoint_id`, `url`, `active`, `enabled_events`). Connect answers add `source` and `secret_destination`.

source.description: Connect only: where the url came from this call: read from the Cookie Munch executor connection (executor_connection_id), sent as completion_webhook_url, or kept from an earlier connect.

secret_destination.description: Connect only, with executor_connection_id: where the completion webhook's signing secret must be set at Cookie Munch. Atlas does not send it there (`sent: false`).

connection_url.description: The connection at Cookie Munch (PATCH it with {"webhookSecret": …}).

secret.description: Which field of this answer holds the secret (privacy_orchestrator.completion_webhook_secret), or null when the endpoint already existed and its secret is not shown again.

executor_key.description: The secret key minted for the orchestrator (the POST /v1/secret_keys shape). `secret` only on the connect that minted it.

action.description: Connect answers only: what this call did with the key. `upgraded`: requested scopes the key lacked were added (secret unchanged); `adopted`: the key named by `key.id` is now the managed one.

secret.description: Only on the connect that minted it. Paste it into the orchestrator's Atlas connection.

idempotent_replay.description: Connect only: true when this key already existed.

warnings.description: Connect only: the consent-manager site check (cmp_site_unknown, cmp_site_domain_mismatch, cmp_site_check_unavailable) and the executor key (executor_key_minted, executor_key_upgraded). Never fails the call.

DesignAsset.description: An uploaded design image. Use asset_id in a design (logo.assetId, background.image.assetId, ...). Stored re-encoded as WebP, scaled to fit 2560 px (1024 px for a logo).

url.description: Where Atlas serves the stored image.

dominant_color.description: #rrggbb for an opaque image, else null.

AtlasDesign.description: A structured sign-in page design: OVERRIDES on top of a preset (every field optional; unset fields come from the preset, then the defaults). Unknown keys are refused. Colours are #RRGGBB; images are uploaded design asset ids (dasset_…), never URLs; fonts are ids from GET /v1/design/catalog. There is no field for raw CSS or HTML.

AtlasDesignPatch.description: A partial design update: nested objects merge, arrays (gradient stops) and values replace, and null removes a setting (falling back to the preset). The merged result is validated as a whole.

ResolvedDesign.description: The fully-resolved design every surface renders (defaults ← preset ← overrides): the same shape as AtlasDesign with every field present.

DesignWarning.description: A contrast warning (advice, never a refusal): a text/background pair below WCAG AA 4.5:1.

path.description: The setting to change, e.g. palette.primaryInk.

organization_id.description: Organization designs only.

design.description: The stored overrides ({} when nothing is stored).

legacy.description: True when nothing is stored and the page is drawn from the older branding settings.

legacy_design.description: When legacy is true: the design derived from the older branding settings (a good starting point for an editor). Null otherwise.

brand.description: Instance designs: the imported brand document layer (null when none). It sits under the stored design.

precedence.description: Instance designs: the layers, lowest first (preset < brand < design < audience). A later layer wins each field it sets.

source.description: Where the layer comes from (the preset id, the brand URL or "inline", "instance"), null when the layer is empty.

sources.description: Instance designs: for each field set by the brand or the design (dotted path, e.g. palette.primary), which layer it comes from. Fields not listed come from the preset.

ignored.description: After a brand import only: the tokens that were not applied, with the reason.

url.description: The brand_url it was fetched from (null when sent inline).

design.description: The design overrides the brand document mapped to.

token.description: e.g. color.accent

to.description: The design field it set, e.g. palette.primary

token.description: The token path in the brand document, e.g. color.sparkle.

scope.description: The selector the CSS is scoped to: ".atlas-root".

css.description: CSS custom properties (--atlas-*) for the scope, including light/dark blocks.

data_attributes.description: Attributes to set on the scoped element (data-atlas-layout, data-atlas-card, …).

font_stylesheets.description: Absolute URLs of the self-hosted font stylesheets to link.

html.description: The sign-in page rendered with the draft design (inert: for a sandboxed preview frame).

dangerouslyReportSkippedEmailsAsVerified.description: DANGEROUS. When true, addresses that skipped proof because requireEmailVerification was false are reported as verified again in users, tokens, webhooks and exports (the old behaviour). Anyone can then sign up as any address and present a verified claim. Atlas still treats those addresses as unproven when linking social sign-ins, auto-joining organizations and accepting invitations. Preflight reports email_verified_unproven while this is on.

audiences.description: The audiences a token may be minted for, and the scopes allowed for each. Anything else is refused.

exchangeClientIds.description: OAuth client ids of confidential clients that may use the token-exchange grant for delegation tokens. Empty means none.

delegationTokens.description: Server-minted delegation tokens (POST /v1/users/{id}/delegation_tokens and the token-exchange grant). Off by default.

externalJwt.description: Trust JWTs minted by an EXTERNAL issuer as a sign-in credential (e.g. a legacy IdP or your own token service). The linked identity is stored under provider ext_jwt:<id>.

issuerAliases.description: Previous issuers of this instance that verification should still accept, for a host or mount move made before Atlas recorded it. Listed in discovery as atlas_previous_issuers and accepted by @atlasauth/backend with previousIssuers "discovery". At most 10; acceptedUntil at most a year ahead.

breachCheckOnSignIn.description: Re-check the password against known breaches at each sign-in: flag (audit only), force_reset, or block.

rejectCommonPasswords.description: Refuse any of the 10,000 most common passwords (bundled list, no network call).

requireEmailVerification.description: Whether a password sign-up must prove the address with an emailed code before it completes. When false the sign-up completes at once, but the address stays unverified (verified, verification.status and email_verified report false) until the user proves it later.

serviceProviders.description: The SPs Atlas issues signed assertions to.

samlIdp.description: Atlas AS a SAML IdP — "Sign in with Atlas" over SAML for a downstream Service Provider (direct SAML; no OIDC/atlas_byo needed).

absoluteMs.description: Absolute session lifetime in ms. At most 90 days; 365 days while longLived is on.

cookieDomain.description: Explicit Domain for the session cookies, for example ".example.com". Needed by a path-mounted instance, where cookies are otherwise host-only. It must cover your sign-in host and can never be a public suffix or Atlas's own domain; an invalid value is refused on write. Default null.

csrfCookie.description: Set a readable __atlas_csrf cookie with each session token: a signed token tied to the session, replaced whenever the session token is. Verify it in your backend with the instance JWKS. Default false.

includeEmailClaim.description: Add email/name to the session JWT.

includeResourceRoleClaims.description: Add a res claim with the user direct resource role assignments (capped; resource_claims_truncated when over the cap).

jwtTtlSeconds.description: Lifetime of the session token (the __session JWT) in seconds, 30 to 900, default 60. A shorter lifetime means faster revocation: a signed-out or banned user stops being accepted by your backend sooner. A longer lifetime means fewer lapses in throttled background tabs, where the browser delays the timer that renews the token.

longLived.description: Long first-party sessions: raises the absoluteMs ceiling from 90 to 365 days. Needs refreshRotation (refused while it is off). Organization caps still only shorten a session.

refreshGraceSeconds.description: Seconds after a refresh token rotates during which presenting the previous one returns the same new token instead of ending the session. 0 to 30, default 30.

signUpMode.description: public: anyone may sign up. waitlist: unknown addresses join a waitlist (403 WAITLISTED) until approved. restricted: invite-only — only an address with a pending, unexpired invitation (POST /v1/invitations or an organization invitation) or an approved waitlist entry may sign up (403 SIGN_UP_RESTRICTED otherwise).

username.description: Username as a login identifier.

strategies.description: Which first-factor sign-in methods are enabled.

strictRequestBodies.description: Strict writes for this instance's secret keys: a Backend API write that carries a body field the endpoint does not know is refused with 422 UNKNOWN_FIELD instead of being accepted and ignored. true for every instance created from 2026-10 on; older instances stay false (lenient: the ignored fields are named in the Atlas-Unknown-Fields response header) until set. One request overrides it with the Atlas-Strict: true | false header. Fields that look writable and have their own call (verified on an email address, banned, …) are refused with 422 READ_ONLY_FIELD either way; echoed id, object, created_at and updated_at are 422 READ_ONLY_FIELD only when strict.

verification.description: Per-method code/link TTLs, lengths and resend limits.

branding.description: On PATCH /v1/instance only branding.audiences is applied (per-audience hosted-page branding, merged per hint; see PATCH /v1/branding for the shape). Every other branding field is written with PATCH /v1/branding.

audiences.description: Audience hint ([a-z0-9_-]{1,32}) → { heading, subheading, logoUrl, primaryColor }, or null to delete that audience.

delegationTokens.description: Server-minted delegation tokens (POST /v1/users/{id}/delegation_tokens and the token-exchange grant). Off by default.

externalJwt.description: Trust JWTs minted by an EXTERNAL issuer as a sign-in credential (e.g. a legacy IdP or your own token service). The linked identity is stored under provider ext_jwt:<id>.

issuerAliases.description: Previous issuers of this instance that verification should still accept, for a host or mount move made before Atlas recorded it. Listed in discovery as atlas_previous_issuers and accepted by @atlasauth/backend with previousIssuers "discovery". At most 10; acceptedUntil at most a year ahead.

breachCheckOnSignIn.description: Re-check the password against known breaches at each sign-in: flag (audit only), force_reset, or block.

rejectCommonPasswords.description: Refuse any of the 10,000 most common passwords (bundled list, no network call).

requireEmailVerification.description: Whether a password sign-up must prove the address with an emailed code before it completes. When false the sign-up completes at once, but the address stays unverified (verified, verification.status and email_verified report false) until the user proves it later.

serviceProviders.description: The SPs Atlas issues signed assertions to.

samlIdp.description: Atlas AS a SAML IdP — "Sign in with Atlas" over SAML for a downstream Service Provider (direct SAML; no OIDC/atlas_byo needed).

absoluteMs.description: Absolute session lifetime in ms. At most 90 days; 365 days while longLived is on.

cookieDomain.description: Explicit Domain for the session cookies, for example ".example.com". Needed by a path-mounted instance, where cookies are otherwise host-only. It must cover your sign-in host and can never be a public suffix or Atlas's own domain; an invalid value is refused on write. Default null.

csrfCookie.description: Set a readable __atlas_csrf cookie with each session token: a signed token tied to the session, replaced whenever the session token is. Verify it in your backend with the instance JWKS. Default false.

includeEmailClaim.description: Add email/name to the session JWT.

includeResourceRoleClaims.description: Add a res claim with the user direct resource role assignments (capped; resource_claims_truncated when over the cap).

jwtTtlSeconds.description: Lifetime of the session token (the __session JWT) in seconds, 30 to 900, default 60. A shorter lifetime means faster revocation: a signed-out or banned user stops being accepted by your backend sooner. A longer lifetime means fewer lapses in throttled background tabs, where the browser delays the timer that renews the token.

longLived.description: Long first-party sessions: raises the absoluteMs ceiling from 90 to 365 days. Needs refreshRotation (refused while it is off). Organization caps still only shorten a session.

refreshGraceSeconds.description: Seconds after a refresh token rotates during which presenting the previous one returns the same new token instead of ending the session. 0 to 30, default 30.

signUpMode.description: public: anyone may sign up. waitlist: unknown addresses join a waitlist (403 WAITLISTED) until approved. restricted: invite-only — only an address with a pending, unexpired invitation (POST /v1/invitations or an organization invitation) or an approved waitlist entry may sign up (403 SIGN_UP_RESTRICTED otherwise).

username.description: Username as a login identifier.

strategies.description: Which first-factor sign-in methods are enabled.

strictRequestBodies.description: Strict writes for this instance's secret keys: a Backend API write that carries a body field the endpoint does not know is refused with 422 UNKNOWN_FIELD instead of being accepted and ignored. true for every instance created from 2026-10 on; older instances stay false (lenient: the ignored fields are named in the Atlas-Unknown-Fields response header) until set. One request overrides it with the Atlas-Strict: true | false header. Fields that look writable and have their own call (verified on an email address, banned, …) are refused with 422 READ_ONLY_FIELD either way; echoed id, object, created_at and updated_at are 422 READ_ONLY_FIELD only when strict.

verification.description: Per-method code/link TTLs, lengths and resend limits.

branding.description: On PATCH /v1/instance only branding.audiences is applied (per-audience hosted-page branding, merged per hint; see PATCH /v1/branding for the shape). Every other branding field is written with PATCH /v1/branding.

audiences.description: Audience hint ([a-z0-9_-]{1,32}) → { heading, subheading, logoUrl, primaryColor }, or null to delete that audience.

AuthConfigPatch.description: A partial auth_config patch for PATCH /v1/instance: send only the sections and fields you change; omitted siblings are kept. Validated: an unknown value returns 422 naming the field. The full resolved shape is GET /v1/instance auth_config_resolved.

status.description: verified only when the address was proven (an emailed code or link, a provider that vouches for it, or your backend). An address that signed up while requireEmailVerification was false is unverified.

strategy.description: How the address was verified: email_code, email_link, oauth, admin, import, scim, lti; skipped when it signed up without proof (held for sign-in, reported unverified); null when not verified.

verified.description: Same as verification.status === "verified": the address was proven.

created_at.description: When the number was added (epoch ms).

User.description: A user as the Backend API serializes it. Never includes private/unsafe metadata (those are write-only here).

sign_in.description: false for a link-only account added with POST /v1/users/{id}/external_accounts: it is shown and delivered but can never sign anyone in.

primary_email.description: The primary address as a flat string; null until a verified primary exists.

external_id.description: The relying party's own id for this user, if set/imported.

password_enabled.description: Whether the account has a usable password (never the hash).

has_passkey.description: Whether the user holds at least one passkey.

required_factors.description: Factor classes this user must always use (POL-04); empty = none.

is_anonymous.description: Whether this identity is still an anonymous guest.

sandbox.description: A sandbox user: set at creation, never changed. Nothing is ever sent to it (email, SMS, push, voice, WhatsApp), it is not counted as a monthly active user or billed, and its tokens carry `env: sandbox`.

status.description: One account state, the same value as the ID token's account_status: banned (an active ban; deactivation by SCIM, directory sync or a workflow is a ban), suspended (a lock, suspension directive or sign-in lockout is in force), else active.

sessions_revoked_at.description: Epoch-ms when ALL of the user's sessions last ended together (BAPI revoke-all, dashboard revoke-all, sign out everywhere, a password change or reset that revokes all, a ban or lock, a compromise signal); null = never. Treat any token issued before it as ended. Also the `user.sessions_revoked` event.

version.description: Strictly increases with every change to the user. Webhook payloads carry the same value: apply an update only if its version is higher than the one you hold.

referral.description: How the user arrived through a referral program (referral attribution on). Null only when the user was never reported to the referral platform; otherwise `status` says where attribution stands (`pending` until the platform answers). Present on read, list, create and update responses.

referral_code.description: The user's own referral code: set once the referral platform enrolled the user as a partner (its answer carried a code) or an admin set one (PATCH /v1/users/{id} referral_code). null when the user is not enrolled, referrals are off, or the code was cleared.

warnings.description: PATCH answers only, when there is something to know: e.g. the referral platform has not confirmed a new referral_code yet (always so in a dry run, which does not ask it).

referral_link.description: The user's own share link: the link the referral platform returned for the partner, else the referral settings' link_template with {code} replaced by the URL-encoded referral_code. null while there is no referral_code, or no platform link and no link_template.

phone_numbers.description: Every phone number of the user. Present on read, list, update and user webhooks.

primary_phone_number.description: The primary phone number (E.164): the one the person made primary, else their oldest verified number; null when none.

phone_number_verified.description: True only when the primary phone number was proven.

external_accounts.description: Every linked provider identity, however it was linked (a sign-in, a connect flow, identities on create, a bulk import or identities/import); the same set GET /v1/users/{id}/identities lists. Present on read, list, create, update and password responses.

UserExternalAccount.description: A provider identity linked to the user. Tokens and the raw provider profile are never included.

provider_email.description: The provider's address at the last sign-in or import (a snapshot, not proof of ownership).

email_verified.description: Whether the provider (or the import) said that address is verified.

image_url.description: The provider's avatar for this identity.

UserReferral.description: A user's inbound referral: where attribution stands and, once attributed, who referred them.

status.description: Where attribution stands: pending (the platform has not answered yet), attributed, none (not referred), failed, held or flagged.

partner_id.description: The platform's id for the referring partner.

partner_external_ref.description: The referrer as the platform knows them (your external_id for that user, or their Atlas id).

referrer_user_id.description: The referrer's Atlas user id, when they are a user of this instance.

matched_via.description: How the platform matched the referral, e.g. code, click, coupon.

referral_status.description: The platform's own status for the referral (e.g. active).

notes.description: The platform's reasoning notes for its answer.

risk_level.description: The risk level assessed at sign-up, when one was.

flagged.description: An admin marked the referral fraudulent.

UserReferralFlag.description: A user's referral after an admin flagged it as fraudulent.

status.description: flagged after this call.

risk_level.description: The risk level assessed at sign-up, when one was.

ReferralSecuritySettings.description: The security part of the referral settings (the `security` object of GET/PATCH /v1/instance/referrals). Referred sign-ups get stronger bot protection, and the referral platform receives a risk verdict with each sign-up.

challenge_referred_signups.description: always (default): a sign-up carrying a referral code must pass the bot challenge, even where the captcha is otherwise off. inherit: the instance captcha policy decides. With no working captcha, always behaves as inherit and preflight reports referrals_without_bot_protection.

on_high_risk.description: flag (default): report the sign-up with its risk. strip: report it as not referred, with rejected.reason. hold: report nothing until the email is proven, then re-assess.

hold_until_email_verified.description: Hold every referred sign-up until the email is proven. Default false.

max_referred_signups_per_ip_hour.description: Referred sign-ups per code from one IP network (/24 or /48) or one device per hour before ip_velocity / device_velocity is raised. Default 5.

ReferralRisk.description: The risk verdict sent with a sign-up to the referral platform (camelCase on the referral protocol).

UserState.description: A user's portable state (progression / tier / flair / entitlements / directives / roles).

tier.description: From public_metadata.tier (any JSON value the integrator stored); present only when set.

flair.description: From public_metadata.flair (any JSON value the integrator stored); present only when set.

suspended_until.description: ISO 8601; present only when a suspension was imposed.

reason.description: Present only when provided.

sessions_revoked.description: Live sessions revoked by imposing the directive.

Organization.description: An organization. private_metadata is backend-only and never serialized here.

created_by.description: The user seated at creation; null for an organization your backend created with no creator.

external_id.description: Your own id for this customer; unique per instance.

role_mappings.description: Role key → your product's name for it (e.g. {"org:admin": "owner"}); a member's mapped name rides in the org_role_mapped token claim.

owner_invitation.description: On create with owner_email only: the invitation sent to that address.

role_source.description: Who manages the role: `scim`, `sso:<connection id>` or `ldap:<connection id>` (the identity provider's groups or roles keep it in step), `directory_sync`, `manual` (set through the API or dashboard; no directory changes it), or null (joined by invitation, or before sources were recorded).

public_metadata.description: Readable by the application; set from the invitation on accept or with PATCH.

private_metadata.description: Backend only: never in a token, a webhook or a client response.

permissions.description: Permissions granted to this member on top of the role; added to org_permissions in the session token.

allowed_sign_in_methods.description: Sign-in methods whose sessions mint with this organization's claims, e.g. ["passkey", "oauth:google"]. Null = any method. A session signed in another way mints without this organization's claims.

Invitation.description: An instance-level invitation (not scoped to an organization).

delivery.description: `email`: your app sends it from organizationInvitation.created, or Atlas mails it when organizations.invitationEmail is "atlas". `link`: nothing is sent; the accept link is the delivery.

accept_by.description: Who may accept by link: `link` (whoever holds it, signed in) or `verified_email`. Null = the instance setting organizations.invitationAccept.

public_metadata.description: Copied to the membership on accept.

private_metadata.description: Copied to the membership on accept; backend only.

permissions.description: Granted on top of the role when the invitation is accepted.

allowed_sign_in_methods.description: Copied to the membership on accept. Null = any method.

accept_token.description: Link delivery only, on create and resend, shown once: the single-use token. Only its SHA-256 is stored.

accept_url.description: Link delivery only, shown once: redirect_url with the token appended as ?invitation_token=. Null when no redirect_url was given.

email_sent.description: Only with organizations.invitationEmail "atlas" on an email invitation: whether Atlas mailed it. false = no email provider could deliver (or it refused); the invitation still exists and a resend tries again.

accepted_email_address.description: The verified address of the user who accepted, when it differs from `email`.

visibility.description: internal roles are backend-assigned only and hidden from org-admin UIs.

organization_id.description: Set on a per-organization custom role; null for an instance-wide role.

implies.description: Permission keys held along with this one, transitively (cycle-safe).

status.description: pending until a check runs; failed after a DNS or well-known check that did not find the token (re-check any time); verified once proven.

verification_methods.description: Every way to prove the domain.

well_known.description: No DNS access: serve `body` as the whole response (200, text/plain) at `url`. Redirects are not followed.

email.description: A code mailed to one of `addresses` through your own email provider (POST …/verification_email).

verification_method.description: How the domain was verified; null while unverified.

idle_expires_at.description: Epoch ms when the session ends from inactivity unless there is activity first (same value as abandon_at). Slides on activity and on POST /v1/sessions/{id}/touch; never past expire_at.

custom_data.description: Custom per-session data the app attached (PUT/PATCH /v1/sessions/{id}/custom_data, or a post_login Action). Null when none.

sign_in_method.description: How the session was signed in: the first-factor strategy (password, email_code, email_link, phone_code, passkey, oauth, sso, saml, ticket, ...). Null for a session created before this was recorded.

provider.description: The social provider id when sign_in_method is oauth; otherwise null.

native_client.description: Present for a native app session: kind unregistered, development or registered, the native app id when one was named, and binding device_key when its refresh token is bound to a key the device holds.

device_label.description: Present for an unregistered or development native session: "Unregistered app on <device>" or "Development app on <device>".

amr.description: The authentication methods proven at sign-in (RFC 8176, e.g. pwd, otp, webauthn, ext, mfa); updated by a step-up. Null for a session created before this was recorded.

user_agent.description: The user agent of the device that signed in. Null when none was sent.

ip_address.description: The client IP at sign-in (through a path mount: the browser IP your proxy asserted with its proxy secret). Dropped 30 days after the session ends.

location.description: Coarse location of the sign-in, when a geo source resolved one.

risk.description: Advisory risk assessment. Null = not assessed (never "safe"). Atlas decides nothing from it.

revoked_at.description: Epoch ms when the session was ended (null while active, or when it simply ran out).

revoked_reason.description: Why the session was ended, e.g. signed_out, revoked_by_api, token_reuse (a refresh token was presented after it had been replaced and its grace window had passed). Null while active.

SessionTouch.description: The session after a keep-alive touch.

custom_data.description: Custom per-session data the app attached (PUT/PATCH /v1/sessions/{id}/custom_data, or a post_login Action). Null when none.

extended.description: true when this touch moved the inactivity window; false when a touch within the last 60 seconds already did (the current state is returned unchanged).

type.description: The key type segment (e.g. `sk`), or null for an untyped key.

scopes.description: Tenant-defined scopes embedded into tokens minted from this key.

constraints.description: Arbitrary constraint claims (e.g. desk_ids, cwd, run_as) embedded into minted tokens.

max_token_lifetime_seconds.description: Org-policy ceiling (seconds) on the lifetime of a token minted from this key.

public_key.description: Registered SPKI PEM public key for proof-of-possession, or null for a bearer key.

public_key_jkt.description: RFC 7638 JWK thumbprint of public_key — the cnf.jkt minted tokens carry (a key_pair key's tokens carry none).

credential.description: `secret`: a shared `ak_` secret. `key_pair`: no secret exists; the holder signs short-lived JWT assertions with a private key Atlas never holds, and `public_key` verifies them.

audience.description: key_pair only: the `aud` an assertion must carry (default: the instance id). Null for a secret key.

key_id.description: The key id (the same as `id`): the `kid` header and `iss` claim of an assertion.

limits.description: Per-key spend caps, metered with POST /v1/api_keys/{id}/usage. null when the key has none.

usage.description: Each cap with its current-window usage (empty when the key has no caps).

enabled.description: A disabled key fails verify and cannot mint tokens until re-enabled; it is not revoked.

rate_limit.description: Per-key verify rate limit: at most max successful verifies per window_seconds. null = none.

remaining.description: Uses left; each successful verify spends one. null = unlimited.

allowed_ips.description: IPv4/IPv6 addresses or CIDR ranges the key may be used from. null = any caller. Verify then needs the end caller client_ip.

revoked_reason.description: Why the key was revoked when a person did not: `membership_ended` (a key bound to an organization lost that membership), `creator_departed` (an organization key whose creator left or lost the manage-keys permission), `organization_deleted`.

organization_id.description: The organization a USER key is bound to (null = unbound). Verify and token mints resolve the current membership, and the key ends with it.

created_by_user_id.description: The member who created an ORGANIZATION key, when recorded.

end_reason.description: Why the key ended, always answered once it has: the stored `revoked_reason`, else `revoked_by_api` (a secret key or person revoked it) or `revoked_by_admin` (a dashboard user did); `signed_out_everywhere` for a key that died with the sign-out. Null while live.

ended_at.description: Epoch ms the key ended (the same value as `revoked_at`).

type.description: api_key, user, system, scim or sso.

revoked_by.description: Who revoked the key. Null while live and for keys revoked before this was recorded.

dies_with.description: `sign_out_everywhere`: the key is revoked when its user subject signs out everywhere. Null = independent of sessions.

metadata.description: The same object as `claims`, under the name most integrators use: your own vocabulary (scopes, team, label), echoed back on verify.

period.description: `request` caps a single debit; `second`/`minute` are fixed rate windows aligned to the UTC clock (e.g. 600 requests per minute); `day`/`month` are UTC calendar windows; `total` never resets.

used.description: Used in the current window (always 0 for a per-request cap).

remaining.description: amount − used, never below 0 (the cap itself for a per-request cap).

window_start.description: Epoch ms the current window started (UTC); null for a per-request cap.

resets_at.description: Epoch ms the current window ends (UTC); null for per-request and total caps.
Epoch ms the window ends; null for total.

allowed.description: true when the debit was recorded; false when it would exceed a cap (nothing was recorded).

code.description: Present only when allowed is false.

exceeded.description: The caps that refused the debit (empty when allowed).

usage.description: Every cap on the key after this call, with remaining.

counters.description: The debited unit's day, month and total counters after this call.

idempotent_replay.description: true when this is the stored outcome of an earlier call with the same idempotency_key (nothing was counted again).

counters.description: Current-window counters for every unit the key has been debited in, capped or not.

token.description: The short-lived JWKS-signed access JWT (token_use:api_key).

jti.description: Unique token id — deny-list this to revoke one token.

key_id.description: The long-lived key this token was minted from (the JWT sub).

organization.description: Present for a key bound to an organization: the membership at mint time (`id`, `role`, `permissions`). `scopes` is then the effective scopes and the token carries the same object as its `organization` claim.

cnf.description: Proof-of-possession confirmation — present only for a PoP key.

expires_in.description: Lifetime in seconds (clamped to key expiry + org ceiling + global cap).

issuer.description: The issuer/JWKS a verifier checks this token against.

revoked_reason.description: Why, when a person did not revoke it: `membership_ended`, `creator_departed` or `organization_deleted`.

organization_id.description: The organization the key was bound to, if any.

end_reason.description: Always answered once the key ended (secret-key callers only): the stored reason, else `revoked_by_api` or `revoked_by_admin`.

revoked_by.description: Who revoked the key (secret-key callers only).

allOf.description: The mint response — the read object plus the reveal-once plaintext key.

secret.description: Reveal-once plaintext ak_ key (create-only). Null for a key_pair key, which has no secret.

private_key.description: key_pair only, and only when Atlas generated the pair: the PKCS#8 PEM private key (the same format as an Apple .p8 file), shown once. Atlas never stores it and an Idempotency-Key retry does not return it. Absent when you supplied your own `public_key`.

ApiKeyVerification.description: The result of verifying an API key secret: `valid: true` with the key details, or `valid: false` (alone for an unknown, revoked, expired or disabled key; with a `code` when a live key is refused by its scopes, rate limit or use budget).

name.description: The key name.

claims.description: The custom claims stored on the key.

scopes.description: The key scopes (null when none are set).

credential.description: Present only when a key-pair assertion was verified (send `token`).

audience.description: key_pair: the audience the assertion named and the key allows.

jti.description: key_pair: the assertion `jti` (single-use until `exp`), null when it carried none.

exp.description: key_pair: the assertion `exp`, in epoch SECONDS as signed.

effective_scopes.description: The key scopes (and any `claims.scope`) expanded through the instance scope implications (`endUserApiKeys.scopeImplications`, e.g. calls:write ⇒ calls:read; `*` = every scope the instance names). Sorted; equals the held scopes when no implications are configured. `required_scopes` is checked against this set.

organization.description: Present for a user key bound to an organization: the user's CURRENT membership. `effective_scopes` is then the key scopes (after implications) that the membership's `permissions` cover: a permission covers a scope of the same name, `*` covers every scope, `<prefix>:*` covers scopes starting `<prefix>:`.

role.description: The member's role key in the organization.

permissions.description: The permissions the role (and the member's groups) grant.

created_by_user_id.description: The member who created an organization key (present when recorded).

limits.description: The key spend caps and rate windows (null when none).

usage.description: Each cap with its current-window usage.

expires_at.description: The key expiry (epoch ms), or null when it never expires.

remaining.description: Uses left after this verify (null = unlimited).

source.description: Which rule chose it, in precedence order: a per-subject override, the API key's own rate_limit, the default policy's entry for the subject's plan, the default policy.

plan.description: The plan slug that chose the limit (source "plan").

version.description: Changes whenever the effective limit changes. Keep a cached copy until it differs.

rate_limit.description: The limit your own API should apply to this key: its per-subject override, its own rate_limit, or the rate-limit policy for its plan or the default policy. null when none applies. Atlas does not enforce it; your service does (GET /v1/rate_limit_policies/resolve returns the same object).

code.description: Present only when a LIVE key was refused by its own policy. Absent for unknown, revoked, expired, disabled or subject-deleted keys (never says which). For a `token` (key-pair assertion) check: `invalid_assertion` answers, with no id, everything that does not prove the holder signed it (malformed, unknown key, bad signature, wrong algorithm, iss not the kid, revoked or disabled key), and the other assertion codes appear only once the signature has verified.

id.description: The key id (with code only).

missing_scopes.description: insufficient_scope: the required scopes the key lacks.

retry_after_ms.description: rate_limited: when the key may verify again.

organization_id.description: Owning org, when org-scoped.

owner_user_id.description: Owning user, when a user-owned device.

status.description: Stored device lifecycle state (unchanged by the owner's state).

owner_usable.description: Whether the owning user is usable (not banned, locked, or deleted). True when the machine has no owner. When false the machine cannot mint or verify tokens even while its stored status stays 'active'.

effective_status.description: Derived status: 'active' only when the machine is active AND its owner is usable; 'owner_suspended' when active but the owner is not; otherwise the raw status.

device_key.description: The stable device self-identifier supplied at enrolment (null when none). Lets a fleet manager correlate this record with the device it re-enrolled across tokens.

public_key_jkt.description: RFC 7638 thumbprint of the device public key.

token_binding.description: The sender constraint every token this machine mints must carry: none (a plain bearer token), dpop (a DPoP proof, token bound with cnf.jkt), mtls (a client certificate, bound with cnf x5t#S256) or any. A proof or certificate sent under none still binds the token.

metadata.description: Device metadata (hostname, os, app_version, last_seen_at).

enrolled_at.description: When the device completed enrolment (epoch ms).

last_token_at.description: When the machine last minted a token (epoch ms; null = never).

revoked_reason.description: Why a revoked machine ended: revoked_by_api, revoked_by_user, owner_signed_out, superseded, delegation_ended. Null while not revoked.

type.description: api_key, user or system.

revoked_by.description: Who revoked the machine. Null while not revoked.

ended_at.description: Epoch ms the machine was revoked. Null while not revoked.

dies_with.description: `sign_out_everywhere`: the machine is revoked when its owner signs out everywhere. Needs an owner.

allOf.description: Machine create/rotate — the read object plus the reveal-once secret.

secret.description: Reveal-once mk_ secret (create/rotate-only).

format.description: token = a long met_ secret; user_code = a short single-use code typed on the device.

allOf.description: Enrolment-token create — the read object plus the reveal-once secret: a met_ token, or the user_code for format user_code.

token.description: Reveal-once met_ enrolment token (create-only; absent for format user_code).

user_code.description: Reveal-once short code, 8 letters shown as XXXX-XXXX (create-only; format user_code).

scopes.description: The scopes the machine may request. Always plain scope values: presets are expanded before storing.

constraints.description: Limits set on the grant, carried in the `constraints` claim of every token the machine mints for this resource server. Null when none.

expires_at.description: When the grant stops minting tokens (epoch ms), or null for no expiry.

expired.description: True once `expires_at` has passed. An expired grant mints nothing and is dropped from verify results.

dies_with.description: Recorded `sign_out_everywhere`. A grant of a machine that has an owner always ends with the owner signing out everywhere.

revoked_at.description: Epoch ms the grant was ended (it is kept as a record for 90 days; `GET .../grants?include_ended=true` lists it). Null while live.

revoked_reason.description: Why it ended: revoked_by_api or owner_signed_out.

role.description: The organization role key.

audience.description: Machine JWT only: the resource server it is bound to.

scopes.description: Machine JWT only: the scopes it carries.

organization_id.description: Machine JWT only: its organization context.

org_role.description: Machine JWT only: its role in that organization.

org_permissions.description: Machine JWT only: that role's permissions when it was minted.

expires_at.description: Machine JWT only: when it expires (epoch ms).

organization_memberships.description: The organizations the machine is a member of now.

token.description: Reveal-once one-time ticket (create-only).
Reveal-once one-time ticket (create-only).

free.description: true when the plan has no Stripe price.

limits.description: Numeric limits this plan grants, e.g. {"max_devices":5}. The structured `ent` session claim carries these.

promotion.description: A display-only promotion shown on the plan card: { label, percent_off | amount_off (minor units), ends_at (epoch ms), code }. It never changes what the provider charges; on the public list an expired promotion is null.

provider_price_id.description: The plan's price reference on its provider (Stripe price, Polar/Dodo/Creem product, Chargebee item price, Autumn plan, Commet plan).

kind.description: base: the subject's main plan (one live at a time). addon: bought alongside it; several may be live.

seat_feature_id.description: Autumn plans: the plan feature whose usage follows the organization's member count (synced on every membership change and by sync_seats).

description.description: Pricing-table copy under the plan name.

badge.description: Pricing-table badge on the plan card, e.g. "Most popular".

sort_order.description: Pricing-table order, ascending; plans with equal values keep newest first.

default_limit_merge.description: How a numeric limit combines across entitling subscriptions unless limit_merge names it.

source.description: provider: asked live of Autumn/Commet; atlas: from the resolved entitlement.

EntitlementOverride.description: A sales-led entitlement override (P1-6): a non-Stripe grant pinning a plan / features / limits onto a user or org. A non-expired override wins over the Stripe-derived entitlement.

plan.description: Plan slug to pin, or null to override features/limits only.

expires_at.description: Epoch ms when the override lapses, or null for open-ended.

allOf.description: The enriched org-get (P0-3): the organization plus its member role breakdown and effective entitlement, so an integrator need not keep a local org mirror.

scanned.description: How many members the role counts were computed over (bounded).

roles.description: Count of members per role key, over the scanned page.

entitlements.description: The org's effective entitlement (plan/features/limits), or null when none.

type.description: The protocol. Enterprise connections are `saml` or `oidc`.

status.description: A `draft` connection never completes a sign-in.

domains.description: The email domains this connection owns.

scim_base_url.description: The SCIM 2.0 base URL for this organization's identity provider (pair it with a SCIM token).

entitlements.description: What an entitlement provider (Autumn, Commet) reports this subscription grants: { features, limits }.

subscriptions.description: FAPI subscription read only: every subscription the subject holds (base + add-ons).

url.description: The HTTPS receiver; for an event destination, a descriptor such as aws-eventbridge://us-east-1/default.

event_naming.description: Which names `*` delivers under: canonical, or the pre-convention spellings (endpoints created before the canonical catalogue).

external.description: A third-party receiver: preflight does not flag its host as off-origin.

managed_by.description: The connected platform (for example `cookiemunch`) that owns this endpoint and holds its secret; null for one you manage. Set by the platform when it connects, or by you on create/PATCH for an endpoint you made for that platform: the URL must be on that platform's API host (for Cookie Munch, api.cookiemunch.net). `atlas plan` lists it under "Managed by a connected platform" and never prunes or exports it; preflight does not flag it as off-origin. null hands it back to you.

filters.description: Delivery filters beyond `enabled_events`: `organization_ids` (only events of these organizations) and `metadata` (predicates over the event data, all must hold). null = no filter.

header_names.description: The static request headers sent on every delivery. Their values are write-only and never returned.

oauth.description: The OAuth client-credentials grant Atlas uses to get a bearer token for deliveries: token_url, client_id, scope, audience, client_secret_set. The client secret is never returned.

max_rps.description: Deliveries per second this endpoint may receive; null = unlimited.

include_private_membership.description: Membership events to this endpoint carry the seat private_metadata.

destination.description: Where deliveries go: { type: "https" } or an event destination with its non-secret settings. Credentials are never returned (credentials_set says whether they are stored).

failing_since.description: Start of the current failure streak (epoch ms), or null when the last delivery succeeded.

last_failing_since.description: Start of the failure streak that preceded the last re-enable (epoch ms); what replay resolves since=failing_since to once the live streak is cleared.

disabled_at.description: When the endpoint was switched off after repeated failures (epoch ms), or null.

success_rate_24h.description: Share of attempts in the last 24 hours that succeeded (0–1), null with no attempts.

alert_contacts.description: Who is emailed when it fails; null = the owners of the account.

alerts_sent.description: Alerts sent for the current streak: first (1 hour), second (24 hours) and the disabled notice (epoch ms or null).

previous_secret_expires_at.description: While a secret rotation overlap is open: when the previous secret stops signing deliveries (epoch ms). Until then every delivery carries two signatures. Null otherwise.

replay.description: On an update that re-enabled the endpoint: the call that replays what it missed.

created.description: On create and PUT by_url: whether this call created the endpoint.

after_failing_ms.description: Disabled after failing this long (72 hours).

after_consecutive_failures.description: Or after this many failed attempts in a row…

consecutive_failures_min_failing_ms.description: …once it has been failing at least this long (24 hours).

TestCallResult.description: The fields every test call answers with (a webhook endpoint test, a hook test), so one check covers both. Other fields on a test answer are specific to that test and kept as they were.

ok.description: True when the receiver answered as a working one should (2xx for a webhook; a valid answer or a deny for a hook). Null while a webhook test is only queued (no ?wait).

status.description: success or failed once attempted; pending while a webhook test is queued.

http_status.description: The HTTP status the receiver answered with; null when no answer came (timeout, network error) or nothing was sent yet.

latency_ms.description: How long the attempt took; null when nothing was sent yet.

delivery_id.description: The delivery, as it appears in the endpoint's delivery log.

event_id.description: The atlas-id header that was sent.

event_type.description: Always the synthetic webhook.test event, signed with the endpoint's real signing secret (both secrets during a rotation overlap).

url.description: The exact URL the attempt was POSTed to (the endpoint URL as stored), so a wrong path shows here.

response_snippet.description: The first 1 KB of the response.

error.description: webhook_http_error, webhook_timeout, webhook_network_error, webhook_redirect_not_followed or webhook_url_blocked:<reason>.

error_kind.description: One word for why the attempt failed: non_2xx (your receiver answered, not 2xx: see http_status and response_snippet), redirect (a 3xx, which Atlas never follows), timeout (no answer within 10 s), tls (certificate or handshake failure), dns, connection_refused, network, url_blocked (the URL resolves to an address Atlas will not call). Null on success.

signature_header_sent.description: The atlas-signature header that was sent, to compare with what your verifier computes.

will_retry.description: A failed test is retried on the normal schedule.

events_days.description: Events are kept this many days (90).

delivery_log_days.description: Delivery attempts are kept this many days (30).

replay_window_days.description: Replay and redeliver reach back this far (90).

allOf.description: The create response — the endpoint plus the whsec_ signing secret, returned only once.

secret.description: whsec_ signing secret (create-only).

actor.description: Who caused the event (`system` when no request did).

idempotency_key.description: The Idempotency-Key header of the request that caused the event, else null.

data.description: The event subject (e.g. the user, session or organization object); its shape depends on `type`.

event_type.description: The name the event was delivered as (the canonical name, or the deprecated spelling the endpoint subscribed to), or null once the event has passed its retention.

latency_ms.description: How long the receiver took to answer.

trace_id.description: The W3C trace-id the delivery carried in its traceparent; every retry repeats it.

payload.description: The event payload that was sent (null once the event has passed its retention).

error.description: Why the attempt failed, as a code: `webhook_redirect_not_followed` (the endpoint answered 3xx; Atlas never follows redirects, see `location`), `webhook_http_error`, `webhook_timeout`, `webhook_network_error` or `webhook_url_blocked`. Null on success or while pending.

location.description: The `Location` header of a 3xx answer, resolved to an absolute URL. Not followed.

next_retry_at.description: When the next attempt is due; null once the delivery succeeded or no attempt is owed.

BackchannelLogoutDelivery.description: One back-channel logout attempt to an OAuth client's or Sign in with Atlas app's backchannel_logout_uri. Atlas never follows redirects: a 3xx answer fails with error `backchannel_redirect_not_followed` and the `location` it pointed at. A 5xx, 408, 429 or no answer is retried on the webhook schedule (5 s, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h, 5 h, 10 h); any other 4xx is final.

trace_id.description: The W3C trace-id the logout_token POST carried in its traceparent.

sid.description: The ended session (`sid_test_…` for a test). Null for "sign out everywhere".

test.description: Sent by the test call; never retried.

error.description: `backchannel_redirect_not_followed`, `backchannel_http_error`, `backchannel_timeout`, `backchannel_network_error` or `backchannel_url_blocked`. Null on success or while pending.

location.description: The absolute `Location` of a 3xx answer. Not followed.

BackchannelLogoutTest.description: The result of a test back-channel logout: a correctly signed logout_token for a synthetic session (`sid_test_…`) with the extra claim `atlas_test: true`, POSTed now. Recorded in the delivery log with `test: true`.

status.description: The HTTP status the receiver answered with; null when nothing came back.

location.description: The `Location` of a 3xx answer. Not followed.

blocked_reason.description: Set when nothing was sent because the URI points at a private, loopback or non-https address.

body_excerpt.description: The first 512 characters of the response body, control characters removed.

next_cursor.description: Pass as starting_after for the next page.

ok.description: True when there are no error-severity findings.

user_count.description: People who have approved the app.

findings.description: Ordered error, then warning, then info.

button_rendered_origins.description: The page origins the Sign in with Atlas button script ran on in the last 7 days: authorize requests carrying atlasid_button (the rendered button, the JavaScript API, a server login route that forwards it) and One Tap. Most recent first. Empty when every sign-in started without the script.

authorize_requests_7d.description: How the app's authorize requests of the last 7 days started: button (atlasid_button=1), js (atlasid_button=js), fedcm (One Tap), fallback (the no-script link, atlasid_fallback=1) and unmarked (none of these). atlas_id_button_never_rendered fires when button, js and fedcm are all 0, at least one request came in, and the homepage includes the script.

fallback_origins.description: The page origins whose sign-ins came through the no-script fallback link in the last 7 days.

homepage_includes_script.description: Whether the app's homepage_url HTML references the button script (checked at most hourly). null = no homepage_url, or it could not be read.

origin.description: The page origin (scheme, host and port).

last_seen_at.description: Epoch ms of the latest request from it.

requests.description: Authorize requests from it in the last 7 days.

ConnectorApiScope.description: A high-value provider API scope surfaced as an opt-in toggle.

scope.description: The provider's scope string, sent verbatim.

gated.description: The provider gates this scope behind app review or an elevated plan.

ConnectorCredentialField.description: One credential input an enabler supplies (e.g. client_id, private_key).

secret.description: Stored encrypted and never returned.

metadata.description: Action-specific context recorded with the entry.

Localization.description: A per-locale content override. Note: created_at/updated_at are ISO-8601 strings here, not epoch-ms.

zone_id.description: The network zone this rule matches instead of `cidr`.

source.description: The current version’s policy source.

request.description: principal, action, resource, context and optional entities.

reasons.description: Names of the policies that decided it.

errors.description: Policies skipped because they errored while evaluating.

annotations.description: The `@annotations` of the policies that decided it, when any carry them.

parent_type.description: The type a resource of this type nests under.

inherit.description: Whether assignments on a parent resource flow down to resources of this type.

includes.description: Other roles of the same type this role also grants.

external_id.description: Your own identifier for the resource.

seq.description: Position in the feed (also the cursor).

change.description: `created` also covers re-assigning a role to update `inherit`.

grants.description: The assignments that allow it (single checks only).

AbacFilter.description: A residual-policy condition over fields of the unknown entity (`resource.department`, `principal.level`; reserved `<var>.$id` and `<var>.$ancestors`). Leaves are total booleans (a missing field is false) and there is no `not`. `and`/`or` carry `args`; `eq|ne|lt|lte|gt|gte` carry `field` with a `value` or a `ref` field; `cmp` carries `cmp`, `left` and `right` terms for arithmetic; `in|not_in` carry `values`; `contains|not_contains` carry a `value` for a set-valued field; `like|not_like` carry a `pattern` (`*` wildcard); `exists|missing` carry a `field`; `relation|not_relation` are unresolved relationship conditions.

decision.description: `allow`/`deny` when the filter is constant; `conditional` otherwise.

relations_resolved.description: true when relationship conditions were replaced by id lists from the FGA store.

text.description: A parameterised boolean expression for WHERE.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `starting_after` for the next page.

total.description: All resources the principal may act on.

method.description: `residual` when one filter was applied to every candidate; `per_resource` when the policies had to be evaluated candidate by candidate.

AbacCoverage.description: Which rules and `when`/`unless` clauses the test cases exercised.

rule.description: 1-based position of the rule in the source.

in_scope.description: Tests whose principal, action and resource fell in the rule’s scope.

matched.description: Tests in which the rule matched.

percent.description: Rules reached, as a whole percentage.

gaps.description: What to add a test for, one sentence each.

source.description: Policy source with `?principal` / `?resource` slots in the scope.

version.description: Increases each time `source` changes; every link follows it.

links_updated.description: On an update that changed `source`: the links that now evaluate the new source.

name.description: Shown as the deciding policy in decisions.

template_version.description: The template version the link currently follows (always the latest).

source.description: The policy source the link evaluates: the template with its slots filled.

schema.description: The entity schema: `entity_types` and `actions`. Null when none is set.

version.description: 0 when none is set.

policy_issues.description: On a save: the errors this schema would give the policies and links already stored (the schema is saved anyway; they must be fixed before those are edited).

policy.description: 1-based position of the policy in the source (0 for a syntax error).

source_name.description: With `policy_issues`: the stored policy or link the issue belongs to.

valid.description: false when there is any error (warnings do not count).

schema_checked.description: false when no schema was set or the source did not parse.

semantic.description: The requests whose decision changes. Null when `semantic` was false.

space.description: Size of the request space the policies define.

exhaustive.description: false when the space was sampled rather than enumerated.

truncated.description: More changes exist than are listed.

assuming.description: Present when a version uses `fga.check`: the assumption the change holds under.

mode.description: report_only never denies; it records what the policy would have done.

allow.description: persistent_session: false forbids a remembered session.

report_only.description: What report-only policies would have decided; never enforced.

status.description: accepted | withdrawn

metadata.description: Free-form context recorded with the consent.

policy_version_id.description: Policy acceptance: the exact version accepted.

content_sha256.description: Policy acceptance: SHA-256 of the content shown.

view_ms.description: Client-attested time the document was open.

FgaAuthorizationModel.description: `model` is present on create + single-get, omitted from list responses.

AuthzDecision.description: One logged authorization decision. `input` is redacted per the capture settings (null when capture is off).

principal.description: Who asked: `Type::id` (ABAC / AuthZEN), the FGA user, or the user id (access policies).

action.description: The action, the FGA relation, or the access-policy stage.

input.description: The request as kept by `input_mode`: identifiers only, or the whole request with the configured paths blanked.

result.description: Reasons (policy names), matched policies, error counts, FGA `allowed` and whether it was served from cache.

policy_revision.description: The signed-bundle revision in force when this was decided (`rev_…`); access-policy decisions carry an `ap_…` digest instead.

policy_version.description: The exact policy versions or FGA model that evaluated.

sample_rate.description: The probability this decision was kept at; divide counts by it to estimate the true volume.

cache_ttl_ms.description: Result-cache TTL in milliseconds; null uses the platform default, 0 turns the cache off.

default_consistency.description: Applied to reads that do not name a consistency mode.

changelog_retention_days.description: Days of tuple change log kept; null keeps all of it.

enabled.description: Record decisions. Off by default.

input_mode.description: `ids` keeps only identifiers; `full` keeps the request minus the `redact` paths; `none` keeps no input.

redact.description: Dotted paths blanked in `full` mode; `*` matches one segment (`context.ip`, `principal.attributes.*`).

ship_to_events.description: Also emit each recorded decision as an `authz.decision` event, so log streams, webhooks and event destinations receive it.

retention_days.description: Days to keep decisions; null keeps them.

revision.description: A digest of the bundle CONTENT (`rev_…`): the same policy has the same revision on every instance.

key_id.description: The instance signing key id (`kid`), published in the JWKS.

signature.description: A detached compact JWS (`header..signature`) over the archive bytes.

manifest.description: format, format_version, revision, created_at, contents and the SHA-256 of every file.

bundle.description: The tar.gz, base64-encoded. Present on create and get; omitted from lists.

PolicyBundleDiff.description: What importing a bundle would change.

absent.description: On the instance but not in the bundle; deleted only with `prune`.
Never deleted by an import: a store holds relationship data.
On the instance but not in the bundle; deleted (with their links) only with `prune`.
On the instance but not in the bundle; deleted only with `prune`.

abac_schema.description: The ABAC entity schema: `absent` means the instance has one and the bundle does not (removed only with `prune`).

identical.description: True when nothing would be created or updated.

FgaTupleCondition.description: A model condition bound to a tuple: the tuple grants only while the CEL expression holds.

name.description: A condition defined in the authorization model.

context.description: Values for the condition parameters fixed on this tuple.

consistency_token.description: The consistency token of the write that made this change.

created_at.description: When the change was recorded (epoch ms).

user.description: The subject: `user:alice`, a userset `group:eng#member`, or a wildcard `user:*`.

expires_at.description: When the tuple stops granting: an ISO 8601 timestamp or epoch milliseconds, in the future. A background sweep then deletes it and logs the change.

FgaUserset.description: One userset-rewrite node: exactly one operator. `this` = directly assigned; `computedUserset` = another relation on the same object; `tupleToUserset` = a relation on objects reached through a tupleset relation; `union` / `intersection` / `difference` combine child rewrites.

FgaRelationReference.description: A user type a relation may be directly assigned: `user`, a userset `group#member`, or the `user:*` wildcard.

condition.description: Tuples on this relation for this user type must carry this model condition (`[user with ip_allowed]`).

FgaCondition.description: A named condition: a CEL expression over typed parameters. Tuples (and requests) supply the parameter values.

expression.description: CEL, e.g. `ip.in_cidr(cidr)`. Up to 2048 characters; every identifier must be a declared parameter. Regex `matches` is not supported.

parameters.description: Parameter name to type.

FgaTypeDefinition.description: One OpenFGA type definition: its relations and their rewrites.

type.description: The type name, e.g. `document`.

FgaUsersetTree.description: The expanded userset tree (Atlas-native expand), discriminated by `type`.

OpenFgaNode.description: An OpenFGA expand `Node`: a `name` and exactly one of `leaf` / `union` / `intersection` / `difference`.

scope_presets.description: Named bundles over `scopes`. Send names as `scope_presets` wherever this API's scopes are requested; they are unioned with `scopes` and expanded before any check.

publish_resource_metadata.description: Atlas serves RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata for this API at /oauth2/resource-metadata?resource=<identifier>.

signing_alg.description: The algorithm of the access tokens issued for this API. RS256 by default. When it differs from the instance key, a second key of that algorithm signs them (published in the same JWKS); only one second key is published, so an instance signing two other algorithms refuses a third (409).

access_token_format.description: `jwt` or `opaque` access tokens for this API; null = inherited from the client / instance.

refresh_token_absolute_ttl_seconds.description: Refresh-token lifetime for grants issued for this API; null = inherited.

refresh_token_idle_ttl_seconds.description: Refresh-token idle timeout for grants issued for this API; null = inherited.

introspection_client_ids.description: client_ids of the confidential clients allowed to introspect this API's tokens.

OrgPolicy.description: Org policy override object. Keys are camelCase (mirrors readOrgPolicy). Only set overrides appear.

requireMfa.description: Require a second factor. MFA is required while this is true OR any requireMfaReasons tag remains. By default it only withholds the org claims from the session token; read org_mfa_required / org_mfa_ok (backend mfaOrgSatisfied) when you authorize from your own tables.

requireMfaReasons.description: Free-form tags (up to 10, lower-case, 40 characters) naming why MFA is required, so two features can share the policy.

mfaEnforcement.description: withhold_claims (default) withholds org claims; require_step_up also refuses activating the org (403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED, reason org_mfa_step_up_required) until the member steps up.

mfaMaxAgeSeconds.description: The last second factor must be at most this old; implies MFA is required.

allowedMfaFactors.description: Accepted second-factor kinds; implies MFA is required. The session records which kind passed; a recovery code, emailed code or older session matches none and must step up.

passwordPolicyOverride.description: Tighten-only password rules layered over the instance policy: minLength, bannedPasswords, and checkBreaches/requireUppercase/requireLowercase/requireNumber/requireSymbol (true only).

allowedSignInMethods.description: Restrict which sign-in methods a member may use (e.g. "password", "passkey", "oauth", "oauth:google", "saml", "magic_link"). Empty/absent = all methods. Enforced by membership; most-restrictive across the user's orgs.

ipAllowlist.description: CIDR allow-list gating sign-in for members (e.g. "203.0.113.0/24"). Empty/absent = unrestricted. Most-restrictive across the user's orgs.

maxSessionAgeSeconds.description: Cap the absolute session lifetime for members, in seconds (300 … 7776000). Null/absent = instance default. Smallest cap across the user's orgs wins.

maxSessions.description: Cap on the concurrent active sessions of each member. A sign-in past the cap ends the member's least recently active session. Smallest cap across the user's orgs wins; it can only tighten the instance cap. Absent = no org cap.

ssoMultiConnection.description: Allow this organization more than one enterprise SSO connection. Absent/false: a second connection is refused.

memberVisibility.description: What ordinary members see of each other in Frontend API member lists: directory (default: name and picture) or private (member id and role only). Members who manage memberships always see names, plus the primary email and MFA status.

ssoBypass.description: Break-glass for forced SSO: email addresses (at most 20) that may still sign in with a password while ssoRequired is on. Every use is audited as sso.break_glass_signin.

itContacts.description: The organization's technical contacts (at most 10), recorded so support and onboarding know who to contact about its connections.

OrgPolicyPatch.description: Org policy PATCH body — camelCase keys; explicit null CLEARS an override.

requireMfaReasons.description: Replaces the whole tag list; null clears it.

requireMfaReasonsAdd.description: Adds tags without touching the others.

requireMfaReasonsRemove.description: Removes tags without touching the others.

passwordPolicyOverride.description: Tighten-only password rules layered over the instance policy: minLength, bannedPasswords, and checkBreaches/requireUppercase/requireLowercase/requireNumber/requireSymbol (true only).

allowedSignInMethods.description: Restrict which sign-in methods a member may use (e.g. "password", "oauth:google", "saml", "magic_link"). null CLEARS the override (all methods). Unknown method → 400.

ipAllowlist.description: CIDR allow-list gating member sign-in. null CLEARS the override. A bad CIDR → 400.

maxSessionAgeSeconds.description: Cap the absolute session lifetime for members, in seconds (300 … 7776000). null CLEARS the override.

maxSessions.description: Cap on the concurrent active sessions of each member (1 … 100). null CLEARS the override.

ssoMultiConnection.description: Allow the organization more than one enterprise SSO connection. null CLEARS the override.

entitlementPlan.description: Retired (never affected entitlements). Only null is accepted, to clear a stored value; any other value → 422. Grant an org a plan/features/limits with POST /v1/entitlement_overrides (subject_type "org").

entitlementOverrides.description: Retired — see entitlementPlan. Only null (clear) is accepted.

memberVisibility.description: What ordinary members see of each other in Frontend API member lists: directory (default: name and picture) or private (member id and role only). Members who manage memberships always see names, plus the primary email and MFA status. null CLEARS the override.

ssoBypass.description: Break-glass email addresses (at most 20) allowed to use a password while ssoRequired is on. null CLEARS the list.

itContacts.description: Technical contacts (at most 10). null CLEARS the list.

ReaderDomain.description: A reader-pool custom domain (its `object` const is 'custom_domain').

OAuthProvider.description: A social/OAuth provider config. Secrets never returned (has_secret marks presence).

credential_fields.description: The fields the redirect flow needs (client id and secret).

modes.description: For a provider with a native (in-page) mode: the credential fields and a hint for each sign-in mode. Native needs no client secret. Null for a redirect-only provider.

connection_extras.description: Non-secret settings a connection OAuth client of this provider (`PUT /v1/connections/oauth_clients`) carries in `host_params`, such as TikTok Shop's `service_id`. A required one must be sent; an unknown key is refused.

key.description: The `host_params` key.

required.description: Must be present on a connection OAuth client of this provider.

pattern.description: Anchored regular expression the whole value must match.

setting_values.description: Credential-less providers only (siwe, siws, siwb, siwf): the stored verifier settings, e.g. { domain, chain_ids, rpc_url }. Empty for every other provider.

native.description: True when this provider signs in through an in-page native library (e.g. Google One Tap / GSI) that verifies an id_token, rather than a redirect. A native provider also requires its `javascript_origins` to be registered on the provider console.

mode.description: The effective sign-in mode. Defaults from the provider's capability (native-capable ⇒ native), but a tenant can force `redirect` via PUT { mode: "redirect" } to skip the in-page library entirely (e.g. when the JavaScript origin can't be registered). Exposed in /v1/client/environment and honoured by the SDK.

javascript_origins.description: Native providers only: the Authorized JavaScript origins to register on the provider console (the in-page library refuses to start on an unregistered origin, failing silently). Atlas draws the button on its hosted host and on the instance's app origins. Empty for a non-native provider.

redirect_uri.description: The exact callback URL to register at the provider console.

atlas_callback.description: Atlas's own callback URL; a custom_redirect_uri forwards ?code&state here.

native_client_ids.description: The extra audiences a native app id_token may carry (set with `native_client_ids` on PUT, an array or a comma list, or settings.native_client_ids; an empty array or string clears it). Empty when none.

custom_redirect_uri.description: A tenant's own already-registered callback (migration): Atlas uses it in the authorize + token exchange and it forwards to atlas_callback. Null when unset.

hosted_id_token.description: For a provider whose authorize page can return an id_token (google, apple, microsoft, twitch): sign-in with only the client_id on every platform (native apps, Expo Go, desktop, web), used automatically while the provider has no client secret. `available` says whether that is the case now; `redirect_uri` is the URL to register with the provider for it. Null for other providers.

enabled.description: Whether the provider is turned on. Saving credentials via PUT does NOT enable it; toggle with POST /v1/oauth_providers/{provider}/enabled.

icon_url.description: The instance's per-provider icon override, or null.

faviconUrl.description: The hosted pages' favicon (https). Without it, the logo is used. Served at /favicon.ico on the Frontend API host.

collect_on.description: When the field is asked for. sign_up (default): the sign-up form. next_sign_in: held at the next sign-in that finds it empty. before_feature: asked by the application via GET /v1/client/me/profile_completion.

reprompt_days.description: An optional next_sign_in field the user skipped is asked again after this many days (default 30; 0 = never).

accountPortal.description: The hosted account page (/hosted/user): panels maps each panel (profile, email_addresses, password, passkeys, mfa, sessions, linked_accounts, connected_apps, shared_resources, ciba, referrals, delete_account) to false to hide it. Absent = shown. A panel whose feature is off for the instance is never drawn. Merged per panel on PATCH (null removes a key; accountPortal: null clears all). Also accepted as account_portal.

audiences.description: Per-audience branding for the hosted sign-in and sign-up pages, keyed by audience hint (1-32 characters: a-z, 0-9, _ and -; at most 20). A sign-in started with audience_hint=<hint> (on /oauth2/authorize or the hosted page URL) uses that entry's heading, subheading, logo and primary colour; any other hint gets the default branding. PATCH merges per hint: an entry replaces that hint, null deletes it, audiences: null removes them all.

subheading.description: Replaces the line under the heading.

primaryColor.description: Replaces the primary colour (hex, rgb() or a CSS colour name).

BrandingSettings.description: The editable branding settings (sign-in page, emails, hosted pages). Every field is optional. On PATCH a field is replaced as sent; inside socialButtons each per-provider map merges per key, a null value deletes that key, a null map clears it, and socialButtons: null removes the whole bag. Retired keys may still appear on read.

faviconUrl.description: The hosted pages' favicon (https). Without it, the logo is used. Served at /favicon.ico on the Frontend API host.

collect_on.description: When the field is asked for. sign_up (default): the sign-up form. next_sign_in: held at the next sign-in that finds it empty. before_feature: asked by the application via GET /v1/client/me/profile_completion.

reprompt_days.description: An optional next_sign_in field the user skipped is asked again after this many days (default 30; 0 = never).

accountPortal.description: The hosted account page (/hosted/user): panels maps each panel (profile, email_addresses, password, passkeys, mfa, sessions, linked_accounts, connected_apps, shared_resources, ciba, referrals, delete_account) to false to hide it. Absent = shown. A panel whose feature is off for the instance is never drawn. Merged per panel on PATCH (null removes a key; accountPortal: null clears all). Also accepted as account_portal.

audiences.description: Per-audience branding for the hosted sign-in and sign-up pages, keyed by audience hint (1-32 characters: a-z, 0-9, _ and -; at most 20).
