A sign-in started with audience_hint=<hint> (on /oauth2/authorize or the hosted page URL) uses that entry's heading, subheading, logo and primary colour; any other hint gets the default branding. PATCH merges per hint: an entry replaces that hint, null deletes it, audiences: null removes them all.

subheading.description: Replaces the line under the heading.

primaryColor.description: Replaces the primary colour (hex, rgb() or a CSS colour name).

account_portal.description: The hosted account page (/hosted/user): panels maps each panel (profile, email_addresses, password, passkeys, mfa, sessions, linked_accounts, connected_apps, shared_resources, ciba, referrals, delete_account) to false to hide it. Absent = shown. A panel whose feature is off for the instance is never drawn. Merged per panel on PATCH (null removes a key; accountPortal: null clears all). Also accepted as account_portal.

BrandingPatch.description: A partial branding change. Every field is optional and replaces the stored value; inside socialButtons each per-provider map merges per key, a null value deletes that key, a null map clears it, and socialButtons: null removes the whole bag. audiences merges per audience hint the same way. A field this endpoint does not know is ignored and named in Atlas-Unknown-Fields, or refused with 422 UNKNOWN_FIELD when the request sends Atlas-Strict: true.

Branding.description: The branding settings, plus `resolved`: what the renderers actually use after dropping anything unsafe.

resolved.description: What the renderers use, after dropping anything unsafe or invalid. Every writable field appears here under the same name and shape you write it (fontFamily, providers, copy, legal, theme, layout, card, interaction, …), holding the value in force: compare your desired state against this object alone. A field you did not set shows its default. Also carries derived renderer values (escapedName, fontStack, providerOrder, providerHidden, eyebrow, headline, subheadline, footer). The retired raw fields customCss / customHtmlHeader / customHtmlFooter resolve to "" unless set on Atlas's own instance.

audiences.description: Every audience the hosted page can theme for, as it reads them (invalid values dropped).

fontFamily.description: The font stack name in force (system when unset or unknown).

fontStack.description: The CSS font-family list fontFamily resolves to.

dormant_accounts.description: Dormant-account reactivation alerts: when an account idle for `threshold_days` signs in again, audit + `user.reactivated` webhook + optional user notice, and optionally a second-factor step-up.

reason.description: Reason code returned when the rule matches.

groups.description: The endpoint groups a rule may name.

replaces_built_in.description: The built-in budget a rule on this group replaces; null when a rule is added on top.

key.description: ip: per client IP; user: per signed-in user (Frontend API) or the user in the path (Backend API), falling back to the IP or key; instance: one budget for every caller.

enabled.description: What GET /v1/appearance reports: the button shows on the embedded <SignIn> and the hosted page.

managed_via.description: instance_toggle: provisioned by Atlas (removed when turned off). linked: your own connection (only unmarked when turned off).

turned_on.description: automatically: Atlas found the one Atlas ID connection your instance manages and turned the button on. by_you: the toggle or a PATCH turned it on. null while off.

turned_off_by_you.description: Off because you turned it off. Atlas will not switch it back on by itself.

connection_status.description: The connection status; the button shows only while it is active.

available.description: Whether this deployment can provision a connection (it has an Atlas ID instance).

issuer.description: The Atlas issuer a connection must point at.

candidates.description: Your active OIDC connections to the Atlas issuer that are not in use: what connection_id may name.

managed_by_this_instance.description: This instance manages the Atlas ID app (its own, or adopted).

UserTraitsSchemaDocument.description: A JSON Schema per target. Targets: public_metadata, unsafe_metadata, private_metadata, organization_public_metadata, organization_private_metadata. Each root has type "object".

version.description: 0 until a schema is stored.

sign_in_url.description: /hosted/sign-in answers 302 here; null serves the Atlas page.

sign_up_url.description: /hosted/sign-up answers 302 here; null serves the Atlas page.

user_url.description: /hosted/user answers 302 here; null serves the Atlas page.

device_url.description: Your own device-flow page: POST /oauth2/device_authorization returns it as verification_uri (and verification_uri_complete with ?user_code=). null: the Atlas page at /oauth2/device.

hosted.description: The Atlas page URLs on this instance.

object.description: The object type the path returns when configured.

channel.description: Messaging providers only: email, sms or push.

message.description: What to call to configure it.

configured.description: Always true on a configured object (the unconfigured reply is { configured: false }).

id.description: The provider id; pass it as provider_id to managed email or the development sender.

mode.description: How the provider sends.

secret_fingerprints.description: For each write-only secret config field that is set: the first 8 hex characters of sha256 of its value, to compare with the value you hold. Never the value.

method.description: cname: proven by a CNAME to Atlas. path: a path mount on your own host, proven by an https file.

base_path.description: method path: the prefix the Frontend API is served under.

routing.description: method path, once verified: atlas_ingress (the host is on Atlas's ingress, which routes the prefix) or customer_proxy (add the reverse-proxy rule in instructions).

frontend_api_url.description: method path: the Frontend API (and, once verified, the issuer) — https://<host><base_path>.

verification.description: method path: the https file that proves the host. Its whole body is the token; the token is bound to this instance, host and base path.

previous_url.description: After a rotation: the replaced token's URL, which still verifies until previous_valid_until.

previous_valid_until.description: After a rotation: when the replaced token stops working (ms since epoch).

last_observation.description: What the most recent failed verification fetch got back, so you can see what answered (a cache, a catch-all page) without guessing. Null until a check fails, and again after one passes.

status.description: The HTTP status.

bytes.description: Body bytes seen; headers are not counted.

bytes_capped.description: True when reading stopped at the 64 KiB read limit, so bytes is a lower bound.

body_prefix.description: The first 200 bytes of the body (printable characters only).

final_url.description: The URL that answered, including the per-check atlas_nonce query parameter. Redirects are not followed.

age.description: The Age response header, when present.

cache_status.description: The cf-cache-status or x-cache response header, when present.

served_from_cache.description: True when age is above 0 or a cache header says HIT: a cache answered, not your origin.

checked_at.description: When the fetch ran (ms since epoch).

instructions.description: method path, once verified: type atlas_ingress (nothing to add) or reverse_proxy (upstream, the headers to forward, and nginx / Caddy / Traefik snippets).

dns.description: DNS automation: the provider Atlas writes this host's record with. The API token is write-only and never returned.

name.description: Fully-qualified record name.

configured.description: Always true on a configured object (the unconfigured reply is { configured: false }).

provider_id.description: Your email provider, in development mode.

active.description: Whether mail goes out through it now. Always false on a production instance.

transport.description: Your email provider: resend, ses, smtp, brevo, mailgun, smtp2go or hermetica (`hermeticor` is accepted as an alias).

from_address.description: The sender: onboarding@resend.dev on Resend by default, or an address your provider has verified.

footer.description: The line added to the end of every message.

templates.description: The only emails it sends: Atlas's own sign-in templates.

note.description: Present for onboarding@resend.dev: Resend delivers it only to your Resend account address.

set.description: Whether a trusted reverse proxy secret is set.

created_at.description: When the current secret was created (ms since epoch).

previous_expires_at.description: After a rotation: when the replaced secret stops working. Null when none is still valid.

secret_header.description: The header your proxy sends the secret in.

client_ip_header.description: The header your proxy sends the browser's IP in.

secret.description: The secret (aps_…). Shown only in this response.

rotated.description: true when an existing secret was replaced.

configured.description: Always true on a configured object (the unconfigured reply is { configured: false }).

backend.description: The email service the domain is set up on: your own account there.

provider_id.description: Your email provider (mode managed_domain) that holds the API key.

feedback_webhook.description: Whether the bounce / complaint webhook is registered on your Resend or Brevo account (create and verify register it). not_registered leaves sending unaffected; the counters in usage then stay 0, and feedback_webhook_error says why.

feedback_webhook_id.description: The webhook's id on your Resend or Brevo account.

feedback_webhook_error.description: Why the last registration failed; null once it is registered.

status.description: not_started | pending | verified | failed | temporary_failure. Email sends only when verified.

limits.description: Always null: no Atlas sending limits apply; the account and its limits are yours.

reputation.description: Mail goes out through your own provider account.

anyOf.description: DNS automation. The records are written and the domain verified in the background; poll this object.

status.description: pending: the records are not written yet. verifying: written; Atlas checks with your provider on a growing interval. verified: done. failed: Atlas stopped (see last_error); fix it and POST again, or POST …/verify.

last_error.description: The last DNS write or provider check error (code: message); null once a step succeeds.

next_check_at.description: Epoch ms of the next background step; null when nothing is due.

RadiusClient.description: reply_attributes inner keys are camelCase (stored value returned unchanged).

ManagedWaf.description: Unconfigured form omits all but the first four keys.

return_url.description: Where "Finish" on the hosted setup page sends the admin.
This ticket's return_url (null = the profile's applies).

http_target.description: An `http` Action's endpoint; null for a `node` Action. Its signing secret is write-only (a generated one is returned once, as `signing_secret` on the create response).

failure_mode.description: What a failed call does: `closed` refuses a gate, `open` carries on.

signing_secret.description: An `http` Action only, on the create (or rotate) response: the signing secret Atlas generated. Shown once, never returned again.

egress_allowlist.description: Hosts the action's `api.http` calls may reach (`api.example.com`, `*.example.com`). Empty = any public host.

rollout.description: A staged version running for a share of executions: its `version` and `percent`. null = none.

scope.description: Who the template is for: `{ type: instance | client | org, id }` (id null for the instance).

locale.description: The language it is for; null = every language.

live.description: The template the hosted page renders: `{ version, updated_at, definition }`.

draft.description: The unpublished template, visible only behind a preview link.

trigger.description: What starts a run: `cron`, `user_created`, `inactive`, `membership_age`, `trial_end`, `webhook_event` (optionally with a `filter` expression) or `manual`, with that trigger's fields.

steps.description: The step tree (1 to 50 top-level steps, 200 in all, branches nested up to 5 deep): `if`, `switch`, `for_each`, `wait`, `set_variable`, `http_request`, `call_connector`, `create_ticket`, `create_iga_request`, `start_campaign`, `revoke_grant`, `approval`, `kv`, `notify`, `disable`, `delete`, `invite`, `add_to_org`, `remove_from_org`, `add_to_team`, `remove_from_team`, `add_to_group`, `remove_from_group`, `call_action`.

next_run_at.description: A cron workflow's next slot, Unix ms; null for any other trigger.

subject.description: What the run was for: `user:<id>`, `event:<id>`, `cron:<slot>`, `membership:<id>`, `trial:<id>:<end>`, `inactive:<id>:<last>` or `manual:<ms>:<user>`.

cancelled_at.description: When the run was cancelled, Unix ms.

cancelled_by.description: Who cancelled it (an API key id or dashboard user id).

retry_count.description: How many times the run was retried from a step.

resume_at.description: While `waiting` on a timer or retry back-off: when the run continues, Unix ms.

path.description: Position in the step tree, e.g. `2.then.0`.

output.description: What the step produced (truncated when large).

test.description: A dry-run test call, kept out of the stats.

answer.description: What the endpoint answered with, reduced to the names it set (never claim values).

stats.description: Real (non-test) calls in the last 24 hours.

challenge.description: custom_challenge_create: what api.challenge.set asked ({ prompt, hint, state }).

challenge_accepted.description: custom_challenge_verify: set ({ amr }) when the code called api.challenge.accept().

lock_reason.description: Set when the code called api.access.lock(). A real run locks the account for 15 minutes and answers 429 LOCKED.

pause_reason.description: Set when the code called api.access.pause() (pre_user_deletion). A real run holds the deletion until the person re-confirms it.

suppressed_access_claims.description: pre_token: claims the code asked to remove from the access token.

suppressed_id_claims.description: pre_token: claims the code asked to remove from the ID token.

user_edits.description: Edits the code asked for with api.user.setBanned / setEmailVerified / setName / setImage. A dry run applies none of them.

sign_up_prefill.description: Registration triggers: api.signUp.prefill values (fill a field the person left empty).

sign_up_modify.description: Registration triggers: api.signUp.modify values (replace what the person typed).

http_call.description: An `http` Action only: how the endpoint call went. The test really calls the endpoint, flagged `test: true`.

http_requests.description: Outbound requests the code queued with api.http (a dry run sends nothing). Query values are masked and only header names are shown.

ActionTemplateSecret.description: A secret a template reads from event.secrets, by NAME only; values are never part of a template.

uses_http.description: The code sends outbound requests with api.http.

missing_secrets.description: Required secrets not supplied yet; set them before enabling the action.

updated.description: false when the action already runs the latest version.

ActionTemplate.description: A gallery template this instance publishes.

Job.description: An import/export job. `result` is present for exports, `results` for imports.

result.description: user_export only: the exported users (no password hashes or secrets).

warnings.description: About a row that succeeded: password_policy_not_applied, unverified_without_hold or account_claim_not_applied. Absent when there are none.
user_import only: the warnings on the job per code, with how many rows and the first 100 external_ids. Also present on an import too big to return `results`.

type.description: Atlas's own kind (picks the worker path). A closure is an `erasure`; see `canonical_type`.

canonical_type.description: The shared data-rights word for this request.

canonicalType.description: Alias of `canonical_type` in the executor protocol spelling.

source.description: What opened it: self-service, a secret key, the dashboard, an orchestrator through /v1/privacy, or a Sign in with Atlas account erasure.

case_id.description: The orchestrator's case id when it drives this request.

external_case.description: The case Atlas opened at the instance's data-rights orchestrator for this request.

product.description: The orchestrator provider id (a preset or your own).

deletion_effective_at.description: Erasures: epoch ms when the account is erased — the date every executor aligns on.

status.description: A deferred erasure is `scheduled` (held in its grace window with a `scheduled_for`/`eta`), distinguishing it from a `pending` request that runs on the next worker pass. The worker promotes it to `processing` once due, then `completed`. `cancelled` = aborted in the grace window; `rejected` = a DPO declined it.

scheduled_for.description: Erasure only: epoch ms when the grace/cancellation window lapses and the worker fulfils it. Null for an export. The window length is per-instance (`compliance.retention.erasureGraceDays`, default 7).

eta.description: Estimated completion (epoch ms). An erasure = the grace-window deadline; an export = null (runs async). Alias of scheduled_for.

due_at.description: When a response is owed (epoch ms): the request time plus compliance.retention.dsrDueDays, or the extended date. null on a closure.

overdue.description: The deadline has passed and the request is still open (a deletion inside its cancellation window is not late).

result.description: Export requests: the data-export bundle once fulfilled (only on single-request reads); otherwise null.

UserLink.description: A verification or reset proof minted for a user without sending it. A credential: handle it like a password.

url.description: Present when the instance delivers this proof as a link.

code.description: Present when the instance delivers this proof as a code (always, for email_verification).

attempt_id.description: password_reset only: the reset attempt the link and code belong to.

source.description: GET /v1/users/:id/groups only: how the user joined.

counted_at.description: Epoch ms of the last count.

url.description: custom only: where the user is sent.

action.description: For example user.updated, user.metadata_replaced, user.password_updated, user.banned, user.unbanned, user.locked, user.unlocked, user.directive_imposed, user.directive_lifted.

field.description: A profile field (first_name, username, ...), a metadata key (public_metadata.plan), password, banned, ban_reason or locked_until.

before.description: The value before the change (absent when redacted).

after.description: The value after the change (absent when redacted).

redacted.description: True for a password or a private_metadata value: only the field name is kept.

expires_at.description: When a timed ban or lock lifts by itself (Unix ms).

source.description: The acknowledging app/system.

atlas.description: Atlas's own data about the subject — the no-secret self-service export bundle.

app_contributions.description: One entry per app that acknowledged, with the blob it contributed.

payload.description: The app's contributed JSON blob, verbatim (any JSON value).

BotDeviceFeatures.description: Client device features reported by the browser SDK for bot detection. Every field is optional on input (an unknown or malformed value is dropped); on a stored signal each is the clamped value or null.

BotBehaviorFeatures.description: Client interaction (mouse/keyboard/timing) features reported by the browser SDK for bot detection. Every field is optional on input; on a stored signal each is the clamped value or null.

risk_signals.description: Per-signal risk-engine detail recorded with the attempt (empty when none was scored).

heuristic_reasons.description: Human-readable reasons the bot heuristic fired, e.g. "navigator.webdriver is set".

peak.description: The highest daily count in the window.

ready.description: Every check that applies to the assumed integration passes.

integration.description: The integration the checks assumed for this origin. redirect = hosted-redirect OIDC sign-in (the app never runs the embedded components), so the cors and session_cookie checks do not apply. embedded = the sign-in components run on the origin.

source.description: declared: allowed_origins names it ({ origin, integration }). embedded_traffic: an Atlas browser SDK called the Frontend API from the origin in the last 7 days. redirect_clients: every OAuth client redirecting to the origin uses the authorization-code flow, and no SDK traffic was seen. default: nothing says, so embedded.

reason.description: A plain sentence saying why.

applies.description: false when the check does not matter for the assumed integration (it then never makes ready false).

from.description: The old origin, scheme://host[:port] (e.g. https://old.example.com). Origins compare as scheme + host + port.

to.description: The new origin. https, or http only for localhost.

dry_run.description: true: report the diff and any problems, write nothing.

test_webhooks.description: On a real run: send each moved webhook endpoint a webhook.test now (up to 10 s each) and return the results as webhook_tests.

applied.description: True when this run wrote changes (never on a dry run, or when nothing was on `from`).

changes.description: Every field that moves (or moved), before → after. Empty when nothing references `from`, so a repeated run returns [].

field.description: The field, e.g. allowed_origins, redirect_uris, backchannel_logout_uri, homepage_url, url, branding.legal.privacyUrl.

before.description: The value now: a URL, a list of URLs, or null.

after.description: The value after the move: a URL, a list of URLs, or null.

problems.description: Rewritten values the field would refuse (e.g. a webhook moving to a loopback host). A real run with problems is a 422 and writes nothing.

app.description: Platform twin only: the app after the move.

moved_webhook_endpoints.description: Webhook endpoints whose url moves (or moved), each with the call that tests it.

url.description: The url after the move.

webhook_tests.description: With test_webhooks: true on a real run: the result of the test sent to each moved endpoint.

next.description: What to do after the move, when anything is left.

target.description: The object that changed (e.g. oauth_client / oac_…, webhook_endpoint / wh_…, custom_domain / dom_…, instance).

changes.description: Always present. The fields that changed, each with its value before and after. On a create `before` is null; on a delete `after` is null. A secret field reads "set", "cleared" or "rotated", never its value. On an older entry that recorded only field names, each change has `values_recorded: false` and null values. Empty on a no-op write.

values_recorded.description: False when only the field name was recorded (older entries).

before.description: The section value before the change (any JSON value; absent when newly set).

after.description: The section value after the change (any JSON value; absent when removed).

no_op.description: True when the write changed nothing (the recorded before and after are identical).

recorded.description: `diff`: before/after values were recorded. `fields`: only the changed field names (older entries). `none`: nothing was recorded.

fields.description: Deprecated: the same names as `changes[].section`.

DirectoryEntry.description: A connector catalog entry, emitted verbatim from core with camelCase keys.

PlatformApp.description: An app (instance) a platform owns. Never carries a secret except on create/rotate/claim.

frontend_api_host.description: The Frontend API host: the default per-app host, or the custom domain once it is active.

issuer.description: The `iss` your session tokens carry. Changes when a custom domain goes active, so read it from here rather than hard-coding it.

discovery_url.description: The OpenID discovery document whose `issuer` equals `issuer`.

jwks_uri.description: The JWKS holding this instance's signing keys.

allowed_origin_integrations.description: The declared integration per allowed origin. Write allowed_origins entries as { origin, integration } to set one.

archived.description: X8 housekeeping: hidden from the default listing. A pure visibility flag — the app still serves auth.

archived_at.description: Epoch ms the app was archived, or null if not archived.

allOf.description: The create/claim response — the app plus its reveal-once sk_ secret.

secret.description: Reveal-once per-instance secret key.

onboarding_secret.description: With `provisioning_key: true`: a full-scope setup key, shown once, that expires at `onboarding_secret_expires_at`.

runtime_secret.description: With `secret_key_profile: "web_app"`: the narrow key for the app's server, shown once.

secret_expires_at.description: With `secret_key_profile`: when `secret` stops working (epoch ms) unless renewed.

onboarding_secret_expires_at.description: When the setup key stops working (epoch ms), 24 hours after the create.

allOf.description: The POST /v1/platform/apps response (X7): the primary instance plus its reveal-once secret, and — unless create_development_sibling is false — a test-mode sibling instance in the opposite environment (development for a production app), sharing the primary's provider/auth config and carrying its OWN publishable key, jwks and reveal-once secret.

sibling_instance.description: The auto-created test-mode sibling in the environment opposite the primary (development for a production app — the default and common case). Has distinct publishable_key and secret from the primary (`sibling_instance.secret`, a sk_test / atlas_test_sk key, revealed like the primary's). Absent when create_development_sibling is false.

path.description: POST here once to get both secrets again.

expires_at.description: When that stops working (epoch ms), 10 minutes after the create.

initial_secret_reveal.description: The one extra look at this response's secrets (primary and sibling), for a caller that lost it.

secret_redacted.description: Present (true) on an Idempotency-Key replay: the secrets are null because they are never stored for replay.

code.description: Stable snake_case identifier. Every code is listed by GET /v1/instance/preflight/codes.

message.description: What is wrong, in a plain sentence.

fix.description: What to do about it, in a plain sentence.

fix_call.description: Only where one exact Backend API call is the whole remedy: that call, ready to send. It is one of the remedies fix describes, so read fix first.

autofix_body.description: With fix_call: the complete body of that call, ready to send as it is.

safe_to_autofix.description: With fix_call: true only when the call cannot lock anyone out or change sign-in for existing users.

subject.description: Ids of what the finding is about (provider, id/client_id, origin, domain_id/host, site_id, …).

group.description: Set on the security posture findings (weaker than the defaults new instances get).

suppressed.description: Only with include_suppressed=true: the finding does not apply to how the instance integrates.

suppressed_reason.description: Only with include_suppressed=true: why it does not apply.

acknowledged.description: Present when the code is acknowledged (PUT /v1/instance/preflight/acks/{code}): a known, accepted warning or info finding that no longer counts. Never on an error.

by.description: The API key or dashboard user that acknowledged it.

InstanceConnection.description: One cross-platform link and its health, in the shared integration-health row shape.

check.description: What was checked: privacy_webhook_delivery, cmp_enabled, cmp_site, atlas_id_app_config or jwt_template_audience.

severity.description: How much a failing row matters (info rows never make the response not ok).

subject.description: Ids of what the row is about.

fix_hint.description: What to do when ok is false.

last_checked_at.description: When this row was observed (epoch ms).

details.description: Kind-specific facts. privacy_webhook: url, events, active, failing_since, last_verified_delivery {id, status, http_status, at} (the last delivery the endpoint accepted with a 2xx), last_delivery. cmp: enabled, site_checked, status (ok | unknown | domain_mismatch | unavailable), code, message, site_domain, other_site_id. atlas_id_app: name, managed_by_instance, redirect_uris, homepage_url, backchannel_logout_uri. jwt_template: algorithm, audience_host.

from_address.description: The From address, e.g. "Acme <no-reply@acme.com>". Must be a sender your provider accepts.

mode.description: How the provider sends. standard (default for a new provider): as configured. development: a development instance sends without a verified domain (Atlas sign-in templates only, "[Atlas test] " subjects, small limits); refused with 409 on a production instance. Omitted on an update: the stored mode is kept for the same transport. managed_domain is set only by managed email.
